evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-agent-team-presets English | [中文](README.zh.md) > **Status: community plugin v0.1.3**, published to npm as > [`dsh-agent-team-presets`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-agent-team-presets). > Install it with `dsh plugin --profile add dsh-agent-team-presets`, or > from GitHub unpinned with `... add github:bloodarea/dsh-agent-team-presets` — > those are the two forms the plugin market can offer updates for; to reproduce one > exact release, pin the ref with `#v0.1.3` instead, and note that a pinned install > is compared only against that same ref, so the market never offers an update for > it, by design. > The supported Harness peer range is `>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0`, checked by the plugin > manager; the Harness version is not this plugin's version. Plugin details for > `dsh-agent-team-presets` should show `v0.1.3`. A card naming > `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-presets` instead is the monorepo > development package, whose version follows the Harness (for example, > `0.2.0-rc.2`), not this community release. `lib/` ships prebuilt; rebuilding > source needs a Harness checkout — see [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md) and > [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## Summary `dsh-agent-team-presets` adds a Settings page that configures named Agent Teams and a composer control that applies one Team to a Session. A Team has a captain and any number of members: the captain carries its own prompt and tool policy, while each member also carries its own provider/model route and reasoning effort, read from the stored Team each time that member is summoned. Applying a Team installs the captain's prompt, restricts its tools, and registers `spawn_team_member`, which summons a member with that member's own persona, route, effort, and tools. A captain leads on the model the Session already selected. ## Project introduction > Turn DeepSeek Harness Agent Teams from ad-hoc lineups into configurable, reusable professional AI teams. **dsh-agent-team-presets** is a visual Agent Team preset manager for DeepSeek Harness. It configures roles, per-member models, reasoning effort, system prompts, and tool permissions, so a professional AI team is configured once and reused on demand. ## Why this plugin? DeepSeek Harness already ships Agent Teams with multi-agent collaboration, but it leaves room in per-team configuration and reuse. This plugin addresses five gaps: - **Teams are hard to reuse.** Native teams focus on runtime creation and collaboration and offer no visual preset management; this plugin saves, duplicates, and reuses team configurations. - **Role setup is repetitive.** Member responsibilities no longer have to be re-described every time: each role's name, description, and system prompt are configured in advance. - **Splitting work across models is awkward.** Every member picks its own model and reasoning effort, so one team combines models by task; the captain keeps leading on the model the session already selected. - **Tool permissions have no fine-grained entry point.** The captain and each member carry their own global tool allow-list, so roles differ in what they may use. - **Switching teams is inconvenient.** Pick a preset team from the composer, with no repeated manual role setup. **Design principle:** native Agent Teams owns collaboration at runtime; dsh-agent-team-presets owns configuring, managing, and reusing teams. ## Screenshots **The Team control in the composer** — apply one preset Team to this Session, or clear it. ![The Team control in the composer](docs/images/01-composer-team-control.png) **Settings → Agent team presets** — every configured Team, with create, duplicate, and delete. ![The Team list in Settings](docs/images/02-team-list.png) **One Team** — its name and description, the captain, and the member roster. ![One Team's editor](docs/images/03-team-editor.png) **One member** — its own provider, model, and reasoning effort. The captain leads on the Session model, so only a member carries a route. ![One member's route pickers](docs/images/04-member-route.png) **The model picker** — every provider and model the deployment currently advertises. ![The model picker](docs/images/05-model-picker.png) **The captain's system prompt** — it becomes the Session prompt; complete `{{variable}}` groups interpolate against registered variables, and an unknown variable fails the request instead of degrading. ![The captain's system prompt](docs/images/06-captain-system-prompt.png) **A member's system prompt** — a summoned member reads it after its Team briefing. ![A member's system prompt](docs/images/07-member-system-prompt.png) **Tool permission: all tools (default)** — adds no restriction; switching modes keeps the saved custom checks. ![Tool permission with all tools](docs/images/08-tools-default.png) **Tool permission: custom allowed tools** — the catalog lists built-in file tools, Team coordination tools, and plugin tools together; an unselected tool is denied at execution time, not merely discouraged in the prompt. ![Tool permission with custom allowed tools](docs/images/09-tools-custom.png) ## Table of Contents - [Project introduction](#project-introduction) - [Why this plugin?](#why-this-plugin) - [Screenshots](#screenshots) - [Use this package](#use-this-package) - [Understand the implementation](#understand-the-implementation) - [Further Exploration](#further-exploration) - [Model Experience](#model-experience) - [Known Limitations and Deferred Work](#known-limitations-and-deferred-work) - [Dev Note](#dev-note) ----- ## Use this package Install the bundle into a profile that already composes `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile` (the Team service, the Team tools, and the Web roster), then open Settings → Agent team presets. ### Install, upgrade, and verify the version From npm — the form with the cleanest update semantics, because the market compares the registry's `latest` tag against the installed version: ```sh dsh plugin --profile add dsh-agent-team-presets ``` From GitHub, unpinned — updates then follow this repository's own `package.json` version: the market compares that version against the installed one, so a release is advertised when the version moves, and a commit that does not bump it is not offered: ```sh dsh plugin --profile add github:bloodarea/dsh-agent-team-presets ``` To reproduce one exact release, pin the ref instead — and note that a pinned install is compared only against that same ref, so the market never offers an update for it, by design: ```sh dsh plugin --profile add github:bloodarea/dsh-agent-team-presets#v0.1.3 ``` Replace `` with the profile the GUI actually runs (for example, `web`). To move a profile from the development link to this release by hand, back up the profile and its Team configuration, remove the installed package, then install this one into the same profile. If the old package is the development link, remove `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-presets`, not `dsh-agent-team-presets`. Do not enable both packages: they own the same `agent-team-presets` settings and client registrations. When migrating a development profile, keep the Team configuration and selections under that entry id, but replace its module name and the selected bundle with `dsh-agent-team-presets`. After switching package identities, restart the running Harness and refresh the GUI; a page refresh alone can leave the old client entry in the Host's module table and produce duplicate-plugin boot failures. Verify the plugin details show both `dsh-agent-team-presets` and `v0.1.3`, with its component running. The Harness's own `0.2.0-rc.*` version is a separate compatibility requirement. ### Desktop and agent-assisted installation **Startup fix for the unreleased 0.1.4 (this fix is untested):** the prebuilt Host Typert and Remote entrypoints now inline their `zod` schema code so a local source link without `node_modules/zod` does not fail its startup import. Strict validation remains enabled; this does not replace the Harness peer compatibility requirements. The old `v0.1.3` tag and already installed copies do not receive this fix automatically. - When the user supplies this repository's GitHub URL, use the `github:` install form above. “I developed it myself” is not authorization to substitute a `file:` / `link:` source checkout or hand-edit the profile. Use a development link only when explicitly requested. - Install into the profile the Desktop actually runs (`desktop`, not the default `web`). The in-app plugin manager targets it; recommend a restart only after a successful installation with no failed operation status. - On a nonzero installation exit, manager failure, or compatibility rejection, stop and report the logs. Do not declare success, hand-append dependencies or patches, or ask the user to keep restarting. Back up configuration before recovery and preserve Team definitions and Session selections. - On Windows, do not rewrite profile JSON with a UTF-8 BOM. This plugin does not rewrite profile manifest encoding, Host locks, or other plugins' dependencies. - BOM parse errors, credential-lock timeouts, and other plugins' installation failures are independent Harness/install-flow issues, outside this fix. Do not disable Typert validation or blindly delete locks while the Host is running. ### Configure a Team **Unreleased 0.1.4 preparation:** custom policies cover inherited and exact-Agent tools, including coordination; the catalog includes standing-preset builtins. Custom mode denies general Node `run_code` and ordinary delegation without a strict durable policy contract. Tool-name policies are not OS/path isolation. Invalid initial applications and busy remounts without their frozen snapshot are quarantined; failed updates retain the old policy. Shared prompt edits require exact Host approval, not merely a human-started turn. These are working-tree changes, not a deployment to the current GUI. See the [remediation report](docs/evidence/0.1.4-remediation.md). **Boundary fixes (same unreleased branch):** every member is now created through this plugin's own subagent execution-backend alias, which the Host writes into its roster and the child's descriptor as a durable identity independent of the snapshot. A marked child whose snapshot is unreadable, whose durable unit cannot be opened, or whose Team identity cannot be resolved is refused inside the creation transaction instead of resuming on the Team Lead's route. A new member is validated against the host's delegation depth cap and its fixed model route first, and a refused creation leaves no intent, no roster row, and no model request. Strict custom policies are applied with native tool calling: when the Session's own Agent scope already declares PTC/both the Team is not applied at all (the previous policy stays and the reason is logged), and when it covered a preset-level PTC presentation the Settings page says so. The Team briefing stays visible under the official `minimal` preset. With the plugin absent entirely, later cold resumes are outside its control. The boundary-fix and real-instance report (`docs/evidence/0.1.4-verify/REPORT.md`) is local working evidence: `docs/evidence/` is not committed. Settings → Agent team presets is three stacked pages, so a narrow Settings panel never crowds: 1. **Teams** — every configured Team as one row (name, member count, session model). Create, duplicate, or delete from here. 2. **One Team** — its name and description, the captain row, and the member roster. Adding a member opens that member's page. 3. **One agent** (captain or member) — identity, tools, and system prompt, each in its own card; a member page adds the model card and deletes that member. Every edit is staged and written by the **Save** control in the shared footer; the stored value lives in the profile's user settings document. Settings accepts saves during a Team task without interrupting it. A Session is busy while its captain is `running` or any teammate is `running` or `provisioning`; its captain persona, briefing, member preset prompts and role descriptions, member tool description and roster, and tool permissions keep the applied definition, and members summoned during that task use that definition. A member's **model route** and each slot's **color** are deliberately outside the frozen definition, because both are read from the stored Team when they are needed: saving a corrected provider, model, or reasoning effort reaches the next member the running task summons without restarting it, and a color change redraws right away. Once the Session is fully idle, it adopts the latest saved definition before its next Team task; successive saves converge to the latest value. Sessions sharing a preset adopt it independently. The footer reports the selected Team's execution state across online Sessions: - **`idle`** — no Session is executing that Team's task; a save takes effect immediately. - **`busy`** — at least one Session is executing; idle Sessions adopt a definition change immediately, while busy Sessions adopt it before their next task. A member's route saved meanwhile applies to the next member summoned, in a task already running as well. A teammate finishing does not release the definition while the captain is still running. - **`unknown`** — execution cannot be confirmed, including before the stream is ready, after it ends or fails, during a connection loss, or when the Host lacks the method or a Team's state. The page does not treat a previous idle frame as current fact. A definition change still cannot affect a task already in progress, while a member's route saved meanwhile applies to the next member summoned. | Field | Meaning | |---|---| | Team name | Display name shown in Settings and in the composer control. | | Captain | The agent that leads the Session: its system prompt becomes the Session prompt and its tool scope scopes the session tools. It leads on the model the Session already selected, so it has no route of its own. | | Members | Role templates the captain summons by name. | | Name | Display name; the teammate target is derived from it (lower-kebab-case, falling back to `member-`). | | Color | Accent mark shown in Settings. | | Description | The role hint the models act on: the captain reads its own description, the Team description, and every member's description, so it can pick the member whose description fits the work; a summoned member reads the Team description and its own description as its role. | | Provider / Model | **Members only.** Route chosen from every provider and model the deployment currently advertises. Empty runs the member on the Session route. | | Reasoning effort | **Members only.** Adapter-owned effort for the selected route; empty uses the model default. | | Allowed tools | Choose **Default: all tools** or **Custom allowed tools** separately for the captain and each member. Custom mode displays the deployment's global and inherited preset tools as an expanded checkbox grid, with select-all and clear controls. Each checkbox's hover text states what the tool actually is: a registry tool keeps its author's English description, this plugin's own three tools share one English text (the tool definition and the hover tip use the same constant), and a name neither source describes is not listed rather than given invented hover text. **Tool descriptions stay English**, because the upstream `ToolDefinition` carries a single description with no localization field and that text is model-facing first; the surrounding UI copy still follows the language setting. Tools are grouped by source: **this plugin**, each **MCP server** (grouped by the Harness-generated `mcp____` form), and **other**. Groups start collapsed and show `chosen/total`; clicking a header expands or collapses it. Each group carries its own **select all**, **invert**, and **clear**, which rewrite only that group and leave every other group's selection alone. The registry records no registering package, so a native tool and a third-party plugin's tool cannot be told apart and are reported honestly under "other" rather than attributed by name; if upstream records the source at registration, that group splits by itself with no rework. Captain-only capabilities (`spawn_team_member`, `get_team_preset`, `update_team_preset`, `interrupt_agent`) are greyed out on a member page with the reason, because the Team service refuses a member call; select-all never persists them into a member allow-list, and an already-stored name stays removable. No checks in custom mode denies all configurable tools; default mode adds no restriction and preserves the saved checks. Captain and member policies apply independently, so a member can have tools the captain cannot use. Unavailable saved names remain removable; invalid names reject application instead of granting unrestricted access. Scoped coordination tools must also be selected; general code and ordinary delegation are denied in custom mode. | | System prompt | Registered as a prompt section template; complete `{{variable}}` groups interpolate against registered prompt variables. A summoned member reads it after its Team briefing. | ### Select a Team The composer's team control sits in the tool row after the permission control. Picking a Team writes this Session's selection; an idle Session applies its captain prompt and tool scope immediately, while a busy Session keeps its current application until it is fully idle. Picking "No team" removes the Team application at the same boundary, restoring the Session's other prompt and tool contributions. The model stays the one the composer already shows, because no Team writes a model selection. ### Share one Team **Export** on a Team row writes that Team as one fixed JSON document, and **Import preset** reads such a document. A shared document carries only what keeps working across deployments: the Team's name and purpose, and the name, description, system prompt, and color of its captain and each member. Model routes and tool permissions stay local, because they name this deployment's providers and tools; a document that carries them is refused instead of being silently trimmed. An import matches by name. When the document's Team name is already configured, the dialog asks whether to **replace that team** or **add it under a new name**. When the captain name or a member name is already used by the Team being replaced, the same dialog asks, per name, whether to **replace that agent** or **add the imported one renamed**. A replacement writes only the fields the document carries, so the target Team keeps its model routes and tool permissions and keeps every member the document does not mention. An import lands in the draft first, so it reaches the settings document only when you press **Save**; an export writes what the page currently shows, including an unsaved draft. ### Let the captain adjust a Team preset Every Session root holds two preset-editing tools, whether or not it has selected a Team. They are the discovery path, not a Team capability: a user may ask the captain to adjust "the Team preset" before any Team is selected, and the captain must be able to read the configured Teams and ask which one. Selecting a Team adds the Team capability and the member tool; it does not add these. A deleted/invalid selected Team is **not** No team. The composer displays the missing Team ID rather than implying no selection; tool errors explain how to choose a valid Team or **No team**. Cancellation removes the plugin policy and the member tool once the captain and its teammates are idle, and leaves the two discovery tools in place. Already-created managed members retain their stored creation-time policy, even after the root deselects. - **`get_team_preset`** reads every editable field of this Session's Team (or of the Team a `team_id` names) with the current settings revision. When the Session selected no Team it reports `no-selection` and lists the configured Teams, so the captain asks the user which one to change instead of guessing. - **`update_team_preset`** replaces `team_description`, `captain_description`, `captain_system_prompt`, and per-member `description` / `system_prompt`, fenced by the revision `get_team_preset` returned. A successful tool write saves to the same settings document as the Settings page and follows the same per-Session adoption timing described above. A captain still running its current task keeps the old definition through its subsequent model steps. **An existing teammate keeps its creation-time description, persona, and tool filter**, including when resumed by a message; the updated preset supplies future new members after that Session adopts it. Send an existing teammate a new requirement to adjust its work without replacing its stored composition. Both tools register in the Session-root Agent scope only, so a teammate never sees them, and the write additionally requires a user-started turn plus exact Host approval of the target, revision, and diff. Disabled, rejected, or unavailable approval writes nothing. Ordinary development input is not shared-prompt authorization; automatic continuations and teammate reports cannot rewrite the preset. Names, member routes, and tool permissions are outside their reach — renaming changes a teammate target and collides with Agent Teams' permanent-name rule, so the Settings page owns it. The tool's write policy differs from the Settings page: if any online Session that selected or still has that Team applied has a teammate `running` or `provisioning`, `update_team_preset` returns `team-busy` without saving. This conservative model-initiated write check counts teammates only, not the captain executing the tool; counting that captain would block every call. Wait for those teammates to finish, or interrupt them with `interrupt_agent`, then call `get_team_preset` again and retry with its revision. The running task keeps its original definition; the Settings page can still save changes for later adoption, and a member route saved there applies to the next member that task summons. `get_team_preset` reports the executing teammate count. The tool also refuses a revision another writer advanced (re-read, retry) and a supplied standing prompt whose `{{variable}}` group cannot resolve. An unknown variable fails the request when the template is used rather than degrading it. Only prompts supplied by the call are checked, so an unrelated edit still succeeds on top of text the Settings page wrote. ## Understand the implementation ### Host composition The Host half owns the live configuration and the per-Session applications: | File | Role | |---|---| | [`src/index.ts`](src/index.ts) | Plugin entry: live Config, per-Session definition freezing and adoption on Agent lifecycle, settings commits, and `team/member` settlements. | | [`src/member-runtime.ts`](src/member-runtime.ts) | Member runtime coordination: pre-spawn intent registration, serial `agent/created` scoped injection (route, persona, tools, team division), and cold-resume re-scoping. | | [`src/member-store.ts`](src/member-store.ts) | Durable member snapshot store backed by `ctx.storage.domain` for fail-closed member configuration recovery across residencies and restarts. | | [`src/execution.ts`](src/execution.ts) | Event-driven execution monitor: captain and teammate status, applied-versus-stored definitions, and aggregate whole-set frames. | | [`src/config.ts`](src/config.ts) | Volatile `teams` and `selections` fields, the continuable-provider names, and the captain-route cleanup of stored Teams. | | [`src/application.ts`](src/application.ts) | Applies one Team to one live Agent: prompt sections, tool scope, and the `spawn_team_member` tool. | | [`src/preset-editor.ts`](src/preset-editor.ts) | Pure preset edits behind the preset tools: the editable-field whitelist, member resolution, and the roster's description limit. | | [`src/preset-tools.ts`](src/preset-tools.ts) | The captain's `get_team_preset` and `update_team_preset`, their authority checks, and the settings write. | | [`src/presets.ts`](src/presets.ts) | Pure helpers shared with the browser half: teammate targets, member lookup, selection rewriting, roster text. | | [`src/tool-catalog.ts`](src/tool-catalog.ts) | Host Remote service `teamPresetsToolCatalog`: restrictable global tools and the `teamPresets.execution` stream for the Settings page. | | [`src/client/*`](src/client) | Browser half: the Settings page, the composer control, and the shared form controller. | Applying a Team installs the captain's prompt as `deployment:persona-prefix` on the Agent's scope, so it shadows the deployment persona for that Session alone. The captain and each member resolve their own tool mode. A custom captain allow-list filters its global tools; a summoned member receives its own custom allow-list, independent of the captain's selection. A captain leads on the model the Session already selected, so this plugin writes no model selection at all: the composer's model control stays the only owner of that reference, and the rendered captain prompt is recorded as a `system/message` surface event before the request, so the model-visible input stays reconstructable from the Session log. The Host half also provides the `teamPresetsToolCatalog` Remote service, which lists exactly the global tools `ctx.tools.restrict()` validates against, so the Settings page cannot offer a name the summon path would refuse. `teamPresets.execution` is a Remote stream of full snapshots: `{ teams: [{ teamId, state, busySessions, executingMembers, pendingSessions }] }`. Counts cover online Sessions that selected or still have the preset applied; `pendingSessions` counts Sessions with no application or an application that differs from the stored selection or frozen definition, leaving out a member route or a color the Session reads live. Frames carry Team identities and aggregate counts, not personas, Session names, or Session content. Lifecycle and settings events refresh the stream without polling; an unreadable roster reports `unknown` unless known activity already establishes `busy`. ### Selecting and storing Teams and per-Session selections live in the plugin's volatile Config fields, which the settings service projects into the profile's user settings document and commits back into the running references with a `loader/volatile-update`. The browser half splits the two jobs: the Settings page edits the staged Teams through `ctx.configForms.get('agent-team-presets')`, whose revision-fenced write queue owns the draft and its save, while the composer's per-Session selection is written through `ctx.remote.settings.mutate` with the revision the shared describe mirror reports and folded back with `acceptView()`. A refused or failed selection is retried once — a refusal triggers a recovery read of the Host document, so the retry carries the revision the Host holds now — and is then reported on the control and on the Settings page with the Host's own refusal text. Each agent stores `toolMode` independently of `tools`. Records without `toolMode` retain their list-only behavior: an empty list means default-all and a nonempty list means custom. A stored captain that still carries `provider`, `model`, or `reasoningEffort` from a document written before captains stopped owning a route is rewritten once without them when the plugin loads. ### Per-teammate settings (official rc.2 plugin-only implementation) In official DeepSeek Harness `0.2.0-rc.2`, the Team service's public `spawnTeammate` API does not pass through custom `agentOptions`, `persona`, or `toolFilter`. This plugin manages member scoping without any host modifications or monkey-patching: 1. **Durable member snapshots (`src/member-store.ts`):** Before calling `ctx.agentTeams.spawnTeammate`, `spawn_team_member` atomically commits a frozen member configuration snapshot (route, reasoning effort, briefing persona, team division of labour, and strict tool policy) into the durable member store backed by `ctx.storage.domain` (the `agent_team_presets_members` unit, `single` layout). 2. **Official-only spawn request (`src/application.ts`):** `ctx.agentTeams.spawnTeammate` is invoked with official-only fields (`name`, `description`, `prompt`, `context`, `provider`, `signal`). 3. **Serial creation-edge installation (`src/member-runtime.ts`):** When the official `agent/created` serial event fires, the plugin resolves the child Agent via `ctx.agentTeams.tryMembership`, claims it against its durable snapshot, and installs scoped model selection (`installModelSelection`), persona prefix (`deployment:persona-prefix`), team context (`agent-team-presets:member-team`), and strict tool guard/restriction before the child's first request is admitted. 4. **Cold resume re-scoping:** When a finished member is awakened later (via `sendMessage`), `agent/created` re-runs and re-applies the exact frozen configuration from the durable store. 5. **Fail-closed security:** If `storageDomain` is unavailable, or if a stored record fails schema validation or version mismatch, member creation is refused rather than allowing the member to execute on the Session's route with unrestricted tools. 6. **Known limitation:** The official Team roster (and `list_agents`) displays the model as the Team Lead's model (`lead-model`) or cr

# dsh-model-rotator

> [简体中文](./README.zh.md) | **English**

Model auto-ranking and transparent failover for DeepSeek Harness.

When the current model hits a quota wall, an expired credential, a rate limit or
a transient network error, this plugin switches to the next-best configured
model **inside the same turn** — and the user sees an ordinary reply.

## What it does

1. **Discovers** every dialable `provider/model` on this machine
   (`ctx.llm.listProviders()` + each adapter's `listModels()`).
2. **Filters** out families that cannot answer a chat turn — embeddings,
   rerankers, ASR/TTS, OCR, image/video generation, content moderators and
   judges. Dialing one of those can only fail the turn and burn a cooldown slot
   that a real model could have used.
3. **Skips the image-reading mode.** dsh-vision-router wraps a chat route into a
   twin (`<provider>-vision`) whose only job is to add image reading to that same
   model. It is one model reachable twice, not a second one, so failing a text
   turn over into it would answer through the image pipeline — and the
   same-model preference below would rank the twin *first*. Those routes are
   therefore never candidates (a model id that merely *mentions* vision is still
   a chat model and stays). The model list can switch one back on when a wrapper
   name does not follow the convention.
4. **Ranks** the survivors by measured connectivity (Laplace-smoothed success
   rate), speed (median TTFT and throughput) and an active failure cooldown. A
   model that *is* the current one — or a close relative of it — on another
   provider carries a bonus, because the model you picked is usually the model
   you want, just from a working channel.
4. **Retries before it believes a failure.** A provider fails transiently: a
   rate-limit blip, a reset socket, an overloaded channel. One miss therefore
   does not count as a fault — the same model gets `retriesPerModel` more tries
   (2 by default, 0–5), `retryBackoffMs` apart (300 ms, then the double of it),
   before the failure is acted on. A retry is not a switch: it asks nothing and
   changes nothing.
5. **Fails over** at the `llm/stream` waterfall: attempt 1 is the untouched
   harness path; a failure that produced **no content at all** abandons that
   attempt, closes its upstream stream, and re-dispatches the next candidate as
   a fresh `ctx.llm.stream()` — the same model first while retries remain, then
   the ranking above.

Once any content chunk has been yielded the attempt is never retried — a second
attempt would duplicate visible text. That zero-content window is exactly the
retryable window.

A turn the caller cancelled (Stop, a deadline, a closed client) ends there: the
walk stops instead of burning attempts on a reply nobody will read.

### What counts as content

"Flow" is the switch that closes the retry window, so it means *the user has been
shown reply text* — and nothing weaker. A `reasoning-delta` is not content: the
harness folds reasoning away again when a retry happens, which is exactly what
makes retrying a reasoning-loop or reasoning-effort failure safe. Markup chunks
(`block-start`, or a `block-end` carrying a reasoning block) are not content
either. Counting those was a real defect: a live model looked dead because a
block-start closed the window and the very next error was taken as final.

### Automatic calls are not conversation turns

A compaction summary and a session title ride the same `llm/stream` seam but are
not a user turn. Their refusals are usually statements about *that lane* — a
proxy answering "bili owns compression here" — so asking a second provider to
carry the plumbing is the wrong reflex: it burns a real model on work nobody
reads, and it is the single loudest source of spurious switching. The plugin
therefore passes any call carrying `purpose: "compaction"` or
`purpose: "session-title"` straight through, error included. An unnamed call —
every ordinary turn — keeps failing over exactly as before.

## Announcing a switch

A switch is otherwise silent: the reply simply arrives from a different model. By
default the plugin posts one line in the conversation when that happens —
`模型已切换：A → B`, with the failure kind in brackets when it is known
(`(quota)`, `(rate-limit)`).

| Behaviour | |
|-----------|--|
| Shape | the host's own notice mechanism: a `user/message` whose source is `{ kind: 'model-rotator/switch', form: 'notice', summary }`. The conversation UI renders that form as a context row, not as something you typed |
| Timing | at the turn boundary, via `agent/turn-stopping` + `agent.steer`. The switch already happened and the answer is already streaming, so announcing it mid-turn would insert a row in the middle of the reply it describes |
| Scope | the root conversation only. A switch inside a subagent transcript is somebody else's log |
| Off | `noticeSwitch: false` (or the settings-page toggle) |

The event type is deliberately **not** a private one. The persistence reader
refuses to interpret a session log containing a type it does not know
(`dsh-session`'s `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES`), so an invented event would make a
log carrying it fail to load. `user/message` is known, and `notice` is a form the
client already understands — the same pair the harness uses for its own
"model changed" line.

The vendor half of the label is the provider's own `displayName` when the host
publishes one (硅基流动 for `siliconflow`), falling back to the route id. The id
stays visible in the model list, because that is what `config.json`'s lists use.

## Asking before switching

A failover replaces the model the user picked, and it can do so silently. The
default is therefore to ask first: when the current model fails with no content,
the plugin raises a question in the conversation through the harness's own
human-interaction seam (`ctx.userQuestions.askTimed()`), offering **切换** and
**保持当前模型**.

| Reply | Outcome |
|-------|---------|
| 切换 (or any answer that is not a refusal) | the next candidate serves the turn |
| 保持当前模型 (or a typed refusal — 不/否/取消/拒绝/no/cancel/stop/…) | nothing further is dialed; the turn ends on the original error |
| no answer inside the window | the switch proceeds — the request was time-boxed, not vetoed |

The question is raised **once per turn**: approving the first switch covers the
rest of that walk, so a cascade of dead models does not become a cascade of
identical cards. The wait is 20 s by default and configurable.

Failover is deliberately fail-open. If the seam is missing, the ask throws, the
turn has no live root agent (a delegated sub-agent has nobody to answer), or the
timeout is reached, the walk continues unconfirmed. An unattended harness must
not stall on a card nobody is watching.

## The failure kind decides the rest

A failure is not just a string: it is classified, and the class decides how long
the model sits out.

**A quota wall is not a rate limit.** `429 insufficient balance` and `429 too many
requests` are the same HTTP status, yet one clears in seconds and the other does
not until the allowance resets. The plugin reads the kind out of the message -
`insufficient quota`, `out of credits, please top up`, `余额不足，请充值`, `额度已用尽`,
`402 Payment Required` and similar - and treats a balance problem differently:

| Kind | Rest | Retry first? |
|------|------|--------------|
| `quota` | until the next day at `quotaCooldownHour` (00:00 local by default), and never less than `quotaCooldownMs` | no - the balance does not refill between two dispatches |
| `auth` | ordinary exponential backoff | yes - a 403 from a burst-rate proxy does recover |
| `unsupported` | ordinary exponential backoff | no - the same provider returns the same refusal to the same request |
| `rate-limit` | ordinary exponential backoff | yes |
| `server` / `network` | ordinary exponential backoff | yes |
| unclassified | ordinary exponential backoff | yes |

`unsupported` is the request-shape refusal — *"provider X model Y does not
support reasoning effort high"*, *"unsupported model"*. It is decided before the
request is read, so the retry dispatches would repeat it verbatim; skipping them
is what turns a session-level mismatch into one switch instead of three.

An authentication failure is classified *before* a bare `429`, because waiting
never repairs a key: for `429 invalid api key` the honest name is `auth`, not
`rate-limit`. The distinction is recorded, not acted on - both take the same
backoff; only `quota` changes the policy.

The rest is at least "the following day at `quotaCooldownHour`". A wall hit at
23:50 still pays the full `quotaCooldownMs` floor, so it returns at 11:50 the
next day rather than ten minutes later at midnight.

`model_rotator_status` shows it: the ranking marks such a row `QUOTA-REST` (with
the remaining hours) rather than `COOLDOWN`, the `type` column names the class,
and a `last failure seen` line lists each model's last error with its kind.

Measured state - counters, the last error and kind, the cooldown horizon -
**outlives the process**, because the restart a user performs right after being
told their balance is gone must not undo the rest. It is written to
`%DSH_HOME%\model-rotator\stats.json` (or `dirname(config.json)`), debounced, and
read back once on first use. Latency samples deliberately stay in memory: they
are a 20-sample sliding window, and a stale window is worse than a short one.
`statsPersistTtlMs` bounds the age of a restored file (24 h by default; 0
disables the file entirely).

## What it does NOT do

It never reads, writes or rewrites model/provider configuration. It does not
touch `cordis.patch.yml`, `agent-default-model`, `llm-pi-ai` or any provider
registration. It only observes the stream waterfall at runtime.

## Non-chat filtering

The harness adapter strips the catalog's own `wire: 'chat'` marker before
handing rows to `listModels()`, so capability cannot be read off the row.
Name matching is the available signal, and it is deliberately narrow — a
pattern must not touch a chat model that merely mentions a modality
(`Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct` is chat; `Z-Image-Turbo` is not).

The filter denies families across vectors/ranking, speech, image generation,
document parsing and safety classifiers — in both the plain and the `-vision`
provider variants. It runs during discovery, so the count the plugin reports
(`discovered`) is already the post-filter pool, and a machine's numbers depend
entirely on which providers are configured. Ask a live install rather than
quoting a figure from here:

```
model_rotator_status      # "discovered" = candidates after this filter
```

## Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `model_rotator_status` | Read-only: enabled state, config path, discovered pool, measured ranking. |
| `model_rotator_benchmark` | Probe candidates with a minimal live request to refresh TTFT/throughput and cooldowns (bounded, spends a little quota). |
| `model_rotator_select` | Pin/unpin the head of the failover order; the ranking still decides the tail. |

The status tool also reports the two manual lists and the vision rule, so a model
the user can see in the directory but not in the ranking can be explained without
reading the code:

```
  disabled models  : workbuddy/hy3
  vision twins     : never a candidate (the dsh-vision-router mode wraps a model, it is not a second one)
  model list route : /_dsh/model-rotator/models (GET the grouped list; POST {key, enabled} to switch one off or on)
```

## Configuration

Optional, at `%DSH_HOME%\model-rotator\config.json` (hot-reloaded on change).
Every field has a safe default, so the plugin works with no file at all.

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "allowImageFailover": false,
  "maxCandidates": 4,
  "cooldownBaseMs": 60000,
  "maxCooldownMs": 1800000,
  "quotaCooldownMs": 43200000,
  "quotaCooldownHour": 0,
  "statsPersistTtlMs": 86400000,
  "confirmSwitch": true,
  "confirmTimeoutMs": 20000,
  "adoptSwitchedModel": true,
  "retriesPerModel": 2,
  "retryBackoffMs": 300,
  "preferSameModel": true,
  "weights": { "connectivity": 0.5, "speed": 0.3 },
  "excludeProviders": [],
  "excludeModels": [],
  "excludePatterns": [],
  "disabledModels": [],
  "enabledModels": [],
  "pinned": ""
}
```

- `enabled` — master switch.
- `allowImageFailover` — image turns are skipped by default: a text-only
  fallback cannot read an image, so failing over there would produce a wrong
  answer rather than a missing one.
- `maxCandidates` — cap per turn (hard ceiling 8).
- `cooldownBaseMs` / `maxCooldownMs` — exponential backoff bounds
  (`base * 2^(n-1)`, clamped to `max`).
- `quotaCooldownMs` — minimum rest after a quota wall (default 12 h, ceiling
  26 h). Counted from the failure, not rounded to the hour.
- `quotaCooldownHour` — local hour (0–23) at which an exhausted model may be
  tried again (default 0 = next midnight). The rest always reaches that hour of
  the *following* day, so a wall hit at 00:05 does not revive the same evening.
- `statsPersistTtlMs` — how long measured state survives a restart (default
  24 h, ceiling 30 d; 0 = do not persist).
- `confirmSwitch` — ask in the conversation before leaving a failed model
  (default `true`; see above).
- `confirmTimeoutMs` — how long that question waits before switching anyway
  (default 20000; clamped to 1 s … 10 min).
- `adoptSwitchedModel` — after a switch, make the model that actually
  answered the model of *this session*, so the conversation header shows what is
  really in use (default `true`). Session-local only: no provider configuration
  and no saved default is touched, and the harness's own "model changed" notice
  then names the right pair.
- `retriesPerModel` — extra tries the same model gets before its failure is
  believed (default 2, hard ceiling 5). A retry needs no confirmation because it
  does not change the model.
- `retryBackoffMs` — pause before each retry (default 300; the nth retry waits
  n times this, capped at 10 s).
- `preferSameModel` — rank the same model on another provider first, then close
  relatives, then the measured ranking (default `true`).
- `noticeSwitch` — post the one-line switch notice in the conversation (default
  `true`; see "Announcing a switch" above).
- `weights` — connectivity vs speed in the score.
- `excludeProviders` / `excludeModels` — keep specific routes out of the pool.
- `excludePatterns` — extra regex sources appended to the non-chat deny list.
  An invalid pattern is skipped, never fatal.
- `disabledModels` — models switched off from the model list on the settings
  page. Each entry is `"provider/model"` or a bare model id (which matches every
  channel serving that model). A per-row entry outranks the channel rule.
- `disabledProviders` — whole channels switched off from a channel header's
  button. One entry per provider id. Closing a channel also clears the per-row
  `enabledModels` entries inside it, so the switch cannot be silently undone;
  enabling a row afterwards writes a new entry that does take effect.
- `enabledModels` — the opposite, and the only way to put a vision twin back into
  rotation when its wrapper name does not follow the `<provider>-vision`
  convention. Written by the same switch.
- `pinned` — preferred head of the failover order.

## Settings page

The plugin ships both halves of a real settings page: the server-side `Config`
schema the Harness serves for the `model-rotator` namespace, and a browser
bundle (`client.js`, declared through `dsh.client` plus `exports["./client"]`)
that renders the form in two host cells from one component:

- **Settings → Model failover**, its own entry in the Settings navigation
  (`settings.section`, id `model-rotator`, order 20). The Harness renders the
  plugin settings pages this way; the shell hands the cell `{ close }` and
  filters by the registration id.
- the **model-rotator** card in the Plugins panel (`plugins.item`), which
  renders the same form as its card body.

Both cells only appear while the host actually serves the namespace. Only the
fields that are safe to personalize appear there:

| Field | |
|-------|--|
| `enabled` | master switch |
| `allowImageFailover` | also fail over image turns |
| `maxCandidates` | models one turn may try |
| `cooldownBaseMs` | backoff base |
| `maxCooldownMs` | backoff cap |
| `quotaCooldownMs` | minimum rest after a quota wall |
| `quotaCooldownHour` | hour at which an exhausted model returns |
| `statsPersistTtlMs` | how long measurements survive a restart |
| `confirmSwitch` | ask before switching |
| `confirmTimeoutMs` | how long that question waits |
| `adoptSwitchedModel` | show the switched model on this session |
| `retriesPerModel` | tries before a failure is believed |
| `retryBackoffMs` | pause between those tries |
| `preferSameModel` | same model on another channel first |

`weights.connectivity` / `weights.speed` are **not** on the page: the form
model stages one top-level key at a time, so nested values stay in
`config.json`. Long lists meant for editing by hand or by tool —
`excludeProviders`, `excludeModels`, `excludePatterns`, `pinned` — stay
there too.

### The model list

Below the settings form the same page renders **模型列表 / Models**: every
discovered `provider/model`, with its health and a switch — plus a switch on each
channel header that closes **every model behind that provider in one click**. The
pair of levels is deliberate: a channel switch is the useful action when a key or
an endpoint dies (everything behind it is unreachable at once), while a row switch
is what you reach for when one model is bad and its neighbours are fine.

The list is split into two sections, because they answer different questions:

| Section | Contents |
|---------|----------|
| **对话渠道** (chat channels) | the routes failover actually ranks — the candidates |
| **识图模式** (vision mode) | the `<provider>-vision` twins, each labelled with the channel it wraps (`amd-vision → amd`) |

**Three fold levels, all independent**: each section, each provider channel inside
it, and the roster as a whole. Chat channels start open and the vision section
starts **closed**: there are as many twins as everything else on this machine
(453 of 906 rows in the last live scan), and none of them is ever a candidate, so
leaving them folded is what makes the page readable at all. Two buttons —
**全部展开 / 全部收起** — open or close every section and channel at once.

Closing a channel writes a single `disabledProviders` entry rather than one entry
per model — the channel is the unit you are thinking in, and a list of a hundred
ids would be unreadable and impossible to undo honestly. Four rules keep the two
levels from fighting:

- the header button is labelled from the channel's own flag, not from whether its
  rows happen to be in rotation — a channel whose rows are all off for per-row
  reasons is still **open**, and one closed from the header must offer the action
  that reopens it;
- a closed channel offers **启用本渠道**, and the row switches underneath stay
  available for putting one model back without reopening the whole channel;
- closing a channel clears the stale per-row overrides inside it (so the button
  does what it says), and a row you switch on **afterwards** wins (a fresh,
  deliberate statement beats an older blanket one);
- a **vision** channel carries no channel switch at all. Its rows are kept out by
  the twin rule, which the channel flag cannot lift, so a button there would write
  an entry that changes nothing while reading like a promise. Use a row switch.

The channel label is the vendor name the host publishes on the registered route
(`硅基流动` for `siliconflow`), falling back to the route id when a route
publishes no label; the id is kept in parentheses when the two differ.

A folded line never hides what matters: every channel header (and every section
header) prints the same tally — derived from the rows, not from a host-supplied
counter, so the two layers cannot disagree. A collapsed provider still says
whether it is healthy. The page also rebuilds the sections from `channels` when
the host does not send `groups`, because the two halves are versioned together
but not *loaded* together.

```
▼ 对话渠道                    453 个 · 可用 447 · 冷却 6 · 关闭 0
    ▼ 硅基流动 (siliconflow)     65 个 · 可用 63 · 冷却 2 · 关闭 0   [关闭本渠道]
        ● deepseek-v4.1-flash   冷却中   retry in 511m · rate-limit      [关闭]
    ▶ cline                    55 个 · 可用 55 · 冷却 0 · 关闭 0   [关闭本渠道]
▶ 识图模式（vision-router 创建）  453 个 · 可用 0 · 冷却 0 · 关闭 453
```

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| dot + label | `可用` (nothing resting, no failure on record), `未测` (never tried), `冷却中`, `额度耗尽` (until the next-day boundary), `异常` (last attempt failed), `已关闭` |
| detail | TTFT and success/attempt counts, or the remaining rest, or why the row is out of rotation |
| switch | 关闭 / 启用 |

The reasons a row can be out of rotation are named rather than collapsed:
`manual` (switched off here), `vision` (the vision-router twin, a default the
switch can overrule), `provider` / `excluded` (from `config.json`),
`non-chat` (a family that cannot answer a chat turn), `combo` (a virtual
route). Only the first two are switchable from the page — the rest are
structural or owned by the file.

The roster reads its data over HTTP rather than through the settings form. Its
route is `/_dsh/model-rotator/models`: `GET` returns the grouped list
(`groups` = the two sections, `channels` = one entry per provider carrying its
`kind` and the `sourceChannel` a twin wraps, `models` = every row; a section and a
channel carry the same `models`/`ok`/`resting`/`off` counters, so one row shape
renders both and a folded line still reports its state),
`POST {key, enabled, scope}` flips one switch and answers with the refreshed list
(`scope: "provider"` for a channel header, omitted or `"model"` for a row). The
form carries the user's *policy* (how many candidates, how long to wait), while
this is a *roster* that changes whenever a provider republishes — and its rows
save one at a time, straight to `config.json`, so a refresh cannot discard a
half-typed number above it. The route is registered through
`ctx.inject(['webServer'], …)` because the host publishes the web server
*after* plugins load; it is auth-gated by the host exactly like every other
non-public path.

The two layers merge as **defaults < config.json < settings page**, and the page
wins only for the keys it actually owns: a key the page never sets still comes
from the file. `model_rotator_select` never writes a page-owned key back into
`config.json`, so a stale file value can never masquerade as authoritative.

The namespace is the plugin's cordis id (`model-rotator`) — a server half
without a client half shows nothing, which is why both ship together. A host
that ships no generic settings form has to be given one: the page is the
plugin's own React form, so the fields above are exactly the ones this bundle
stages, not every key the `Config` schema accepts.

The `Config` export needs schemastery *inside the host process*. The plugin
ships its own copy under `vendor/node_modules/` and loads that copy by absolute
path when a bare import cannot be resolved from the plugin's real path, which is
what makes the page appear on installs where the manifest link resolves outside
the profile's `node_modules`.

`model_rotator_status` ends with an **in force right now** block that lists the
merged value of every effective key next to the layer it came from
(`[default]`, `[config.json]` or `[settings page]`), so what is actually
driving the plugin is visible without reading two files and doing the merge in
your head. Further lines report the live picture: `ask channel` (whether the
pre-switch question can actually reach you, and why not when it cannot),
`adopt on switch`, `model in use now` (read from this session's request
header), `session switch` (whether the plugin can record the swapped model on
the session), `failure verdict` and `switch order`.

## Install

```
dsh plugin --profile desktop add <path-to-this-directory>
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so its `cordis.patch.yml` wires the
plugin automatically. A full app restart is required for the host to load it.

## Test

```
node test-offline.mjs     # failover + consent gate, against a stub harness
node test-settings.mjs    # server-side settings contract, against the host rules
node test-client.mjs      # browser bundle: loader shape, card registration, fields
```

All three run with no network and no DSH process. `test-offline.mjs` (135
assertions) covers failure-then-retry, no-retry-once-text-flows, image-turn skip,
all-candidates-failed, cooldown accounting, aborted-signal passthrough,
non-chat filtering through a real waterfall, tool registration, and the consent
gate (prompt off, approved, declined by button and by typed text, timeout,
one-question-per-walk, and every fail-open path). Failure classification and the
quota rest are asserted through the exported `classifyFailureKind()` and
`quotaRestUntil()` seams — day boundaries, the pre-midnight floor, a month
rollover, "a quota wall never burns a retry", "an unsupported request is not
retried", and the on-disk round trip including TTL expiry and a malformed file.
The non-chat assertions call the exported `isNonChatModelId()` seam so they
test the shipped pattern table rather than a copy of it.

Two later scenarios pin the defects fixed after the first live run: **16** — a
`-vision` provider is never dialed, while a *model named* something-vision
stays a candidate, and switching a twin back on really does restore it; and
**17** — a reasoning-only attempt still gets its retries, text still closes the
walk, and an empty `block-start` counts as nothing. The list route is driven
end to end in **14** through an opt-in HTTP harness (GET, POST, the file write,
a bare model id, an empty key, a hand-edited file, and the whole channel switch
including its precedence rules). **16** additionally
asserts the two page sections — the twins counted apart from the chat channels,
each naming the channel it wraps — and **15** that a `purpose: "compaction"` call
is passed through untouched while an ordinary turn still fails over.

Two more offline cases cover the record itself: a stored `lastErrorKind` is
re-derived from its prose when the file is loaded, so a pattern added in a later
build relabels the history it was written for (a stored quota wall keeps resting
until tomorrow instead of being retried the moment it is read back); and a failure
payload that arrives as an object is serialised rather than stringified into
`[object Object]` — unreadable, and unclassifiable, which would cost a real quota
wall its daily rest.

**18** covers the switch notice: the message shape the session accepts (a
`user/message` with form `notice`, a fresh id, a summary inside the host's
120-character bound), the vendor-name bug above, the turn-boundary delivery
through `agent.steer`, one notice per switch rather than per boundary, no notice
in a subagent transcript, none on an aborted turn, and the off switch.

Persistence makes the suite order-sensitive by nature: a cooldown that survives
the process would let scenario 5's dead keys decide scenario 9's candidate
order. Every harness therefore mounts onto a stats file of its own, and the two
that mean to assert across applies opt into sharing one explicitly.

`test-settings.mjs` (34 assertions) asserts the host's own rules, not this
plugin's opinion of them: it copies the shipped `volatileForm()` walk and
checks that the exported `Config` yields exactly the intended page fields
(a non-volatile sibling is dropped), and that the page outranks `config.json`
for the keys it owns while the file still fills the rest. It loads the host's
real `schemastery` and `cosmokit`, so `createVolatile()` handles behave
exactly as they do in the app.

`test-client.mjs` (44 assertions) runs `client.js` against a stub module
loader: the `window.__ModuleLoader__.load()` shape, the exported `apply` /
`inject`, the two cells (`settings.section` and `plugins.item`) registered for
the `model-rotator` namespace, and — the anti-drift check — that the fields the card renders and
stages are exactly the volatile fields the schema walk above yields. A field the
bundle forgets to stage is a setting nobody can edit; one it invents throws
`plugin card has no field <name>` inside the real form.

Its last block goes further than source matching: it renders the roster with a real
hooks runtime (state, effects, memoized callbacks, re-renders) against a payload
shaped like the host's, presses the buttons a reader would press, and asserts what
comes back — both sections, the derived tally, the folded and expanded states of
each fold level, and that the list is fetched exactly once. A regex can prove a
feature is mentioned; only a render proves it works, and this is what caught a
re-fetch loop the source checks could not see.

## License

MIT

# dsh-notify-me

简体中文 | [English](README.en.md)

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-notify-me?style=flat-square&label=npm&color=cb3837)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-notify-me)
[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-notify-me?style=flat-square&label=downloads%2Fmonth&color=1F883D)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-notify-me)
[![npm total downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/dsh-notify-me?style=flat-square&label=total%20downloads&color=1F883D)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-notify-me)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)
![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-browser-blue)
![Size](https://img.shields.io/badge/bundle-%7E137KB-green)
[![Awesome DSH Plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg)](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com)

---

**离开 DSH 页面也不错过任何动静。** 当模型停下来需要你操作（审批 / 方案待确认 / 提问）、或你在别的软件时回复正好在后台完成，dsh-notify-me 会用系统通知 + 提示音 + 标签页标题标记提醒你——权限审批的通知还带「同意 / 拒绝」按钮，点一下就完成裁决，不用切回页面。开关和通知语言都直接在 **DSH 设置 → 通知提醒** 里改。

---

## 为什么需要它

DSH 的两种权限模式各有代价：

| 模式 | 你付出的代价 | 代价形态 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 不开完整访问（`workspace-write` + ask） | **等待**——agent 卡在审批上，不盯着页面就是干等 | 时间成本，随会话数增长 |
| 开完整访问（full access） | **不可逆风险**——放弃的是事前拦截能力 | 风险成本，与你盯不盯无关 |

dsh-notify-me 把「监督」和「守在屏幕前」解耦：只在真的出现决策点（审批 / 方案确认 / 提问）或回复跑完时，才用系统通知把你叫回来——**让你敢不开完整访问**，不必靠放弃拦截能力来换效率。它不降低 full access 本身的权限风险（它不是沙箱），只是把 ask 模式的等待成本压到接近零。

---

> 🔎 想找这个插件？可以搜：`dsh-notify-me`、**消息提醒**、**可操作提醒**、**桌面通知**、**需要你操作**、**回复完成提醒**、**后台完成提醒**、**外部通知**、**Discord / Bark / Gotify 推送**（npm 关键词已含以上中英文词）。

## 效果预览

| 系统通知效果（截图来自 Windows） |
| --- |
| ![DSH 通知效果](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromoany/dsh-notify-me/main/docs/screenshots/notify-toast.png) |

[更新日志](CHANGELOG.md)

## 提醒时机

| 时机 | 提醒内容 | 默认 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 🔔 **模型需要你操作** — 审批请求 / 方案待确认（plan review）/ 提问（`ask_user_question`） | 通知 + 提示音 + `🔔 需要你 ·` 标题标记；审批的通知上直接带「同意 / 拒绝」按钮 | 页面可见也提醒（当前对话除外：默认只留标题标记） |
| ✅ **回复完成** — 一轮回复跑完；后台会话完成也会报 | 通知 + 提示音；后台会话**完成但还没看**的期间标题带 `✅ 回复完成 ·` 标记，打开该会话即撤 | 仅页面隐藏/后台时提醒（标题标记不受此限） |

> **后台**子代理（subagent）子会话的等待与完成默认**不提醒**：DSH 把每个子代理子会话列成独立会话，但它们是所属主对话那一轮里的步骤，提醒只会是噪音。你当前打开的那个子代理会话不算在内，照常提醒。设置页「子代理会话不提醒」可关掉这个静音。

## 在 DSH 设置里改配置

打开 **设置 → 通知提醒**（首次安装后刷新一次页面即可看到），页面提供：

- **启用提醒** 主开关：关闭后不再弹系统通知、不播放提示音、也不改标签页标题；
- **运行环境**（默认自动识别）：按页面协议识别 Web 端 / 桌面端（DSH Desktop，`dsh-app://`），识别不准时可手动指定——桌面端点通知走 `dsh://` 深链抬窗、快捷裁决按钮不可用；Web 端走 `window.focus()` 与 Service Worker 桥。手动覆盖与自动识别不一致时，设置页会明示检测结果；
- **系统通知 / 提示音 / 音量**：Toast、提示音开关与音量滑块；
- **音效来源**（「需要你」与「回复完成」各自独立选）：内置合成音（默认）/ 自定义音频文件 / 系统通知音。选「自定义音频文件」可在设置页挑一个本地音频（上限 1 MiB，存在浏览器本地，可试听与移除）；选「系统通知音」则完全不播插件音效，通知照发，声音交给操作系统（音色跟着系统通知设置走），此时「试听」会改发一条测试通知——该模式没有插件可播的音，你听到的就是它。任一来源缺文件、读不出来或存不下时自动回落到内置合成音，提醒不会因此变成哑的；
- **外部通知**（默认关）：把提醒同时转发到你自己的推送端点，人不在电脑前也能收到——支持 **Discord Webhook** / **Bark** / **Gotify** / **自定义 Webhook**，可加多个目标，每个选类型填地址（Discord 填 Webhook 地址；Bark 填 `https://api.day.app/<设备密钥>`；Gotify 填 `https://<服务器>/message?token=<应用令牌>`；自定义端点收一条 POST JSON：`{source, event, title, body, sessionId, time}`）；「转发「需要你」」「转发「回复完成」」各自独立开关；**发送测试通知**往所有目标发一条测试消息（不受这两类开关限制，也不会冒充真提醒）。转发跟本地提醒走同一套触发规则（「当前对话不弹通知」等开关同样管它）；提醒正文会原样发往你填的地址，**只填你自己信任的端点**；
- **页面打开时也提醒「需要你」**（默认开）与 **页面打开时也提醒「回复完成」**（默认关）；
- **当前对话不弹通知**（默认开）：等待就发生在你正看着的对话里时只留标题标记，不弹通知也不响音（免得盖住审批卡片）；页面切到后台立刻补发，若你已经处理掉就作废。其它后台会话不受影响；
- **子代理会话不提醒**（默认开）：后台子代理（subagent）子会话的「需要你」与「回复完成」都不提醒——它们是主对话那一轮的步骤，完成由主对话自己的提醒覆盖；你当前打开的那个子代理会话照常提醒；关掉后恢复逐会话提醒；
- **点击通知回到对应对话**（默认开）：点通知把 DSH 带到前台并切到提醒所属的对话；多个 DSH 标签页同时开着时，一次点击只调起一个窗口（优先当前可见的那个）并只切它的对话，其余标签页不动；关掉后点通知不做任何事。桌面端（DSH Desktop）同样会把窗口带到前台并切对话：页面侧的 `window.focus()` 在 Electron 里抬不动原生窗口，1.5.2 起改走应用自己的 `dsh://open` 深链调窗（窗口隐藏在托盘里也能被抬回来）；
- **审批通知上直接裁决**（默认开）：权限审批的通知上带「同意 / 拒绝」按钮，点一下就按审批卡片的「允许一次 / 拒绝」直接裁决，不用切回页面；点通知正文仍是原来的「切回对应对话」。**桌面端暂不支持按钮**（`dsh-app://` 页面无法注册 Service Worker），审批通知自动退回无按钮样式，设置页会明示这一限制；
- **通知语言**：跟随界面 / 简体中文 / English——决定通知文字与 `🔔 …` 标题标记使用的语言；
- **测试按钮**：用当前设置立即发一条「需要你」「回复完成」或「审批按钮」测试提醒（**不受**上面「页面打开时也提醒」开关限制；「需要你」测试的标题标记约 6 秒后自动消失）；
- **版本信息**：设置页底部常显当前插件版本号（`dsh-notify-me v…`）——报障、核对是否装上新版本时直接照抄这一行。

> 需要浏览器通知权限：页面上点一下 → 允许；或地址栏锁 → 站点设置 → 通知 → 允许 → 刷新。macOS 还要在 系统设置 → 通知 里允许该浏览器。

## 提醒方式

- **系统通知**：经浏览器弹出的系统通知，进 Windows 通知中心或 macOS 通知中心（点击回到提醒所属的对话；审批的通知点按钮直接裁决）
- **提示音**：默认是 WebAudio 合成音（「需要你」与「完成」使用不同音型）；可在设置里为两类提醒分别换成自定义音频文件，或改成让操作系统播放它自己的通知音
- **标签页标题标记**：有待处理事项时，标题前出现 `🔔 需要你 · …` / `🔔 Action needed · …`；后台会话**完成但还没看**时出现 `✅ 回复完成 · …` / `✅ Reply finished · …`，打开对应会话（或它再次开跑）即消失。两种标记可同时出现，「需要你」在前；宿主改写标题后标记基于新标题重建
- **外部通知**（可选，默认关）：按设置里配的推送目标，把同一条提醒转发到 Discord Webhook / Bark / Gotify / 自定义 Webhook——临时离开电脑时，手机上的推送渠道照样收到

本插件是**浏览器层**实现：DSH 页面需保持打开（最小化/后台即可——那正是它监听的「离开」状态）。

## 安装

```powershell
# DSH 官方插件命令：安装并自动挂载进 web profile
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-notify-me
```

重启 `dsh web` 后硬刷新页面（Ctrl+Shift+R）。

**兼容性** — 插件按宿主代际自动选源，逐版本声明见 `package.json` 的 `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases`：

| 宿主代际 | 「需要你」交互来源 | 判断当前会话 | 点通知切会话 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `≤ 0.1.2-alpha.1` | 控制器快照的 `pending[]` | 快照 `current` | `sessions.open()` |
| `0.1.2-alpha.2 .. 0.1.6-alpha.1` | `uiSession.pendingInteractions` | 快照 `current` | `sessions.open()` |
| `≥ 0.1.6-alpha.2`（含 `0.2.0-rc.2`） | `uiSession.sessionStatus` | `retainedBy.mainView` | `uiWorkspace.openSession()` |

区间仅作示意：插件按 store 形状自动选源（`sessionStatus` 存在即走新路），版本号只是各形状的出现边界。`package.json` 的 `peerDependencies` 范围同理只影响 npm install 的提示文案——兼容与否以 `dshReleases` 的逐版实测声明为准，未实测的新版本由形状驱动兜底。

实测**真正激活**（各自独立 profile 启动：设置里出现「通知提醒」分区，即插件的 `apply` 确实执行）于 `0.1.2-rc.1`、`0.1.5-rc.2` 与 `0.2.0-rc.2`；更早的 `0.1.1-rc.2` 亦验证过。两个坑值得记住：一是 `dsh.client.inject` 里列了新版运行时已不再提供的包，客户端条目会停在 `pending (waiting for services: …)` 而永不执行——1.1.3 在 `0.1.2-rc.1` 及以后正是这样失效的；二是宿主换存储/字段名时**不会报错**，提醒只会静默失效——`0.2.0-rc.2` 上 `pendingInteractions`→`sessionStatus`、`list.current`→`retainedBy.mainView`、`sessions.open()`→`uiWorkspace.openSession()` 都是这一类，所以每次适配都要用 `window.__dshNotifyMe.debug()` 确认真的是 `bound`、以及用的是哪个来源。

**验证** — F12 控制台执行：

```js
window.__dshNotifyMe.test("done")        // 「完成」示例
window.__dshNotifyMe.test("attention")   // 「需要你」示例
window.__dshNotifyMe.test("approval")    // 「审批按钮」示例：通知上有「同意 / 拒绝」，点着试试
window.__dshNotifyMe.debug()             // 桥接状态看 bridge 字段，active = 按钮可用
```

没反应？九成是：通知权限被拒绝（在页面上点一下 → 选「允许」；或地址栏锁 → 站点设置 → 通知 → 允许 → 刷新）、装完没重启 DSH、系统设置里浏览器通知被关。

## 控制台高级配置

设置页是第一入口；想脚本化/批量改或恢复默认时，偏好存 `localStorage`（`dshNotifyMe.config`），可用控制台实时调整：

```js
window.__dshNotifyMe.config                       // 查看
window.__dshNotifyMe.setConfig({
  enabled: true,           // false = 关闭所有提醒（主开关）
  language: "auto",        // 'auto' 跟随界面 | 'zh' 简体中文 | 'en' English
  attentionHiddenOnly: false, // true = 页面可见时「需要你」不提醒
  currentHiddenOnly: true,    // true = 当前对话的等待只留标题标记（转后台补发）
  doneHiddenOnly: true,       // false = 页面可见时「完成」也提醒
  ignoreSubagent: true,       // true = 后台子代理（subagent）会话不提醒（当前打开的照常）
  toast: true,                // 系统通知开关
  sound: true,                // 提示音开关（含「系统通知音」模式）
  soundDone: "synth",         // 「完成」音效来源：'synth' 内置 | 'custom' 自定义文件 | 'system' 系统通知音
  soundAttention: "synth",    // 「需要你」音效来源，取值同上
  volume: 0.5,                // 音量 0~1
  autoFocus: true,            // 点通知回到提醒所属的对话
  quickActions: true,         // 审批通知上的「同意 / 拒绝」按钮
  externalEnabled: false,     // 外部通知转发主开关（默认关：不填端点就什么都不发）
  externalAttention: true,    // 转发「需要你」（触发规则跟本地提醒完全一致）
  externalDone: true,         // 转发「回复完成」
  externalTargets: []         // 推送目标：[{id, type:'discord'|'bark'|'gotify'|'custom', url}]
})
window.__dshNotifyMe.resetConfig()                // 恢复默认（同时清掉已选的自定义音效文件）
window.__dshNotifyMe.decide("approval:3", "allowed-once")  // 程序化裁决："allowed-once" | "rejected"
window.__dshNotifyMe.testExternal()               // 向所有推送目标发一条测试通知，返回 {sent, unverified, failed, statuses}
```

> 自定义音效文件不在 `dshNotifyMe.config` 里，而是按类别各存一个键（`dshNotifyMe.sound.done` / `dshNotifyMe.sound.attention`，内容是 `{name, size, data}` 的 data URL）——一个文件转成 data URL 会膨胀约 1.37 倍，塞进配置会拖慢每次读取。`resetConfig()` 会连这两个键一起清掉。
>
> 想确认当前生效的来源，看 `window.__dshNotifyMe.debug()` 的 `soundDone` / `soundAttention` 与 `customSoundDone` / `customSoundAttention`。

## 工作原理

提醒核心按宿主代际取源（见上表），当前会话一律来自客户端 `sessions` 服务：

- **当前会话** `SessionSnapshot`：`running` true→false = 回复完成；
- **待办交互**：`uiSession` 的 `sessionStatus`（`≥ 0.1.6`，逐会话 `pendingInteraction`）或 `pendingInteractions`（`0.1.2 .. 0.1.5`）出现新 key = 模型在等你，容器里带上审批工具名 / 理由、提问文本；旧宿主回落到控制器快照的 `pending[]`；
- **其它已列会话**摘要：`running` true→false（或旧宿主的 `completed` 边沿）= 后台工作提醒。宿主的「完成未读」级别标志负责补漏与标题标记：`≥ 0.1.6` 用 `sessionStatus` 行的 `completionUnread`（后台会话完成即点亮、打开该会话/再次开跑/会话消失即清零），旧宿主用列表行的 `completed` 提醒位（选中会话即清零）；页面没看见的完成边沿（插件热重载中途、快照合并跳变）由此补报一次，边沿与级别标志同来时按短时间窗合并，只响一声。
- **子代理会话**：列表行带 `origin: 'subagent'`（并有 `parentId`）的**后台**会话默认静音；你正打开着的那个子代理会话不算静音对象，它的提醒走当前对话的常规规则（页面可见时默认只留标题标记、转后台补发），切进来时积压的等待同样补上，切走后重新静音。只有 `parentId`、没有 `origin` 的分支（fork）会话属于你自己的对话，始终照常提醒。

提醒核心仍然零第三方运行时依赖、完全自包含：通知文字按所选语言（跟随界面 / 中文 / English）即时解析。设置页是**可选**的 React 呈现层——当 DSH web profile 提供 `slots` / `locale` / `react` 时才注册进「设置 → 通知提醒」，缺任一能力时插件自动降级为纯提醒（无设置页），不影响功能。

### 快捷裁决怎么走通的

通知按钮（`actions`）只属于 Service Worker 弹的持久通知，往 `new Notification()` 里传 `actions` 会直接抛 `TypeError`——这是绕不开的浏览器限制。所以 bundle 一份文件干两件事：页面里照常注册提醒工厂，同一份字节再注册成一个只干转信的 Service Worker，把「点了哪个按钮」（同意 / 拒绝 / 点正文）带回页面。真正的裁决发生在页面里，调的是审批卡片自己用的 `PendingApproval.answer('allowed-once' | 'rejected')`，所以「同意」就是「允许一次」，不多放行任何东西。点正文的「调窗口 + 切对话」同样归 worker 这半侧调度：它用 `client.focus()` 只调起一个窗口（优先当前可见的），并只让那个窗口切对话——多个 DSH 标签页不会互相抢焦点或一起乱切。

每条按钮通知按交互 key 记账，一次只认领一条等待；请求被页面里答掉、或被新请求顶替之后，残留通知上的按钮再点也不会误裁，只是安静地关掉。带按钮的通知不设自动消失——审批没裁决就一直留在通知中心里等你。

### 桌面端怎么抬窗的

DSH Desktop 是一层 Electron 壳，页面跑在 `dsh-app://app` 下：DOM 的 `window.focus()` 只动浏览器窗口对象、碰不到原生窗口，壳的 `will-navigate` / `window-open` 又把页面里发 `dsh://` 的常规出口全堵上了——所以 1.5.1 及以前点通知只在后台切好对话，窗口不上前台。1.5.2 起点通知正文时页面发一条隐藏 iframe 导航到 `dsh://open`：子框架导航不经过壳的 `will-navigate` 拦截，URL 交给系统协议注册，应用的单实例锁收到第二次启动后走 `focusPrimaryWindow()`（restore + show + focus）——与登录完成页把客户端置前是同一条路。窗口隐藏在托盘、被别的窗口压住、最小化，都能被抬回来。浏览器端不受影响，仍走 `window.focus()` / worker `client.focus()`。

真实壳已实测（DSH Desktop 0.2.0-rc.2，issue #9 三轮复测）：点通知 = 抬窗 + 切会话一步到位，跨会话、窗口在后台时同样稳定。触发时机是这条链路的关键：深链必须在**带用户手势的处理器**里发——通知的 `onclick` 自带手势，所以产品路径通；而无手势的脚本化注入（如 CDP evaluate 手工塞 iframe）会被 Chromium 静默丢弃、外部协议根本不回流，复现时看起来就像「通道被拦死」。

## 已知限制

- 页面必须开着才会提醒（后台标签/最小化可以；关标签页即失效——浏览器层方案固有限制）。
- 通知经由浏览器弹出，需允许浏览器通知权限，且勿扰模式不能屏蔽它。
- 每次页面加载后第一次出声/弹通知前，需在页面上点击过一次（浏览器自动播放与权限策略）。
- 未授权通知权限时只有提示音与标题标记。
- 快捷裁决按钮要 Service Worker：`http://127.0.0.1`、`https` 可用，`http://192.168.x.x` 这类局域网地址不行；**桌面端（`dsh-app://`）已实测无法注册 Service Worker**，按钮渲染不了，审批通知退回无按钮样式。浏览器或桌面宿主不渲染通知按钮时，`window.__dshNotifyMe.debug()` 的 `bridge` 字段会说明原因，其余功能不受影响。
- macOS：浏览器里提醒、提示音、标题标记、点通知跳转都没有平台假设，照常工作；但 DSH Desktop（Electron）的系统通知要求应用已签名，未签名的通知直接发不出去，官方 macOS 版是否满足这一前提未实测；审批按钮在 macOS 桌面宿主上的渲染同样未实测（Windows 桌面端已实测不渲染，见上条），不渲染时自动退回无按钮通知。
- 配置存在浏览器 `localStorage`：换浏览器/设备或清除站点数据后会回到默认值（设置页可一键恢复默认）。
- `≥ 0.1.6`（含 `0.2.0-rc.2`）的「回复完成」提醒正文只有会话名，不再附带回复摘要——宿主快照已不再提供 `nodes`；提醒本身照常触发。
- 标题标记由宿主与插件共同写 `document.title`：宿主重算标题时标记可能被覆盖，直到下一次提醒事件重新写成。
- 「当前对话不弹通知」按 `document.hidden` 判定：窗口被别的应用完全盖住时仍算「页面可见」，此时当前对话的等待照样静默。
- 外部通知转发受浏览器跨域（CORS）限制：端点不放行时自动降级为「送出但不可确认」（no-cors），如实标为「已送出不可确认」；Discord Webhook 官方放行跨域，可直接确认送达。HTTP 错误如实记失败、不重试。转发在本地提醒决定要发之后才触发，所以被「当前对话不弹通知」等规则静音的提醒也不会外发。

## 开发自检

```powershell
node --check lib\client.js
node --check lib\index.js
node smoke\smoke-test.cjs        # 离线状态机冒烟测试：三代宿主 + 主开关 + 中英语言用例 + 快捷裁决桥（Service Worker 半侧一并跑）
node smoke\cordis-host-test.mjs  # 真 cordis 端到端（找不到本机 DSH 时自动跳过）
npm pack --dry-run               # 预览发布包
```

`cordis-host-test.mjs` 会从本机 DSH 安装借 `@deepseek-ai/cordis`（依次探测 npm 全局目录、`~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules` 与 `~/.dsh/profiles/node_modules` 平铺回退目录）；源码 checkout 里没有 profile 依赖时，用 `DSH_CORDIS_PATH=<checkout>/vendor/cordis/lib/index.js` 指定即可。

## 致谢与贡献须知

贡献者（按 handle 列出，链接指向他们参与的 PR / issue）：

- [@AgMahone](https://github.com/AgMahone) — [#7](https://github.com/chromoany/dsh-notify-me/pull/7)：0.1.6+ / 0.2.0 宿主代际支持，以及通知双响、cordis 查找路径的报障与复测；
- [@d0ublecl1ck](https://github.com/d0ublecl1ck) — [#8](https://github.com/chromoany/dsh-notify-me/pull/8)：子代理会话静音（`ignoreSubagent`）与配套测试、文档；1.4.0 里「只静音后台子代理、当前打开的照常提醒」的口径同样出自他在 #8 讨论里的建议，落地由维护者完成；
- [@EliteOtaku](https://github.com/EliteOtaku) — [#9](https://github.com/chromoany/dsh-notify-me/issues/9)：桌面端抬窗链路（1.5.2）的逐层排查与真实壳三轮复测——确认点通知抬窗 + 切会话稳定生效，并定位出「无用户手势的脚本化注入被 Chromium 静默丢弃」这一复现差异，纠正了最初「沙箱拦死」的判断；
- [@Wh1stle05](https://github.com/Wh1stle05) — [#10](https://github.com/chromoany/dsh-notify-me/pull/10)：「音效来源」功能（内置合成音 / 自定义音频文件 / 系统通知音，「需要你」与「回复完成」各自独立选），含设置页交互、回落链与测试、文档；「系统通知音」试听改发测试通知、假 React 按索引跨渲染保持 hook 状态这两处修正同样出自该 PR。
- [@yanzhaohui1999](https://github.com/yanzhaohui1999) — [#13](https://github.com/chromoany/dsh-notify-me/issues/13) / [#14](https://github.com/chromoany/dsh-notify-me/pull/14)：482 个会话下空闲页面烧 CPU 的性能报告（定位到 `currentSessionId()` 每行重扫全表，实测占 CPU 5.9%~6.5%）与修复（一次列表变化只推导一次「当前会话」），并带先红后绿的回归断言——4 行与 40 行的列表变化代价必须相等（上游报 7 vs 43，修后 5 vs 5）。
- [@RiZhiZhaoYi](https://github.com/RiZhiZhaoYi) — [#12](https://github.com/chromoany/dsh-notify-me/issues/12)：外部通知转发（Discord Webhook / Bark / Gotify / 自定义 Webhook）的功能建议与使用场景（1.7.0）。

署名口径：本仓库收编外部 PR 时以维护者提交落地——不沿用原 commit、不挂 Co-authored-by，GitHub 的 contributors 图只显示维护者，贡献者以上面的致谢署名。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-plugin-session-manager

仓库：<https://github.com/cmsj33071/dsh-plugin-session-manager>

DSH 会话管理插件：给会话行「…」菜单加上**导出备份**、**归档**、**彻底删除**三项能力，并在宿主侧自带一套安全门与回收站。提供三件事：

| 能力 | 性质 | 入口 |
|---|---|---|
| **导出备份** | 只读，可反复执行 | 会话行菜单 → 下载备份（ZIP）／备份到 DSH 目录 |
| **归档（软删除）** | 可逆，走官方 API | 会话行菜单 → 归档 |
| **彻底删除** | 不可逆（可回收站恢复） | 会话行菜单 → 彻底删除… → 确认框 |

> **当前状态：可用。** 曾因宿主半侧解析 DSH home 失败而长期「休眠」（装了但界面无任何入口），另有一个必崩的客户端 hook 顺序错误；两者均已修复并验证，见下一节。
>
> 本文档里的 `C:\Users\33071\...` 是作者机器路径，作为实测证据保留；自己动手时把 `$env:USERPROFILE` 那一层换成你的用户目录即可。

---

## 快速开始

```powershell
# 1. 装进 profile（pnpm/node 用 DSH 自带的那份；DSH 安装位置按自己的改）
$dsHome   = "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh"
$resource = "C:\Users\33071\AppData\Local\Programs\DeepSeek Harness\resources"
$node = "$resource\runtime\primary-runtime\dependencies\node\bin\node.exe"
$pnpm = "$resource\runtime\pnpm\bin\pnpm.cjs"

# 从 GitHub 装（公开仓库）
& $node $pnpm --dir "$dsHome\profiles\desktop" add "github:cmsj33071/dsh-plugin-session-manager"
# 或从本地源码目录装
& $node $pnpm --dir "$dsHome\profiles\desktop" add "file:<本目录的绝对路径>"
```

```jsonc
// 2. 在 <profile>\package.json 的 dsh.profile.bundles 末尾追加；不要手写 cordis.patch.yml
"dsh-plugin-session-manager"
```

3. 重启 DSH，确认 `<DSH_HOME>\session-manager\active.json` 出现、会话行「…」里出现「会话管理」一组。

插件**零运行时依赖**（宿主半侧只 import `node:*`），客户端无构建步骤，clone 下来即可用。

---

## 本次修复（2026-10-15）

| # | 症状 | 根因 | 修法 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 插件「装了但什么都没出现」，`~/.dsh/session-manager/active.json` 始终不存在 | `resolveHome()` 只认 `ctx.get('homePaths')` 和 `$DSH_HOME`。但 **`homePaths` 不是 cordis 服务**：在 121 MiB 的 `app.asar` 全文里搜 `homePaths` 命中 **0** 次，`@deepseek-ai/dsh-home-paths` 是纯函数库（其 README 原文：*Use it as a direct library dependency, not through `cordis.yml`*）；而桌面宿主进程的 `DSH_HOME` 是空的（实测 boot 探针 `dshHomeEnv: null`）。两个候选全部落空 → home 为 `undefined` → 插件保持空闲 | 按 `dsh-home-paths` 的优先级自行解析：`config.home` → `homePaths`（若真存在）→ **非空** `$DSH_HOME` → `os.homedir()/.dsh`。只 import `node:os`，不引入任何 `@deepseek-ai/*` 依赖 |
| 2 | 「彻底删除…」确认框永不出现（点了像没反应） | 确认框组件在第二个 `useSessionManager` **之前**就 `return null`。React 按位置识别 hook：无待确认时 1 个 hook、有待确认时 2 个 → 抛 `Rendered more hooks than during the previous render` | 两个 hook 调用提到所有提前 return 之前；无待确认时 selector 返回 `undefined` |
| 3 | 预览（plan）可能写盘 | 写锁探测用 `open(id,'write')`，而 JSONL 后端在**历史代际**日志上会在 write-open 时发布迁移后的后继文件 | 代际低于当前格式（v4）时跳过写锁探测（计划项记为 `lockProbe: 'not-probed'`）；删除前仍有 `flush` + revision 比对兜底 |
| 4 | 诊断噪音 | `lib/index.js` 每次加载写 3 个 `probe-*.json` | 删掉分阶段探针，只保留 `active.json`，并让它记录 `home` / `homeSource` / `routes` / `failures` |
| 5 | 部分文件带 GBK/UTF-8 混编乱码（`鈥?`、`閳?`） | 早期写入编码错误 | 全部改回正确的 `—` |
| 6 | 清单指向不存在的 `lib/types/index.d.ts` | `types` / `exports["."].types` 声明了但文件从未创建 | 补上该声明文件 |
| 7 | 删除成功后侧边栏仍留着那一行（点开报错） | 侧边栏渲染的是客户端 Session Controller 的**缓存基线**，而基线只在拉取时从持久化后端重建；删掉磁盘上的日志不会通知它 | 确认删除成功后调用 `ctx.get('sessions').refresh()` 重新拉基线（`refresh` 不在 `sessions` 服务文档契约里，因此按调用时探测 + `typeof` 守卫处理，缺失即静默跳过），失败不改变「删除已成功」的结论 |

**为什么自检没发现第 1 条**：`check-manifest.mjs` 的桩上下文**自己伪造了 `homePaths.dshHome`**，于是「插件取不到 home」这条真实路径从未被覆盖——测试通过、插件照旧休眠。该桩已删除，并新增一组断言直接覆盖「没有任何服务、也没有 `$DSH_HOME`」时的默认 home。

---

## 为什么这个插件必须自己实现删除

DSH **在设计上刻意没有会话删除能力**，这不是遗漏：

- `dsh-session-persistence` 的已知限制原文：`No deletion or retention API — pruning stored sessions is out-of-band backend maintenance.`
- JSONL 后端原文：`Nothing deletes session files — logs accumulate under root until removed externally.`
- workspace 包把 `session deletion` 列为 absent capability。
- 客户端 `session.*` 的 19 个 Remote 方法里没有删除/归档；归档在 `workspace.*`。
- 桌面 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里也没有任何相关覆盖。

所以「删除」只能由插件在宿主侧按后端的磁盘约定自己完成。本插件把这件事做成**默认可逆**（移入回收站），并加了一组硬性安全门。

## 界面接入点

按官方插件的做法，只做**加法**，不替换任何现有 UI：

| slot | 类型 | 用途 |
|---|---|---|
| `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` | `list` | 会话行「…」菜单里新增一组「会话管理」。同席已有官方 pin(100)/rename(200)/fork(300)/archive(400)，本插件取 `order: 500`。 |
| `shell.overlay` | `list` | 确认框挂载点，与官方 `workspace.session-archive` 等确认框同一层。 |

行菜单的 owner props 是 `{ sessionId, displayTitle }`，并额外注入 `useMenuOpenState()`（动作前必须先关菜单，否则会被行自身的 dismiss 吞掉）与 `useShortcuts()`。

删除成功后，操作会再调用一次 `ctx.get('sessions').refresh()`：侧边栏的行来自客户端 Session Controller 的基线快照（宿主每次都从持久化后端重读，见 `session-query` 的 `listSessions`），不重新拉取的话被删的行会继续显示。该调用是可选的（`refresh()` 不在服务文档契约里），缺失或被拒都不影响「删除已完成」的结论。

删除同时清掉两类衍生状态：`~/.dsh/storages/session_projcache/sessions/<id>.json`（projection cache，列表的冷会话摘要会读它）与插件自己的所有权索引条目。会话搜索索引（`dsh-session-query-sqlite`）不需要插件插手——它会在下一次搜索时按持久化快照对账，自行剔除已消失的源。

导出 ZIP 复用官方已交付的 `/api/session.export`（`dsh-session-log-export`），它已经能导出「会话 + 子会话 + 全部附件」。备份到 DSH 目录走本插件自己的路由，落规范 JSONL，不依赖浏览器下载目录。

## 宿主路由

全部注册在 `connection.fetch`（精确路由、同源鉴权 cookie，客户端无需附加凭据），前缀 `/api/session-manager`。客户端一律使用**文档相对路径**（无前导 `/`）。

| 方法 | 路径 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` / `HEAD` | `/` | 会话清单：`items`、`warnings`、`storage`、`truncated` |
| `POST` | `/plan` | 删除预览：返回将要移除的目录集合（每项含 `bytes` / `files` / `revision` / `logGeneration` / `lockProbe`）、总字节数、血亲子集、**拦截原因**、一次性 `token` |
| `POST` | `/remove` | 执行删除：必须携带 `token`，可选 `force` |
| `POST` | `/export` | 导出到 DSH 目录（`~/.dsh/session-manager/exports/<时间戳>-<label>/`） |
| `GET` | `/trash` | 回收站条目 |
| `POST` | `/trash/prune` | 按保留期清理回收站 |

命令：`/sessions` 报告存储与回收站用量，不产生模型轮次。

## 安全设计

删除是本插件里唯一破坏性操作，因此它被设计成「默认拦下来，只有明确确认才动」。代码中的硬性保证：

1. **先预览，后执行，token 绑定。** `token` 是对「本次将删除的目录 id + 字节数 + 存储 revision + 子会话集合」的 SHA-256 摘要。预览之后任何会话新增、消失或被重写，token 都会失配并拒绝执行（`session/confirmation-mismatch`）。
2. **活动会话不放行。** `ctx.sessions.get(id)` 命中则计入拦截。带 `force` 时会先 `agents.get(id).cancel({kind:'user'})` 再 `await whenIdle()`（默认上限 10s，超时即拒绝）。
   > 这一条不是洁癖：删除一个仍有活写句柄的会话，会让该句柄在下一次 append 时用 `open(path,'a')` 重建一个**没有 header 帧**的残片，此后该会话永久 `SessionPersistenceCorruptionError`。
3. **跨进程写锁不放行。** 通过 `sessionPersistence.open(id,'write')` 探测 `SessionAlreadyOwnedError`（Windows 上是内核租约，零超时等待，不会卡住预览），命中即拒绝（`session/writer-held`）。**但历史代际日志不探测**：JSONL 后端在 write-open 一个非当前格式的后代时会在 open 内发布迁移文件（`publishStoredMigration`），而预览必须只读；这类会话的计划项记 `lockProbe: 'not-probed'`，删除前由 flush + revision 比对兜底。
4. **血缘闭包必须完整。** 删除会递归覆盖全部子孙（`header.parentSession` 传递闭包）。以下情形一律拦截：存在被排除在计划外的子会话（会产生孤儿）、计划内会话的父会话不可见（血缘链不可信）、后端列出但磁盘无法定位的会话落在计划内。
5. **不 unlink，先进回收站。** 目录用 `rename` 移入 `~/.dsh/session-manager/trash/<ISO时间>-<id>/`，并写 `manifest.json`。同一卷上 `rename` 是原子的，因此不会出现「删一半」的破损目录，也留下了恢复路径（`restoreTrashEntry`）。保留期默认 30 天，`trashRetentionDays: 0` 关闭清理。
6. **删除顺序：先子后父。** 即使中途失败也不会留下「记录中的子会话已消失」的父目录。
7. **同步清理衍生状态。** 删除日志后一并删 `~/.dsh/storages/session_projcache/sessions/<id>.json`。该缓存是派生数据且**没有任何驱逐机制**（本机已积累 6 个孤儿），不清就是长期脏数据。
8. **绝不碰附件。** 附件是内容寻址、去重、可跨会话共享的，按会话删会破坏**其他**会话的历史读取。

## 配置

| 字段 | 默认值 | 含义 |
|---|---|---|
| `home` | 未设置 | 显式 DSH home；优先级最高，覆盖 `$DSH_HOME` 与 `~/.dsh` |
| `sessionsRoot` | `<DSH_HOME>/sessions` | 会话存储根；后端 `root` 是配置项，非默认部署需显式指定 |
| `storagesRoot` | `<DSH_HOME>/storages` | 派生状态根，用于定位 projection cache |
| `clearProjectionCache` | `true` | 删除时一并清理该会话的 projection cache 记录 |
| `trashRetentionDays` | `30` | 回收站保留天数；`0` 关闭清理 |
| `trackOwnership` | `true` | 维护插件自有的会话所有权索引 |
| `allowForceRemoveLive` | `true` | 是否允许在停稳活动会话后强制删除 |
| `stopTimeoutMs` | `10000` | 等待活动会话 `whenIdle()` 的上限 |
| `listLimit` | `500` | 单次清单返回上限 |

`SessionsRoot` 未显式提供时按 `<DSH_HOME>/sessions` 推断；home 的解析优先级是 `config.home` → `homePaths` 服务（若组合里真有）→ 非空 `$DSH_HOME` → `~/.dsh`。全部落空时插件保持空闲并打一条 warn，而不是抛错。
