It ports frequently used CLI operations (token calculation, code search, session management) to native Rust, while delegating conversation workflows and model execution transparently to upstream `dsh`. All existing arguments and options continue to work as-is. ## Why rdsh? - ⚡ **Sub-millisecond startup & low memory**: `--version` launches in ~0.90 ms with ~2.9 MB peak memory, compared to ~88 ms and ~66 MB for Node.js-based `dsh`. - 🔄 **100% Drop-in Compatible**: Subcommands that are not rdsh-native are passed straight to upstream `dsh`. Existing scripts and workflows keep running unchanged. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and run health diagnostics (`rdsh doctor`) instantly without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and `rdsh_inspect` can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and inspect local prerequisites (`rdsh doctor --json`) without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and agent tools can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. ## Table of Contents - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Usage](#usage) - [Running with `dsh` Compatibility](#running-with-dsh-compatibility) - [Fast Native Commands](#fast-native-commands) - [Credential sharing with rdsh auth](#credential-sharing-with-rdsh-auth) - [Agent Tool Isolation](#agent-tool-isolation) - [Hook Guard](#hook-guard-rdsh-guard) - [Context Injection](#context-injection-rdsh-context) - [Dependency Graph and Change Impact](#dependency-graph-and-change-impact-rdsh-deps) - [Web UI & Dashboard](#web-ui--dashboard) - [Using with Smart-DSH](#using-with-smart-dsh) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Safety Design](#safety-design) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Community](#community) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Quick Start Already using **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, OpenCode or Gemini CLI**? [Connect the project dashboard through MCP](docs/MCP-CLIENTS.md) to share tasks, questions and structured UI while keeping your current coding agent. This entry point requires Node.js 22+; DSH and Rust are optional. ### 1. Install (Prebuilt Binary) **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --from-release ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell $f = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'rdsh-install.ps1' Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile $f -UseBasicParsing & $f -FromRelease ``` ### 2. Verify & Setup ```sh rdsh --version && rdsh doctor # verify install and original dsh rdsh setup # interactive setup (or rdsh setup --web for browser UI) ``` *Note: If you have an existing login from Codex CLI (ChatGPT OAuth) or opencode, import it with `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex`.* ### 3. Start a Conversation ```sh rdsh tui # start with TUI profile # or rdsh --profile web # start with Web profile ``` ## Requirements | Item | Detail | | --- | --- | | OS | Linux, macOS, WSL, Windows (native) | | DSH runtime | Required for conversations and agent runs (native tools and diagnostics run standalone) | | Rust | 1.85+ (only needed when building from source; prebuilt binaries require no Rust) | | Optional | Node.js 22+ for the [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md); SearXNG for `search-web` | ## Installation ### Building from Source & Advanced Options **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh ./install.sh # build + install to ~/.local/bin/rdsh ./install.sh --as-dsh # also replace `dsh` command (original backed up as dsh-orig) ./install.sh --restore # undo the replacement ./install.sh --prefix=DIR # custom install directory (default: ~/.local/bin) ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh .\install.ps1 # build + install to %LOCALAPPDATA%\rdsh\bin .\install.ps1 -AsDsh # also replace `dsh` command .\install.ps1 -Restore # undo the replacement .\install.ps1 -Wsl # also install inside WSL via install.sh ``` | OS | Script | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./install.sh` | Needs `cargo` or `curl` (guided via rustup if missing). | | WSL | `./install.sh` inside distro | Auto-detects WSL. `install.ps1 -Wsl` installs in both environments. | | Windows (native) | `.\install.ps1` | Needs Rust and MSVC build tools (`winget install Rustlang.Rustup`). | ## Usage ### Running with `dsh` Compatibility Run any standard `dsh` command unchanged: ```sh rdsh tui # equivalent to: dsh --profile tui rdsh --profile web --patch x.yml # launch with configuration overlay rdsh --dry-run tui -- --resume id # print what would be executed ``` When installed with `./install.sh --as-dsh`, typing `dsh` automatically uses the fast `rdsh` launcher. ### Fast Native Commands Native tools execute in Rust without starting Node.js: ```sh rdsh tokens ./README.md # estimate token count (~4 chars = 1 tok, CJK = 1 tok each) echo "..." | rdsh prune --max-tokens 4000 # prune context within a token budget rdsh search TODO --dir . --max 100 # fast parallel text search rdsh sessions --limit 20 --tokens # list sessions and unpacked token estimates rdsh compact ./s.jsonl # compact session JSONL (source remains untouched) rdsh doctor # check health of dsh, environment, and paths rdsh doctor --json # read-only metadata for scripts; no DSH/Node launch rdsh profiles / rdsh skills # list available profiles and skills rdsh desktop status # detect the DeepSeek Harness Desktop app and profile rdsh bench --n 5 # benchmark startup speed between rdsh and dsh ``` On Windows, compressed session histories are not opened until rdsh can reject parent junctions safely; `sessions --tokens` may omit those histories and its totals are inexact. ### Credential sharing with rdsh auth External credentials are inventoried without showing their values. Nothing is copied until you select a source and credential. OAuth copies use DSH's existing version-1 store at $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; API keys use its named refs. The selection policy contains only identifiers at $DSH_HOME/rdsh-auth-sharing.json. ```sh rdsh auth # sources, destinations, selection and undo steps rdsh auth --json # secret-free machine-readable inventory rdsh --dry-run auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # preview; writes no files rdsh auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # share only Codex OAuth rdsh auth --select opencode:openai-codex --import # OpenCode openai maps to openai-codex rdsh auth --select codex:OPENAI_API_KEY --import # separate opt-in for Codex's API key rdsh auth --select env:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY --import # explicitly persist this environment key rdsh auth --unselect codex:openai-codex # stop future copies; retain the existing copy rdsh setup # sync selected credentials, then guide setup rdsh setup --web # inventory, selection commands and explicit key save ``` For a one-time import, use `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex --source codex` or `rdsh auth --import --ref OPENAI_API_KEY --source codex`. These filters do not save or extend future-copy consent; `--select`/`--unselect` are separate persistent policy changes. Repeat --select/--unselect for individual credentials. Selecting enables future imports from that CLI/provider, including boot, dump-config, plugin, raw dsh delegation and setup. --import immediately applies the selection. Even a newer grant in another, unselected CLI cannot be chosen. Newer DSH grants and existing API-key refs/records remain in place. Other entries, comments and line endings are preserved. Unix credential and policy files use mode 0600. The inventory checks Codex's ~/.codex/auth.json and OpenCode's $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json (or its platform default data directory), plus the legacy ~/.config/opencode/auth.json fallback. Selectors for OpenCode use DSH provider IDs; opencode:openai-codex is the selector for its openai login. Environment-key persistence supports DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. These are format/presence checks, not live authentication tests. An environment variable already supplied to rdsh is inherited by DSH and its child processes without rdsh writing a file. The JSON inventory marks this route persistent=false, lists its destination and explains how to stop/revoke it. Using the reference does not opt in to storing it. setup --yes no longer saves every environment key; choose each one with auth --select env:NAME --import. Interactive setup and the web form still allow an explicit, individual key save. **Scope and undo:** saved entries are available to every DSH profile using the same DSH_HOME. Unselect stops future rdsh imports; it does not delete a saved copy or invalidate a running process. Stop DSH and remove the named record/ref from the credential store to stop using a saved copy. To invalidate the credential itself, revoke the OAuth grant or rotate the API key at its provider. That may also disconnect the source CLI. This controls rdsh copying, not DSH's own refreshes, inherited environment access or an OS sandbox. **Migration:** existing DSH credentials are retained. A missing policy selects nothing, including for legacy auth --import. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=1 does not restore the old import-all behavior. Inventory and preview first, then choose the sources you need. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=0 disables automatic imports while keeping the selection; an explicit auth --import still works. Invalid/unreadable policies fail closed instead of falling back to legacy sync. Consent changes and rdsh credential writes share a lock, so a completed unselect cannot be bypassed by a queued rdsh import using an earlier policy. After a crashed writer, check that no rdsh auth/setup writer is active before removing $DSH_HOME/.rdsh-auth-sharing.lock; the launcher skips copying while it is locked. setup --web issues a new local access key at startup in its #key=... URL. The tab retains that key; status reads, key saves and closing require it. Keep the startup URL private. The page shows copy destinations and separate unselect, saved-copy removal and provider revocation steps before a key save. ### Optional extras (off by default) Server-type features stay off until enabled, so a plain install remains a fast dsh: ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve,search-web rdsh settings get extras.enable ``` | Extra | Command | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `serve` | `rdsh serve` (default :38080) | Local status page, localhost only, per-launch key. | | `search-web` | `rdsh search-web "query" --limit 5` | Needs SearXNG. | To connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that dsh does not ship (HAI, Sarashina, a home llama.cpp / vLLM / LM Studio / Ollama server), add it as a profile route: ```sh rdsh provider add hai --model deepseek-v4-flash # key from HAI_API_KEY or --key-stdin rdsh provider add sarashina # key from SARASHINA_API_KEY; mini and nano built in rdsh provider add local-openai --base-url http://host:8080/v1 --discover --no-key rdsh provider list # presets, per-profile route and key status ``` Details: [docs/PROVIDERS.md](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Model Catalog (`rdsh models`) DeepSeek Harness answers "which models can this provider serve?" from the catalog bundled in its `@earendil-works/pi-ai` dependency, which is generated when that package is published. Anything a provider changes afterwards is absent from the picker until that dependency is upgraded — and a profile that lists `models:` explicitly replaces the bundled catalog for the route anyway. `rdsh models` reads the provider's own catalog (the local Codex CLI, or Kimi Code's `/v1/models` endpoint with the profile's API key) and folds it into the profile: ```sh rdsh models # read-only: missing ids and stale names rdsh models --provider kimi-coding # one provider only rdsh models sync # add missing entries, refresh stale names rdsh models sync --profile web --dry-run # preview one profile ``` Nothing is deleted, an existing entry keeps every other byte (a name the provider's current one already contains is left as written), and a profile the command does not recognize is refused instead of rewritten. The harness picks the changes up on the next config reload or restart. ### Agent Tool Isolation Delegated agent tools keep normal file access by default: the model reads and writes the project like any other tool. `--share-file` isolates **`rdsh_inspect` only**. On Linux (with bubblewrap and prlimit) that tool sees just the files you explicitly share: ```sh rdsh --share-file README.md --share-file src/main.rs --profile tui ``` From `rdsh_inspect`, only the shared files are mounted read-only, host files stay out of reach and the sandbox has no network. Turn the same boundary on for every run with `rdsh features on agent_tool_sandbox` (off again with `rdsh features off agent_tool_sandbox`, or force it with `RDSH_SECURITY=1`). Other DSH tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `run_code`, ...) are **not** isolated and follow upstream DSH permissions and approvals. Startup prints `[rdsh security] rdsh_inspect is isolated; other DSH tools use upstream permissions`. ### Hook Guard (`rdsh guard`) Integrates with DSH `hooks.json` to inspect and block dangerous commands before execution: ```sh echo "$input" | rdsh guard --deny "rm -rf /*" --deny "*token*" ``` For an opt-in structured check of supported file tools, pass a policy file. This example permits `Read` only under one existing project directory: ```json { "schema": 1, "rules": [ { "id": "project-read", "tool": "Read", "access": "read", "roots": ["/absolute/project/path"] } ] } ``` ```sh echo "$hook_json" | rdsh guard --policy-file ./hook-policy.json --json ``` The structured classifier supports the `Read`, `Write`, and `Edit` file-path schemas. It canonicalizes the working directory and target, checks the selected tool and read/write scope against existing policy roots, and reports `allow`, `deny`, or `unknown` with a non-sensitive reason. In JSON mode an `allow` is classification only and omits `decision`; the host still owns permission and approval. Unknown tools, shell commands, malformed input, and unsupported tool arguments fail closed. Shell parsing and network destinations are not implemented. Path checks are advisory and can race with later filesystem changes; this hook is not an OS sandbox. Use the actual execution sandbox for enforcement. ```json { "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "rdsh guard --deny \"rm -rf /*\"" }] } ] } } ``` ### Context Injection (`rdsh context`) `rdsh context inject` assembles this turn's context — goal, constraints, decisions, working set, git state, retrieved code, and curated memory — and emits it in the DSH `UserPromptSubmit` hook contract, so the model sees it without any copy-paste: ```sh rdsh features on context_engine # the engine is opt-in rdsh context hook install # merges $DSH_HOME/hooks.json (idempotent) rdsh context hook status --json ``` The hook is fail-open: it never blocks a prompt and always exits 0. Only an unreadable settings document or an unparseable payload inject nothing at all; a corrupt index or a missed deadline drops just what depends on them — the graph or the code search — and still injects goal, constraints, and memory. Injection has its own budget (`context.inject_budget`, default 1200 tokens) and deadline (`context.inject_deadline_ms`, default 1200 ms); once the deadline passes the code search is skipped and only memory, goal, and constraints go out. Memory holds curated items, not a transcript dump: ```sh rdsh context remember "Keep the API compatible" --kind constraint rdsh context distill --session ~/.dsh/sessions///session.v4.jsonl.zstd --apply rdsh context memory --json # active and superseded entries rdsh context forget mem_ab12cd34ef56 ``` `distill` reads user turns only (zstd session logs included) and extracts decisions, constraints, and retractions with deterministic markers, superseding an older overlapping entry instead of guessing. `rdsh context build --require-stable` exits 3 unless the snapshot is provably stable: a file or git state that changed during assembly counts, and so does a git state it cannot read, so a stale or unknown snapshot is never reported as fresh. ### Dependency Graph and Change Impact (`rdsh deps`) ```sh rdsh deps build # incremental index under $DSH_HOME/rdsh-index rdsh deps query engine_score # where a symbol is defined and referenced rdsh deps impact src/context.rs # direct/transitive dependents + affected tests ``` The extractor covers Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, and Go and records imports, definitions, and static call sites per file. Unchanged files (same size and mtime) are reused, so repeated runs stay fast. It is a static approximation: dynamic dispatch, indirect calls, macros, and generated code remain explicitly `unknown` and are reported as unresolved counts rather than guessed, and a missing index means "no information", never "no dependencies". When the index exists, `rdsh context build` and `rdsh context inject` also pull in the graph neighbours of the files their search matched, so a retrieved excerpt arrives with the files it actually depends on. Native execution overhead is ~1 ms per invocation. ## Low-end hosts Default profile: `RDSH_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, then `general.default_profile` in rdsh settings, then local `tui`, else a guided error. Set the saved default with `rdsh settings set general.default_profile web`; an explicit `--profile ` keeps its precedence. rdsh aims to remain useful on modest machines: older x86-64 CPUs, older Linux distributions, and hosts without Node.js installed. - **Faster Node startup.** When rdsh launches dsh, it sets `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` to `~/.cache/rdsh-node-compile-cache`, letting Node reuse compiled code across launches (Node 22.1 or newer; older versions ignore it). An existing `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` value is preserved. Set `RDSH_NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=0`, or use `--passthrough` / `RDSH_PASSTHROUGH=1`, to opt out. - **Broad CPU support.** Prebuilt x86-64 binaries do not require AVX or BMI; the static musl build also runs on systems with older glibc. - **Session token estimates.** `sessions --tokens` reads a decompressed size from the zstd frame header when available. Most streaming frames need the `zstd -dc` fallback. Results are cached under `~/.cache/rdsh/sessions-tokens.json` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` takes precedence); set `RDSH_TOKENS_CACHE=0` to disable the cache. A `?` marks an estimate that could not be read, for example when the zstd CLI is unavailable. - **Bounded parallel work.** Search and session scans use at most eight worker threads. The zstd CLI fallback uses 8 to 32 parallel processes. - **Native commands without Node.** Commands such as `tokens`, `search`, and `sessions` keep working without Node. To delegate conversations, install `@deepseek-ai/dsh` or set `DSH_ORIG_BIN` (or `RDSH_ORIG_BIN`). - **Low-priority updates.** `sync-dsh.sh` updates dsh and rdsh, verifies archive bytes against that registry, and rolls back a failed update candidate. By default it uses the stable release selected by the reviewed repository digest registry; set `RDSH_SYNC_FROM_SOURCE=1` to build from `main` under `nice -n 19` and `ionice -c3` when available. The systemd unit runs at low priority; adjust its `ExecStart` to your checkout. ## Web UI & Dashboard ### Lightweight Local Web UI (`rdsh serve`) A lightweight status and token estimation page running on localhost (default `:38080`, does not conflict with DSH `:3080`): ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve # enable the server feature rdsh serve # launch (bound to localhost, protected with a one-time token) ``` ### Extended Dashboard (`rdsh-dashboard`) Optional Node.js dashboard for project metrics, human-in-the-loop Q&A, and mobile access (requires Node.js 22+): ```sh rdsh-dashboard project --project ``` *On native Windows, the dashboard runs in the system tray and can be opened or stopped from the taskbar (`--no-tray` keeps it in the terminal). See [dashboard/README.md](dashboard/README.md). External agent CLIs (cursor-agent, devin) can be run as supervised jobs: see [docs/AGENT-RUNNERS.md](docs/AGENT-RUNNERS.md).* ## Desktop App (Electron) DeepSeek Harness Desktop is an Electron shell around the complete Web application. It shares `$DSH_HOME` with the CLI but owns a **reserved profile** (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop`) and its own bundled command runtime, so the npm `dsh` CLI cannot manage its plugins. `rdsh desktop` detects all of that and forwards plugin attachment to the app's own command — rdsh never boots or rewrites the profile: ```sh rdsh desktop status # app, command runtime, profile, plugin state (read-only) rdsh desktop install --plugins-dir . # rdsh-settings + default third-party (sound, gitview) rdsh desktop install --plugins-dir . --compute # + the resident compute bridge rdsh desktop install --plugins-dir . --no-sound --no-gitview # skip third-party rdsh desktop verify # exit nonzero when the profile has no rdsh plugin ``` The same is available through the profile installer and the installers: ```sh PROFILE=desktop ./plugins/install.sh # every recommended package, forwarded correctly ./install.sh --desktop # attach the rdsh plugins during installation ``` *Quit the app before attaching plugins, reopen it afterwards. The app's own Plugins page installs the same packages without any command. The Electron runtime itself is never replaced: in-app delegation stays limited to the opt-in, fail-open compute bridge. See [DESKTOP-INTEGRATION.md](docs/DESKTOP-INTEGRATION.md).* Two optional plugins extend the existing Desktop/Web runtime: - [File organization](plugins/rdsh-easy-work/README.md): select a folder, preview extension-based categories, copy after confirmation, and archive the copies to undo. Originals stay in place. Execution currently requires Linux; Windows and macOS support preview only. No AI connection is needed. - [Bounded exploration subagents](plugins/rdsh-subagent-optimizer/README.md): fresh context, bounded concurrency and output, and active duplicate suppression through the native DSH `spawn` provider (0.2.0-rc.2). Use the app's Plugins page to add the corresponding directory, or enable `EASY_WORK=1` / `SUBAGENTS=1` in `plugins/install.sh`. These are opt-in features being prepared for 0.4.0. See the [acceptance evidence](docs/reviews/2026-10-14-easy-work.md). [Desktop SDK and upstream preparation](desktop/README.md) provide a pinned official SDK, an isolated fork home, bundled Rust launcher, and a dedicated rustdsh update channel. Source preparation and SDK transport are tested; signed Desktop installers and update acceptance still require platform builds. ## Using with Smart-DSH [Smart-DSH](https://github.com/hikarioyama/Smart-DSH) (a web-profile plugin bundle) works smoothly alongside rdsh: ```sh rdsh doctor # check dsh version and Smart-DSH bundles rdsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/bundle # add plugins rdsh --profile web # boot web with plugins enabled ``` Ports never collide (DSH Web: `3080`, rdsh serve: `38080`). Ports never collide (dsh web GUI :3080, `rdsh serve` :38080). With `install.sh --as-dsh`, point Smart-DSH helper scripts at `dsh-orig` or export `DSH_PACKAGE_DIR`. ## Web dashboard For the read-only workflow member board in DSH's conversation GUI, use the [verified source-patch preparation tool](plugins/workflow-board/README.md) with an isolated compatible source checkout. It includes the 18-file board/UI projection patch, compatibility diagnostics and fixture tests; building and adopting the patched DSH are separate steps. For bounded MCP resource artifacts and explicit resource-link reads, use the [verified source-patch preparation tool](plugins/mcp-resource-artifacts/README.md) with an isolated checkout at its pinned DSH revision. Resource links are never fetched automatically, binary payloads stay out of model text, and building or adopting the patched DSH are separate steps. ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve # replaces the enabled-extra list rdsh serve # open the URL containing #key=... printed by rdsh (localhost only) ``` | API | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `GET /api/version` | version (requires key) | | `GET /api/doctor` | health check | | `POST /api/tokens` | token estimate for `{"text"}` | | `POST /api/prune` | prune `{"text","max_tokens"}` to budget | | `GET /api/bench?n=3` | startup measurement | | `GET /api/sessions?limit=20` | recent sessions | | `GET /api/skills`, `/api/profiles` | name lists | All APIs require the per-launch key in the `X-RDSH-Token` header (the browser UI reads it from its URL). No CDN is used; the page works offline. `rdsh serve` is the quick local status page. For project metrics, human Q&A, and phone access, use the optional [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md) (needs Node.js 22+): `rdsh-dashboard project --project ` or `rdsh-dashboard harness` for the original Harness Web UI. On native Windows the launcher can live in the tray (right-click Open / Exit, double-click opens; `--no-tray` stays in the terminal). Add `--include-project ` to a project launch to show read-only active, waiting, and needs-attention counts for only the projects explicitly listed at startup. Details stay in each project's dashboard; unreadable projects show their last successful observation time and an unknown state. The original Harness update banner appears right after an update is recorded, every two hours from its update time, and on every full page reload. Dismiss / X or a successful updater check closes the current occurrence; the two-hour schedule continues. Unchanged release checks do not record a new update. Switching projects keeps it closed until the next slot, and close events reach other GUI ports of the same OS user. Activating new code needs one normal GUI restart/reload; see [browser verification](docs/evidence/update-notice-repeat/README.md). rdsh bundles only Smart-DSH's phone-width layout, as [`plugins/rdsh-mobile-ui`](plugins/rdsh-mobile-ui/README.md) (MIT, adapted from Smart-DSH): at 767px and below the chat and composer use the full width and the logo opens the session list in one tap. Smart-DSH's notifications, Esc-to-stop, task hub and shared-HMR workaround stay upstream — install the upstream bundle when you want those. ## Benchmarks Measurements conducted on Linux x86_64: | Benchmark | rdsh | Upstream dsh / Baseline | Improvement | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `--version` startup | **~0.90 ms** | ~88 ms | **~98x faster** | | `--version` peak RSS | **~2.9 MB** | ~66 MB | **~1/23 memory** | | Hook-equivalent memory | **~2.7 MB** | ~45 MB (Node equivalent) | **~1/16 memory** | | Code search (`search`) | **~17 ms** | ~41 ms | **~2.4x faster** | | Token estimate (`tokens`) | **~12 ms** | ~35 ms | **~2.9x faster** | | Session list (`sessions --tokens`) | **~0.41 s** | ~1.65 s | **~4.0x faster** | | Binary size | **~1.97 MB** (single binary) | ~508 MB (Node tree) | **Ultra compact** | *Reproduce with `rdsh bench --n 5`. See [docs/BENCHMARKS.md](docs/BENCHMARKS.md) for detailed test setups and measurements.* ## Safety Design 1. **Upstream Fidelity**: Never reimplements conversation loops or agent logic; delegates directly to upstream `dsh`. 2. **Non-Destructive**: Read operations (tokens, search, session listing, compacting) never modify source file

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # rdsh-compute (opt-in PoC) DSH Web → 常駐 `rdsh compute` → 純粋計算の橋渡しです。既定は OFF。 - 有効化: `RDSH_COMPUTE=1`（それ以外は元の Node 実装を使います） - 対象は純粋な文字列計算のみ（`tokens.estimate` / `tokens.prune`） - セッション・認証・モデル呼び出しは扱いません - 失敗・タイムアウト（既定 5s）・版不一致は元の処理にフォールバック - 1 MiB 超は送りません。大きな履歴は呼び出し側で分割します 判定は `docs/WEB-COMPUTE.md` の `T_total` 式で行います。 単体が速いだけでは採用しません。 # rdsh — a fast, safe Rust launcher for `dsh` [![ci](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![dashboard](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml) [![docs](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.85%2B-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [Japanese version](README.ja.md) An independent community project; not an official DeepSeek or DeepSeek Harness project. `rdsh` is a fast, safe launcher for [DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It ports frequently used CLI operations (token calculation, code search, session management) to native Rust, while delegating conversation workflows and model execution transparently to upstream `dsh`. All existing arguments and options continue to work as-is. ## Why rdsh? - ⚡ **Sub-millisecond startup & low memory**: `--version` launches in ~0.90 ms with ~2.9 MB peak memory, compared to ~88 ms and ~66 MB for Node.js-based `dsh`. - 🔄 **100% Drop-in Compatible**: Subcommands that are not rdsh-native are passed straight to upstream `dsh`. Existing scripts and workflows keep running unchanged. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and run health diagnostics (`rdsh doctor`) instantly without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and `rdsh_inspect` can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and inspect local prerequisites (`rdsh doctor --json`) without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and agent tools can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. ## Table of Contents - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Usage](#usage) - [Running with `dsh` Compatibility](#running-with-dsh-compatibility) - [Fast Native Commands](#fast-native-commands) - [Credential sharing with rdsh auth](#credential-sharing-with-rdsh-auth) - [Agent Tool Isolation](#agent-tool-isolation) - [Hook Guard](#hook-guard-rdsh-guard) - [Context Injection](#context-injection-rdsh-context) - [Dependency Graph and Change Impact](#dependency-graph-and-change-impact-rdsh-deps) - [Web UI & Dashboard](#web-ui--dashboard) - [Using with Smart-DSH](#using-with-smart-dsh) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Safety Design](#safety-design) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Community](#community) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Quick Start Already using **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, OpenCode or Gemini CLI**? [Connect the project dashboard through MCP](docs/MCP-CLIENTS.md) to share tasks, questions and structured UI while keeping your current coding agent. This entry point requires Node.js 22+; DSH and Rust are optional. ### 1. Install (Prebuilt Binary) **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --from-release ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell $f = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'rdsh-install.ps1' Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile $f -UseBasicParsing & $f -FromRelease ``` ### 2. Verify & Setup ```sh rdsh --version && rdsh doctor # verify install and original dsh rdsh setup # interactive setup (or rdsh setup --web for browser UI) ``` *Note: If you have an existing login from Codex CLI (ChatGPT OAuth) or opencode, import it with `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex`.* ### 3. Start a Conversation ```sh rdsh tui # start with TUI profile # or rdsh --profile web # start with Web profile ``` ## Requirements | Item | Detail | | --- | --- | | OS | Linux, macOS, WSL, Windows (native) | | DSH runtime | Required for conversations and agent runs (native tools and diagnostics run standalone) | | Rust | 1.85+ (only needed when building from source; prebuilt binaries require no Rust) | | Optional | Node.js 22+ for the [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md); SearXNG for `search-web` | ## Installation ### Building from Source & Advanced Options **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh ./install.sh # build + install to ~/.local/bin/rdsh ./install.sh --as-dsh # also replace `dsh` command (original backed up as dsh-orig) ./install.sh --restore # undo the replacement ./install.sh --prefix=DIR # custom install directory (default: ~/.local/bin) ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh .\install.ps1 # build + install to %LOCALAPPDATA%\rdsh\bin .\install.ps1 -AsDsh # also replace `dsh` command .\install.ps1 -Restore # undo the replacement .\install.ps1 -Wsl # also install inside WSL via install.sh ``` | OS | Script | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./install.sh` | Needs `cargo` or `curl` (guided via rustup if missing). | | WSL | `./install.sh` inside distro | Auto-detects WSL. `install.ps1 -Wsl` installs in both environments. | | Windows (native) | `.\install.ps1` | Needs Rust and MSVC build tools (`winget install Rustlang.Rustup`). | ## Usage ### Running with `dsh` Compatibility Run any standard `dsh` command unchanged: ```sh rdsh tui # equivalent to: dsh --profile tui rdsh --profile web --patch x.yml # launch with configuration overlay rdsh --dry-run tui -- --resume id # print what would be executed ``` When installed with `./install.sh --as-dsh`, typing `dsh` automatically uses the fast `rdsh` launcher. ### Fast Native Commands Native tools execute in Rust without starting Node.js: ```sh rdsh tokens ./README.md # estimate token count (~4 chars = 1 tok, CJK = 1 tok each) echo "..." | rdsh prune --max-tokens 4000 # prune context within a token budget rdsh search TODO --dir . --max 100 # fast parallel text search rdsh sessions --limit 20 --tokens # list sessions and unpacked token estimates rdsh compact ./s.jsonl # compact session JSONL (source remains untouched) rdsh doctor # check health of dsh, environment, and paths rdsh doctor --json # read-only metadata for scripts; no DSH/Node launch rdsh profiles / rdsh skills # list available profiles and skills rdsh desktop status # detect the DeepSeek Harness Desktop app and profile rdsh bench --n 5 # benchmark startup speed between rdsh and dsh ``` On Windows, compressed session histories are not opened until rdsh can reject parent junctions safely; `sessions --tokens` may omit those histories and its totals are inexact. ### Credential sharing with rdsh auth External credentials are inventoried without showing their values. Nothing is copied until you select a source and credential. OAuth copies use DSH's existing version-1 store at $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; API keys use its named refs. The selection policy contains only identifiers at $DSH_HOME/rdsh-auth-sharing.json. ```sh rdsh auth # sources, destinations, selection and undo steps rdsh auth --json # secret-free machine-readable inventory rdsh --dry-run auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # preview; writes no files rdsh auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # share only Codex OAuth rdsh auth --select opencode:openai-codex --import # OpenCode openai maps to openai-codex rdsh auth --select codex:OPENAI_API_KEY --import # separate opt-in for Codex's API key rdsh auth --select env:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY --import # explicitly persist this environment key rdsh auth --unselect codex:openai-codex # stop future copies; retain the existing copy rdsh setup # sync selected credentials, then guide setup rdsh setup --web # inventory, selection commands and explicit key save ``` For a one-time import, use `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex --source codex` or `rdsh auth --import --ref OPENAI_API_KEY --source codex`. These filters do not save or extend future-copy consent; `--select`/`--unselect` are separate persistent policy changes. Repeat --select/--unselect for individual credentials. Selecting enables future imports from that CLI/provider, including boot, dump-config, plugin, raw dsh delegation and setup. --import immediately applies the selection. Even a newer grant in another, unselected CLI cannot be chosen. Newer DSH grants and existing API-key refs/records remain in place. Other entries, comments and line endings are preserved. Unix credential and policy files use mode 0600. The inventory checks Codex's ~/.codex/auth.json and OpenCode's $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json (or its platform default data directory), plus the legacy ~/.config/opencode/auth.json fallback. Selectors for OpenCode use DSH provider IDs; opencode:openai-codex is the selector for its openai login. Environment-key persistence supports DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. These are format/presence checks, not live authentication tests. An environment variable already supplied to rdsh is inherited by DSH and its child processes without rdsh writing a file. The JSON inventory marks this route persistent=false, lists its destination and explains how to stop/revoke it. Using the reference does not opt in to storing it. setup --yes no longer saves every environment key; choose each one with auth --select env:NAME --import. Interactive setup and the web form still allow an explicit, individual key save. **Scope and undo:** saved entries are available to every DSH profile using the same DSH_HOME. Unselect stops future rdsh imports; it does not delete a saved copy or invalidate a running process. Stop DSH and remove the named record/ref from the credential store to stop using a saved copy. To invalidate the credential itself, revoke the OAuth grant or rotate the API key at its provider. That may also disconnect the source CLI. This controls rdsh copying, not DSH's own refreshes, inherited environment access or an OS sandbox. **Migration:** existing DSH credentials are retained. A missing policy selects nothing, including for legacy auth --import. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=1 does not restore the old import-all behavior. Inventory and preview first, then choose the sources you need. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=0 disables automatic imports while keeping the selection; an explicit auth --import still works. Invalid/unreadable policies fail closed instead of falling back to legacy sync. Consent changes and rdsh credential writes share a lock, so a completed unselect cannot be bypassed by a queued rdsh import using an earlier policy. After a crashed writer, check that no rdsh auth/setup writer is active before removing $DSH_HOME/.rdsh-auth-sharing.lock; the launcher skips copying while it is locked. setup --web issues a new local access key at startup in its #key=... URL. The tab retains that key; status reads, key saves and closing require it. Keep the startup URL private. The page shows copy destinations and separate unselect, saved-copy removal and provider revocation steps before a key save. ### Optional extras (off by default) Server-type features stay off until enabled, so a plain install remains a fast dsh: ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve,search-web rdsh settings get extras.enable ``` | Extra | Command | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `serve` | `rdsh serve` (default :38080) | Local status page, localhost only, per-launch key. | | `search-web` | `rdsh search-web "query" --limit 5` | Needs SearXNG. | To connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that dsh does not ship (HAI, Sarashina, a home llama.cpp / vLLM / LM Studio / Ollama server), add it as a profile route: ```sh rdsh provider add hai --model deepseek-v4-flash # key from HAI_API_KEY or --key-stdin rdsh provider add sarashina # key from SARASHINA_API_KEY; mini and nano built in rdsh provider add local-openai --base-url http://host:8080/v1 --discover --no-key rdsh provider list # presets, per-profile route and key status ``` Details: [docs/PROVIDERS.md](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Model Catalog (`rdsh models`) DeepSeek Harness answers "which models can this provider serve?" from the catalog bundled in its `@earendil-works/pi-ai` dependency, which is generated when that package is published. Anything a provider changes afterwards is absent from the picker until that dependency is upgraded — and a profile that lists `models:` explicitly replaces the bundled catalog for the route anyway. `rdsh models` reads the provider's own catalog (the local Codex CLI, or Kimi Code's `/v1/models` endpoint with the profile's API key) and folds it into the profile: ```sh rdsh models # read-only: missing ids and stale names rdsh models --provider kimi-coding # one provider only rdsh models sync # add missing entries, refresh stale names rdsh models sync --profile web --dry-run # preview one profile ``` Nothing is deleted, an existing entry keeps every other byte (a name the provider's current one already contains is left as written), and a profile the command does not recognize is refused instead of rewritten. The harness picks the changes up on the next config reload or restart. ### Agent Tool Isolation Delegated agent tools keep normal file access by default: the model reads and writes the project like any other tool. `--share-file` isolates **`rdsh_inspect` only**. On Linux (with bubblewrap and prlimit) that tool sees just the files you explicitly share: ```sh rdsh --share-file README.md --share-file src/main.rs --profile tui ``` From `rdsh_inspect`, only the shared files are mounted read-only, host files stay out of reach and the sandbox has no network. Turn the same boundary on for every run with `rdsh features on agent_tool_sandbox` (off again with `rdsh features off agent_tool_sandbox`, or force it with `RDSH_SECURITY=1`). Other DSH tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `run_code`, ...) are **not** isolated and follow upstream DSH permissions and approvals. Startup prints `[rdsh security] rdsh_inspect is isolated; other DSH tools use upstream permissions`. ### Hook Guard (`rdsh guard`) Integrates with DSH `hooks.json` to inspect and block dangerous commands before execution: ```sh echo "$input" | rdsh guard --deny "rm -rf /*" --deny "*token*" ``` For an opt-in structured check of supported file tools, pass a policy file. This example permits `Read` only under one existing project directory: ```json { "schema": 1, "rules": [ { "id": "project-read", "tool": "Read", "access": "read", "roots": ["/absolute/project/path"] } ] } ``` ```sh echo "$hook_json" | rdsh guard --policy-file ./hook-policy.json --json ``` The structured classifier supports the `Read`, `Write`, and `Edit` file-path schemas. It canonicalizes the working directory and target, checks the selected tool and read/write scope against existing policy roots, and reports `allow`, `deny`, or `unknown` with a non-sensitive reason. In JSON mode an `allow` is classification only and omits `decision`; the host still owns permission and approval. Unknown tools, shell commands, malformed input, and unsupported tool arguments fail closed. Shell parsing and network destinations are not implemented. Path checks are advisory and can race with later filesystem changes; this hook is not an OS sandbox. Use the actual execution sandbox for enforcement. ```json { "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "rdsh guard --deny \"rm -rf /*\"" }] } ] } } ``` ### Context Injection (`rdsh context`) `rdsh context inject` assembles this turn's context — goal, constraints, decisions, working set, git state, retrieved code, and curated memory — and emits it in the DSH `UserPromptSubmit` hook contract, so the model sees it without any copy-paste: ```sh rdsh features on context_engine # the engine is opt-in rdsh context hook install # merges $DSH_HOME/hooks.json (idempotent) rdsh context hook status --json ``` The hook is fail-open: it never blocks a prompt and always exits 0. Only an unreadable settings document or an unparseable payload inject nothing at all; a corrupt index or a missed deadline drops just what depends on them — the graph or the code search — and still injects goal, constraints, and memory. Injection has its own budget (`context.inject_budget`, default 1200 tokens) and deadline (`context.inject_deadline_ms`, default 1200 ms); once the deadline passes the code search is skipped and only memory, goal, and constraints go out. Memory holds curated items, not a transcript dump: ```sh rdsh context remember "Keep the API compatible" --kind constraint rdsh context distill --session ~/.dsh/sessions///session.v4.jsonl.zstd --apply rdsh context memory --json # active and superseded entries rdsh context forget mem_ab12cd34ef56 ``` `distill` reads user turns only (zstd session logs included) and extracts decisions, constraints, and retractions with deterministic markers, superseding an older overlapping entry instead of guessing. `rdsh context build --require-stable` exits 3 unless the snapshot is provably stable: a file or git state that changed during assembly counts, and so does a git state it cannot read, so a stale or unknown snapshot is never reported as fresh. ### Dependency Graph and Change Impact (`rdsh deps`) ```sh rdsh deps build # incremental index under $DSH_HOME/rdsh-index rdsh deps query engine_score # where a symbol is defined and referenced rdsh deps impact src/context.rs # direct/transitive dependents + affected tests ``` The extractor covers Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, and Go and records imports, definitions, and static call sites per file. Unchanged files (same size and mtime) are reused, so repeated runs stay fast. It is a static approximation: dynamic dispatch, indirect calls, macros, and generated code remain explicitly `unknown` and are reported as unresolved counts rather than guessed, and a missing index means "no information", never "no dependencies". When the index exists, `rdsh context build` and `rdsh context inject` also pull in the graph neighbours of the files their search matched, so a retrieved excerpt arrives with the files it actually depends on. Native execution overhead is ~1 ms per invocation. ## Low-end hosts Default profile: `RDSH_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, then `general.default_profile` in rdsh settings, then local `tui`, else a guided error. Set the saved default with `rdsh settings set general.default_profile web`; an explicit `--profile ` keeps its precedence. rdsh aims to remain useful on modest machines: older x86-64 CPUs, older Linux distributions, and hosts without Node.js installed. - **Faster Node startup.** When rdsh launches dsh, it sets `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` to `~/.cache/rdsh-node-compile-cache`, letting Node reuse compiled code across launches (Node 22.1 or newer; older versions ignore it). An existing `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` value is preserved. Set `RDSH_NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=0`, or use `--passthrough` / `RDSH_PASSTHROUGH=1`, to opt out. - **Broad CPU support.** Prebuilt x86-64 binaries do not require AVX or BMI; the static musl build also runs on systems with older glibc. - **Session token estimates.** `sessions --tokens` reads a decompressed size from the zstd frame header when available. Most streaming frames need the `zstd -dc` fallback. Results are cached under `~/.cache/rdsh/sessions-tokens.json` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` takes precedence); set `RDSH_TOKENS_CACHE=0` to disable the cache. A `?` marks an estimate that could not be read, for example when the zstd CLI is unavailable. - **Bounded parallel work.** Search and session scans use at most eight worker threads. The zstd CLI fallback uses 8 to 32 parallel processes. - **Native commands without Node.** Commands such as `tokens`, `search`, and `sessions` keep working without Node. To delegate conversations, install `@deepseek-ai/dsh` or set `DSH_ORIG_BIN` (or `RDSH_ORIG_BIN`). - **Low-priority updates.** `sync-dsh.sh` updates dsh and rdsh, verifies archive bytes against that registry, and rolls back a failed update candidate. By default it uses the stable release selected by the reviewed repository digest registry; set `RDSH_SYNC_FROM_SOURCE=1` to build from `main` under `nice -n 19` and `ionice -c3` when available. The systemd unit runs at low priority; adjust its `ExecStart` to your checkout. ## Web UI & Dashboard ### Lightweight Local Web UI (`rdsh serve`) A lightweight status and token estimation page running on localhost (default `:38080`, does not conflict with DSH `:3080`): ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve # enable the server feature rdsh serve # launch (bound to localhost, protected with a one-time token) ``` ### Extended Dashboard (`rdsh-dashboard`) Optional Node.js dashboard for project metrics, human-in-the-loop Q&A, and mobile access (requires Node.js 22+): ```sh rdsh-dashboard project --project ``` *On native Windows, the dashboard runs in the system tray and can be opened or stopped from the taskbar (`--no-tray` keeps it in the terminal). See [dashboard/README.md](dashboard/README.md). External agent CLIs (cursor-agent, devin) can be run as supervised jobs: see [docs/AGENT-RUNNERS.md](docs/AGENT-RUNNERS.md).* ## Desktop App (Electron) DeepSeek Harness Desktop is an Electron shell around the complete Web application. It shares `$DSH_HOME` with the CLI but owns a **reserved profile** (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop`) and its own bundled command runtime, so the npm `dsh` CLI cannot manage its plugins. `rdsh desktop` detects all of that and forwards plugin attachment to the app's own command — rdsh never boots or rewrites the profile: ```sh rdsh desktop status # app, command runtime, profile, plugin state (read-only) rdsh desktop install --plugins-dir . # rdsh-settings + default third-party (sound, gitview) rdsh desktop install --plugins-dir . --compute # + the resident compute bridge rdsh desktop install --plugins-dir . --no-sound --no-gitview # skip third-party rdsh desktop verify # exit nonzero when the profile has no rdsh plugin ``` The same is available through the profile installer and the installers: ```sh PROFILE=desktop ./plugins/install.sh # every recommended package, forwarded correctly ./install.sh --desktop # attach the rdsh plugins during installation ``` *Quit the app before attaching plugins, reopen it afterwards. The app's own Plugins page installs the same packages without any command. The Electron runtime itself is never replaced: in-app delegation stays limited to the opt-in, fail-open compute bridge. See [DESKTOP-INTEGRATION.md](docs/DESKTOP-INTEGRATION.md).* Two optional plugins extend the existing Desktop/Web runtime: - [File organization](plugins/rdsh-easy-work/README.md): select a folder, preview extension-based categories, copy after confirmation, and archive the copies to undo. Originals stay in place. Execution currently requires Linux; Windows and macOS support preview only. No AI connection is needed. - [Bounded exploration subagents](plugins/rdsh-subagent-optimizer/README.md): fresh context, bounded concurrency and output, and active duplicate suppression through the native DSH `spawn` provider (0.2.0-rc.2). Use the app's Plugins page to add the corresponding directory, or enable `EASY_WORK=1` / `SUBAGENTS=1` in `plugins/install.sh`. These are opt-in features being prepared for 0.4.0. See the [acceptance evidence](docs/reviews/2026-10-14-easy-work.md). [Desktop SDK and upstream preparation](desktop/README.md) provide a pinned official SDK, an isolated fork home, bundled Rust launcher, and a dedicated rustdsh update channel. Source preparation and SDK transport are tested; signed Desktop installers and update acceptance still require platform builds. ## Using with Smart-DSH [Smart-DSH](https://github.com/hikarioyama/Smart-DSH) (a web-profile plugin bundle) works smoothly alongside rdsh: ```sh rdsh doctor # check dsh version and Smart-DSH bundles rdsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/bundle # add plugins rdsh --profile web # boot web with plugins enabled ``` Ports never collide (DSH Web: `3080`, rdsh serve: `38080`). Ports never collide (dsh web GUI :3080, `rdsh serve` :38080). With `install.sh --as-dsh`, point Smart-DSH helper scripts at `dsh-orig` or export `DSH_PACKAGE_DIR`. ## Web dashboard For the read-only workflow member board in DSH's conversation GUI, use the [verified source-patch preparation tool](plugins/workflow-board/README.md) with an isolated compatible source checkout. It includes the 18-file board/UI projection patch, compatibility diagnostics and fixture tests; building and adopting the patched DSH are separate steps. For bounded MCP resource artifacts and explicit resource-link reads, use the [verified source-patch preparation tool](plugins/mcp-resource-artifacts/README.md) with an isolated checkout at its pinned DSH revision. Resource links are never fetched automatically, binary payloads stay out of model text, and building or adopting the patched DSH are separate steps. ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve # replaces the enabled-extra list rdsh serve # open the URL containing #key=... printed by rdsh (localhost only) ``` | API | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `GET /api/version` | version (requires key) | | `GET /api/doctor` | health check | | `POST /api/tokens` | token estimate for `{"text"}` | | `POST /api/prune` | prune `{"text","max_tokens"}` to budget | | `GET /api/bench?n=3` | startup measurement | | `GET /api/sessions?limit=20` | recent sessions | | `GET /api/skills`, `/api/profiles` | name lists | All APIs require the per-launch key in the `X-RDSH-Token` header (the browser UI reads it from its URL). No CDN is used; the page works offline. `rdsh serve` is the quick local status page. For project metrics, human Q&A, and phone access, use the optional [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md) (needs Node.js 22+): `rdsh-dashboard project --project ` or `rdsh-dashboard harness` for the original Harness Web UI. On native Windows the launcher can live in the tray (right-click Open / Exit, double-click opens; `--no-tray` stays in the terminal). Add `--include-project ` to a project launch to show read-only active, waiting, and needs-attention counts for only the projects explicitly listed at startup. Details stay in each project's dashboard; unreadable projects show their last successful observation time and an unknown state. The original Harness update banner appears right after an update is recorded, every two hours from its update time, and on every full page reload. Dismiss / X or a successful updater check closes the current occurrence; the two-hour schedule continues. Unchanged release checks do not record a new update. Switching projects keeps it closed until the next slot, and close events reach other GUI ports of the same OS user. Activating new code needs one normal GUI restart/reload; see [browser verification](docs/evidence/update-notice-repeat/README.md). rdsh bundles only Smart-DSH's phone-width layout, as [`plugins/rdsh-mobile-ui`](plugins/rdsh-mobile-ui/README.md) (MIT, adapted from Smart-DSH): at 767px and below the chat and composer use the full width and the logo opens the session list in one tap. Smart-DSH's notifications, Esc-to-stop, task hub and shared-HMR workaround stay upstream — install the upstream bundle when you want those. ## Benchmarks Measurements conducted on Linux x86_64: | Benchmark | rdsh | Upstream dsh / Baseline | Improvement | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `--version` startup | **~0.90 ms** | ~88 ms | **~98x faster** | | `--version` peak RSS | **~2.9 MB** | ~66 MB | **~1/23 memory** | | Hook-equivalent memory | **~2.7 MB** | ~45 MB (Node equivalent) | **~1/16 memory** | | Code search (`search`) | **~17 ms** | ~41 ms | **~2.4x faster** | | Token estimate (`tokens`) | **~12 ms** | ~35 ms | **~2.9x faster** | | Session list (`sessions --tokens`) | **~0.41 s** | ~1.65 s | **~4.0x faster** | | Binary size | **~1.97 MB** (single binary) | ~508 MB (Node tree) | **Ultra compact** | *Reproduce with `rdsh bench --n 5`
