evidence.readmeExcerpt: # rdsh official SDK bridge CursorとAntigravityの公式SDKをDSHのモデルプロバイダーとして使い、会話ループ・ツール実行・承認をrdsh/DSHに維持する、任意導入のプラグインです。Devinは承認必須の `devin_cli` ツールとして登録します。 ## 動作 SDKには毎回、DSHの履歴とツールの説明をテキストとして渡します。各SDKは独立した空の一時ワークスペースで、操作ツール・MCP・subagent・ambient設定を無効化し、1つのJSON回答を返します。SDK自体の内部ランタイムは存在しますが、DSHの会話ループやツール実行を委譲しません。 一時ワークスペースとSDKの保存領域は、通常終了時に加え、タイムアウト・キャンセル・出力上限による強制終了時も子プロセスの終了を待って削除します。削除に失敗した場合はエラーを返します。 JSON変換層は宣言したツール名・引数のJSON Schema・呼出しIDの重複・追加フィールドを検証します。不正JSONだけ最大1回修正を要求し、認証・通信失敗を別経路への切替で隠しません。回答は検証完了後にDSHへ返すため、モデルの部分出力は配信しません。現在はテキスト入力のみ対応します。 `temperature`・`maxTokens`・`stop` の生成制御は未対応です。指定された場合は、認証解決やSDK生成を始める前に `UNSUPPORTED_GENERATION_OPTION` で拒否します。 `devin_cli` はDSHの承認後に、現在のセッションのワークスペース内でインストール済みCLIを起動します。CLIの信頼・権限設定を保持し、shellを介さず、タイムアウト・キャンセル・出力量制限を適用します。Devin内部のエージェントループと操作はDevinが所有するため、DSHは委譲全体を承認します。既定実行ファイルは `~/.local/bin/devin` です。 ## 導入 DSHの `llm`・`tools`・`credentials` サービスが必要です。DSH 0.2.0-rc.2、Node.js 25で実動確認しました。Antigravity SDKはPython 3.10以上を要求します。 リポジトリのルートから実行します。 ```sh npm ci --prefix plugins/rdsh-direct-models python3 -m venv plugins/rdsh-direct-models/.venv plugins/rdsh-direct-models/.venv/bin/pip install -r plugins/rdsh-direct-models/requirements.txt export RDSH_AGY_PYTHON="$PWD/plugins/rdsh-direct-models/.venv/bin/python" dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD/plugins/rdsh-direct-models" rdsh web ``` `RDSH_AGY_PYTHON` は実際にDSHを起動する環境に設定してください。未指定ならプラグイン直下の `.venv/bin/python` を使います。インストール先に仮想環境を複製する必要はありません。別プロフィールへ導入する場合は `--profile web` を変更してください。Rustランチャーや既存プロフィールの既定モデルは変更しません。 GUIのモデル一覧で `Cursor (official SDK, rdsh tools)` または `Antigravity (official SDK, rdsh tools)` を選択します。DSHの構成へ直接挿入する場合は、次のpatchも使用できます。 ```yaml - insert: - id: rdsh-direct-models name: /absolute/path/to/rustdsh/plugins/rdsh-direct-models/index.mjs - id: agent-default-model config: provider: cursor-sdk model: composer-2.5 ``` Antigravityの確認済み組合せは `provider: agy-sdk` / `model: gemini-3.8-flash` です。Cursorは公式SDKのモデル一覧を取得します。Antigravityの一覧はインストール済みSDKの既定モデルを表示するため、利用権限の確認は実際の生成時に行います。 ## 認証 - Cursor: `CURSOR_API_KEY` または公式SDKが管理する `~/.cursor/sdk/auth.json`。キーの発行・保存はこのプラグインでは行いません。 - Antigravity: 呼出しごとにDSH credential serviceの `GEMINI_API_KEY`、`GOOGLE_API_KEY` を解決し、SDK子プロセスの環境へ渡します。環境の同名キー、`GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI` / `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_ENTERPRISE`、`GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`、`GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`、`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` も使用できます。接続設定の `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY`（小文字名も可）、`SSL_CERT_FILE` / `SSL_CERT_DIR` も保持します。子プロセスへはこれらと必要なOS実行環境だけを渡し、他のプロバイダーのキーやコード注入用の環境設定、TLS秘密の記録設定を継承しません。Antigravity CLIのOAuthやサブスクリプションを引き継ぐ経路ではありません。 - Devin: CLI自身の既存認証とワークスペース信頼設定を使用します。追加の信頼や権限を自動付与しません。 Windowsではproxy名の大小文字を同一視し、呼出し側の明示設定を優先します。同じ入力に大小両名がある場合は、大文字名の文字列値（空文字を含む）を優先します。Unixでは両名を保持し、優先順位はSDK側のtransportに従います。 キーをpromptや設定例に埋め込まないでください。SDK診断は秘密を含む可能性があるため破棄し、失敗分類だけを返します。Devin出力は既知の秘密とAPIキー形式をマスクしますが、任意の機密情報を完全に除去する仕組みではありません。 ## 検証 DSHを通常の `~/.local/lib/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh` へ導入した環境で、次を実行します。 ```sh npm test --prefix plugins/rdsh-direct-models python3 -I -B plugins/rdsh-direct-models/agy-sdk.test.py node plugins/rdsh-direct-models/sdk-runtime-smoke.mjs ``` Nodeの66テストとPythonの4テストでJSON境界、SDK能力の無効化、タイムアウト、キャンセル、出力上限、秘密の切断境界、ワークスペース制限、子環境の制限と接続設定の保持、Windowsでの大小文字にまたがるproxy上書き、生成制御の拒否、Enterprise認証判定、強制終了後の一時領域削除を確認します。実DSH ToolRuntime/Cordisを使い、不正引数の遮断、承認拒否、承認後のファイル読取、結果の履歴反映、Devin拒否時の非起動も検証します。通常テストは外部APIやCLIを呼びません。 実Devinを検証する場合は、CLIで信頼済みの検証専用フォルダーを指定してください。通常の信頼設定を迂回しません。検証fixture内の承認サービスは、固定の無害な確認要求1件だけを許可し、本番の承認設定を変更しません。 ```sh node plugins/rdsh-direct-models/sdk-runtime-smoke.mjs --live-devin --workspace /absolute/path/to/trusted-smoke-workspace ``` 2026-10-15の実確認: Cursor `composer-2.5` とAntigravity `gemini-3.8-flash` の生成、DSH経由でpromptに含めないランダムnonceファイルを読み取った後の継続回答、両方のGUI生成に成功しました。Devinは実ToolRuntimeから応答マーカーの生成と終了コード0を確認しました。認証・課金・モデルの利用可否は各アカウントに依存します。テスト結果に個人の認証情報やホーム設定は含めません。 # rdsh — a fast, safe Rust launcher for `dsh` [![ci](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![dashboard](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml) [![docs](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.85%2B-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [Japanese version](README.ja.md) An independent community project; not an official DeepSeek or DeepSeek Harness project. `rdsh` is a fast, safe launcher for [DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It ports frequently used CLI operations (token calculation, code search, session management) to native Rust, while delegating conversation workflows and model execution transparently to upstream `dsh`. All existing arguments and options continue to work as-is. ## Why rdsh? - ⚡ **Sub-millisecond startup & low memory**: `--version` launches in ~0.90 ms with ~2.9 MB peak memory, compared to ~88 ms and ~66 MB for Node.js-based `dsh`. - 🔄 **100% Drop-in Compatible**: Subcommands that are not rdsh-native are passed straight to upstream `dsh`. Existing scripts and workflows keep running unchanged. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and run health diagnostics (`rdsh doctor`) instantly without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and `rdsh_inspect` can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and inspect local prerequisites (`rdsh doctor --json`) without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and agent tools can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. ## Table of Contents - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Usage](#usage) - [Running with `dsh` Compatibility](#running-with-dsh-compatibility) - [Fast Native Commands](#fast-native-commands) - [Credential sharing with rdsh auth](#credential-sharing-with-rdsh-auth) - [Agent Tool Isolation](#agent-tool-isolation) - [Hook Guard](#hook-guard-rdsh-guard) - [Context Injection](#context-injection-rdsh-context) - [Dependency Graph and Change Impact](#dependency-graph-and-change-impact-rdsh-deps) - [Web UI & Dashboard](#web-ui--dashboard) - [Using with Smart-DSH](#using-with-smart-dsh) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Safety Design](#safety-design) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Community](#community) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Quick Start Already using **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, OpenCode or Gemini CLI**? [Connect the project dashboard through MCP](docs/MCP-CLIENTS.md) to share tasks, questions and structured UI while keeping your current coding agent. This entry point requires Node.js 22+; DSH and Rust are optional. ### 1. Install (Prebuilt Binary) **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --from-release ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell $f = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'rdsh-install.ps1' Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile $f -UseBasicParsing & $f -FromRelease ``` ### 2. Verify & Setup ```sh rdsh --version && rdsh doctor # verify install and original dsh rdsh setup # interactive setup (or rdsh setup --web for browser UI) ``` *Note: If you have an existing login from Codex CLI (ChatGPT OAuth) or opencode, import it with `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex`.* ### 3. Start a Conversation ```sh rdsh tui # start with TUI profile # or rdsh --profile web # start with Web profile ``` ## Requirements | Item | Detail | | --- | --- | | OS | Linux, macOS, WSL, Windows (native) | | DSH runtime | Required for conversations and agent runs (native tools and diagnostics run standalone) | | Rust | 1.85+ (only needed when building from source; prebuilt binaries require no Rust) | | Optional | Node.js 22+ for the [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md); SearXNG for `search-web` | ## Installation ### Building from Source & Advanced Options **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh ./install.sh # build + install to ~/.local/bin/rdsh ./install.sh --as-dsh # also replace `dsh` command (original backed up as dsh-orig) ./install.sh --restore # undo the replacement ./install.sh --prefix=DIR # custom install directory (default: ~/.local/bin) ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh .\install.ps1 # build + install to %LOCALAPPDATA%\rdsh\bin .\install.ps1 -AsDsh # also replace `dsh` command .\install.ps1 -Restore # undo the replacement .\install.ps1 -Wsl # also install inside WSL via install.sh ``` | OS | Script | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./install.sh` | Needs `cargo` or `curl` (guided via rustup if missing). | | WSL | `./install.sh` inside distro | Auto-detects WSL. `install.ps1 -Wsl` installs in both environments. | | Windows (native) | `.\install.ps1` | Needs Rust and MSVC build tools (`winget install Rustlang.Rustup`). | ## Usage ### Running with `dsh` Compatibility Run any standard `dsh` command unchanged: ```sh rdsh tui # equivalent to: dsh --profile tui rdsh --profile web --patch x.yml # launch with configuration overlay rdsh --dry-run tui -- --resume id # print what would be executed ``` When installed with `./install.sh --as-dsh`, typing `dsh` automatically uses the fast `rdsh` launcher. ### Fast Native Commands Native tools execute in Rust without starting Node.js: ```sh rdsh tokens ./README.md # estimate token count (~4 chars = 1 tok, CJK = 1 tok each) echo "..." | rdsh prune --max-tokens 4000 # prune context within a token budget rdsh search TODO --dir . --max 100 # fast parallel text search rdsh sessions --limit 20 --tokens # list sessions and unpacked token estimates rdsh compact ./s.jsonl # compact session JSONL (source remains untouched) rdsh doctor # check health of dsh, environment, and paths rdsh doctor --json # read-only metadata for scripts; no DSH/Node launch rdsh profiles / rdsh skills # list available profiles and skills rdsh desktop status # detect the DeepSeek Harness Desktop app and profile rdsh bench --n 5 # benchmark startup speed between rdsh and dsh ``` On Windows, compressed session histories are not opened until rdsh can reject parent junctions safely; `sessions --tokens` may omit those histories and its totals are inexact. ### Credential sharing with rdsh auth External credentials are inventoried without showing their values. Nothing is copied until you select a source and credential. OAuth copies use DSH's existing version-1 store at $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; API keys use its named refs. The selection policy contains only identifiers at $DSH_HOME/rdsh-auth-sharing.json. ```sh rdsh auth # sources, destinations, selection and undo steps rdsh auth --json # secret-free machine-readable inventory rdsh --dry-run auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # preview; writes no files rdsh auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # share only Codex OAuth rdsh auth --select opencode:openai-codex --import # OpenCode openai maps to openai-codex rdsh auth --select codex:OPENAI_API_KEY --import # separate opt-in for Codex's API key rdsh auth --select env:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY --import # explicitly persist this environment key rdsh auth --unselect codex:openai-codex # stop future copies; retain the existing copy rdsh setup # sync selected credentials, then guide setup rdsh setup --web # inventory, selection commands and explicit key save ``` For a one-time import, use `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex --source codex` or `rdsh auth --import --ref OPENAI_API_KEY --source codex`. These filters do not save or extend future-copy consent; `--select`/`--unselect` are separate persistent policy changes. Repeat --select/--unselect for individual credentials. Selecting enables future imports from that CLI/provider, including boot, dump-config, plugin, raw dsh delegation and setup. --import immediately applies the selection. Even a newer grant in another, unselected CLI cannot be chosen. Newer DSH grants and existing API-key refs/records remain in place. Other entries, comments and line endings are preserved. Unix credential and policy files use mode 0600. The inventory checks Codex's ~/.codex/auth.json and OpenCode's $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json (or its platform default data directory), plus the legacy ~/.config/opencode/auth.json fallback. Selectors for OpenCode use DSH provider IDs; opencode:openai-codex is the selector for its openai login. Environment-key persistence supports DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. These are format/presence checks, not live authentication tests. An environment variable already supplied to rdsh is inherited by DSH and its child processes without rdsh writing a file. The JSON inventory marks this route persistent=false, lists its destination and explains how to stop/revoke it. Using the reference does not opt in to storing it. setup --yes no longer saves every environment key; choose each one with auth --select env:NAME --import. Interactive setup and the web form still allow an explicit, individual key save. **Scope and undo:** saved entries are available to every DSH profile using the same DSH_HOME. Unselect stops future rdsh imports; it does not delete a saved copy or invalidate a running process. Stop DSH and remove the named record/ref from the credential store to stop using a saved copy. To invalidate the credential itself, revoke the OAuth grant or rotate the API key at its provider. That may also disconnect the source CLI. This controls rdsh copying, not DSH's own refreshes, inherited environment access or an OS sandbox. **Migration:** existing DSH credentials are retained. A missing policy selects nothing, including for legacy auth --import. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=1 does not restore the old import-all behavior. Inventory and preview first, then choose the sources you need. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=0 disables automatic imports while keeping the selection; an explicit auth --import still works. Invalid/unreadable policies fail closed instead of falling back to legacy sync. Consent changes and rdsh credential writes share a lock, so a completed unselect cannot be bypassed by a queued rdsh import using an earlier policy. After a crashed writer, check that no rdsh auth/setup writer is active before removing $DSH_HOME/.rdsh-auth-sharing.lock; the launcher skips copying while it is locked. setup --web issues a new local access key at startup in its #key=... URL. The tab retains that key; status reads, key saves and closing require it. Keep the startup URL private. The page shows copy destinations and separate unselect, saved-copy removal and provider revocation steps before a key save. ### Optional extras (off by default) Server-type features stay off until enabled, so a plain install remains a fast dsh: ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve,search-web rdsh settings get extras.enable ``` | Extra | Command | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `serve` | `rdsh serve` (default :38080) | Local status page, localhost only, per-launch key. | | `search-web` | `rdsh search-web "query" --limit 5` | Needs SearXNG. | To connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that dsh does not ship (HAI, Sarashina, a home llama.cpp / vLLM / LM Studio / Ollama server), add it as a profile route: ```sh rdsh provider add hai --model deepseek-v4-flash # key from HAI_API_KEY or --key-stdin rdsh provider add sarashina # key from SARASHINA_API_KEY; mini and nano built in rdsh provider add local-openai --base-url http://host:8080/v1 --discover --no-key rdsh provider list # presets, per-profile route and key status ``` Details: [docs/PROVIDERS.md](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Model Catalog (`rdsh models`) DeepSeek Harness answers "which models can this provider serve?" from the catalog bundled in its `@earendil-works/pi-ai` dependency, which is generated when that package is published. Anything a provider changes afterwards is absent from the picker until that dependency is upgraded — and a profile that lists `models:` explicitly replaces the bundled catalog for the route anyway. `rdsh models` reads the provider's own catalog (the local Codex CLI, or Kimi Code's `/v1/models` endpoint with the profile's API key) and folds it into the profile: ```sh rdsh models # read-only: missing ids and stale names rdsh models --provider kimi-coding # one provider only rdsh models sync # add missing entries, refresh stale names rdsh models sync --profile web --dry-run # preview one profile ``` Nothing is deleted, an existing entry keeps every other byte (a name the provider's current one already contains is left as written), and a profile the command does not recognize is refused instead of rewritten. The harness picks the changes up on the next config reload or restart. ### Agent Tool Isolation Delegated agent tools keep normal file access by default: the model reads and writes the project like any other tool. `--share-file` isolates **`rdsh_inspect` only**. On Linux (with bubblewrap and prlimit) that tool sees just the files you explicitly share: ```sh rdsh --share-file README.md --share-file src/main.rs --profile tui ``` From `rdsh_inspect`, only the shared files are mounted read-only, host files stay out of reach and the sandbox has no network. Turn the same boundary on for every run with `rdsh features on agent_tool_sandbox` (off again with `rdsh features off agent_tool_sandbox`, or force it with `RDSH_SECURITY=1`). Other DSH tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `run_code`, ...) are **not** isolated and follow upstream DSH permissions and approvals. Startup prints `[rdsh security] rdsh_inspect is isolated; other DSH tools use upstream permissions`. ### Hook Guard (`rdsh guard`) Integrates with DSH `hooks.json` to inspect and block dangerous commands before execution: ```sh echo "$input" | rdsh guard --deny "rm -rf /*" --deny "*token*" ``` For an opt-in structured check of supported file tools, pass a policy file. This example permits `Read` only under one existing project directory: ```json { "schema": 1, "rules": [ { "id": "project-read", "tool": "Read", "access": "read", "roots": ["/absolute/project/path"] } ] } ``` ```sh echo "$hook_json" | rdsh guard --policy-file ./hook-policy.json --json ``` The structured classifier supports the `Read`, `Write`, and `Edit` file-path schemas. It canonicalizes the working directory and target, checks the selected tool and read/write scope against existing policy roots, and reports `allow`, `deny`, or `unknown` with a non-sensitive reason. In JSON mode an `allow` is classification only and omits `decision`; the host still owns permission and approval. Unknown tools, shell commands, malformed input, and unsupported tool arguments fail closed. Shell parsing and network destinations are not implemented. Path checks are advisory and can race with later filesystem changes; this hook is not an OS sandbox. Use the actual execution sandbox for enforcement. ```json { "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "rdsh guard --deny \"rm -rf /*\"" }] } ] } } ``` ### Context Injection (`rdsh context`) `rdsh context inject` assembles this turn's context — goal, constraints, decisions, working set, git state, retrieved code, and curated memory — and emits it in the DSH `UserPromptSubmit` hook contract, so the model sees it without any copy-paste: ```sh rdsh features on context_engine # the engine is opt-in rdsh context hook install # merges $DSH_HOME/hooks.json (idempotent) rdsh context hook status --json ``` The hook is fail-open: it never blocks a prompt and always exits 0. Only an unreadable settings document or an unparseable payload inject nothing at all; a corrupt index or a missed deadline drops just what depends on them — the graph or the code search — and still injects goal, constraints, and memory. Injection has its own budget (`context.inject_budget`, default 1200 tokens) and deadline (`context.inject_deadline_ms`, default 1200 ms); once the deadline passes the code search is skipped and only memory, goal, and constraints go out. Memory holds curated items, not a transcript dump: ```sh rdsh context remember "Keep the API compatible" --kind constraint rdsh context distill --session ~/.dsh/sessions///session.v4.jsonl.zstd --apply rdsh context memory --json # active and superseded entries rdsh context forget mem_ab12cd34ef56 ``` `distill` reads user turns only (zstd session logs included) and extracts decisions, constraints, and retractions with deterministic markers, superseding an older overlapping entry instead of guessing. `rdsh context build --require-stable` exits 3 unless the snapshot is provably stable: a file or git state that changed during assembly counts, and so does a git state it cannot read, so a stale or unknown snapshot is never reported as fresh. ### Dependency Graph and Change Impact (`rdsh deps`) ```sh rdsh deps build # incremental index under $DSH_HOME/rdsh-index rdsh deps query engine_score # where a symbol is defined and referenced rdsh deps impact src/context.rs # direct/transitive dependents + affected tests ``` The extractor covers Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, and Go and records imports, definitions, and static call sites per file. Unchanged files (same size and mtime) are reused, so repeated runs stay fast. It is a static approximation: dynamic dispatch, indirect calls, macros, and generated code remain explicitly `unknown` and are reported as unresolved counts rather than guessed, and a missing index means "no information", never "no dependencies". When the index exists, `rdsh context build` and `rdsh context inject` also pull in the graph neighbours of the files their search matched, so a retrieved excerpt arrives with the files it actually depends on. Native execution overhead is ~1 ms per invocation. ## Low-end hosts Default profile: `RDSH_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, then `general.default_profile` in rdsh settings, then local `tui`, else a guided error. Set the saved default with `rdsh settings set general.default_profile web`; an explicit `--profile ` keeps its precedence. rdsh aims to remain useful on modest machines: older x86-64 CPUs, older Linux distributions, and hosts without Node.js installed. - **Faster Node startup.** When rdsh launches dsh, it sets `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` to `~/.cache/rdsh-node-compile-cache`, letting Node reuse compiled code across launches (Node 22.1 or newer; older versions ignore it). An existing `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` value is preserved. Set `RDSH_NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=0`, or use `--passthrough` / `RDSH_PASSTHROUGH=1`, to opt out. - **Broad CPU support.** Prebuilt x86-64 binaries do not require AVX or BMI; the static musl build also runs on systems with older glibc. - **Session token estimates.** `sessions --tokens` reads a decompressed size from the zstd frame header when available. Most streaming frames need the `zstd -dc` fallback. Results are cached under `~/.cache/rdsh/sessions-tokens.json` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` takes precedence); set `RDSH_TOKENS_CACHE=0` to disable the cache. A `?` marks an estimate that could not be read, for example when the zstd CLI is unavailable. - **Bounded parallel work.** Search and session scans use at most eight worker threads. The zstd CLI fallback uses 8 to 32 parallel processes. - **Native commands without Node.** Commands such as `tokens`, `search`, and `sessions` keep working without Node. To delegate conversations, install `@deepseek-ai/dsh` or set `DSH_ORIG_BIN` (or `RDSH_ORIG_BIN`). - **Low-priority updates.** `sync-dsh.sh` updates dsh and rdsh, verifies archive bytes against that registry, and rolls back a failed update candidate. By default it uses the stable release selected by the reviewed repository digest registry; set `RDSH_SYNC_FROM_SOURCE=1` to build from `main` under `nice -n 19` and `ionice -c3` when available. The systemd unit runs at low priority; adjust its `ExecStart` to your checkout. ## Web UI & Dashboard ### Lightweight Local Web UI (`rdsh serve`) A lightweight status and token estimation page running on localhost (default `:38080`, does not conflict with DSH `:3080`): ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve # enable the server feature rdsh serve # launch (bound to localhost, protected with a one-time token) ``` ### Extended Dashboard (`rdsh-dashboard`) Optional Node.js dashboard for project metrics, human-in-the-loop Q&A, and mobile access (requires Node.js 22+): ```sh rdsh-dashboard project --project ``` *On native Windows, the dashboard runs in the system tray and can be opened or stopped from the taskbar (`--no-tray` keeps it in the terminal). See [dashboard/README.md](dashboard/README.md). External agent CLIs (cursor-agent, devin) can be run as supervised jobs: see [docs/AGENT-RUNNERS.md](docs/AGENT-RUNNERS.md).* ## Desktop App (Electron) DeepSeek Harness Desktop is an Electron shell around the complete Web application. It shares `$DSH_HOME` with the CLI but owns a **reserved profile** (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop`) and its own bundled command runtime, so the npm `dsh` CLI cannot manage its plugins. `rdsh desktop` detects all of that and forwards plugin attachment to the app's own command — rdsh never boots or rewrites the profile: ```sh rdsh desktop status # app, command runtime, profile, plugin state (read-only) rdsh desktop install --plugins-dir . # rdsh-settings + default third-party (sound, gitview) rdsh desktop install --plugins-dir . --compute # + the resident compute bridge rdsh desktop install --plugins-dir . --no-sound --no-gitview # skip third-party rdsh desktop verify # exit nonzero when the profile has no rdsh plugin ``` The same is available through the profile installer and the installers: ```sh PROFILE=desktop ./plugins/install.sh # every recommended package, forwarded correctly ./install.sh --desktop # attach the rdsh plugins during installation ``` *Quit the app before attaching plugins, reopen it afterwards. The app's own Plugins page installs the same packages without any command. The Electron runtime itself is never replaced: in-app delegation stays limited to the opt-in, fail-open compute bridge. See [DESKTOP-INTEGRATION.md](docs/DESKTOP-INTEGRATION.md).* Two optional plugins extend the existing Desktop/Web runtime: - [File organization](plugins/rdsh-easy-work/README.md): select a folder, preview extension-based categories, copy after confirmation, and archive the copies to undo. Originals stay in place. Execution currently requires Linux; Windows and macOS support preview only. No AI connection is needed. - [Bounded exploration subagents](plugins/rdsh-subagent-optimizer/README.md): fresh context, bounded concurrency and output, and active duplicate suppression through the native DSH `spawn` provider (0.2.0-rc.2). Use the app's Plugins page to add the corresponding directory, or enable `EASY_WORK=1` / `SUBAGENTS=1` in `plugins/install.sh`. These are opt-in features being prepared for 0.4.0. See the [acceptance evidence](docs/reviews/2026-10-14-easy-work.md). [Desktop SDK and upstream preparation](desktop/README.md) provide a pinned official SDK, an isolated fork home, bundled Rust launcher, and a dedicated rustdsh update channel. Source preparation and SDK transport are tested; signed Desktop installers and update acceptance still require platform builds. ## Using with Smart-DSH [Smart-DSH](https://github.com/hikarioyama/Smart-DSH) (a web-profile plugin bundle) works smoothly alongside rdsh: ```sh rdsh doctor # check dsh version and Smart-DSH bundles rdsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/bundle # add plugins rdsh --profile web # boot web with plugins enabled ``` Ports never collide (DSH Web: `3080`, rdsh serve: `38080`). Ports never collide (dsh web GUI :3080, `rdsh serve` :38080). With `install.sh --as-dsh`, point Smart-DSH helper scripts at `dsh-orig` or export `DSH_PACKAGE_DIR`. ## Web dashboard For the read-only workflow member board in DSH's conversation GUI, use the [verified source-patch preparation tool](plugins/workflow-board/README.md) with an isolated compatible source checkout. evidence.readmeExcerpt: # フォルダから始めるファイル整理 DSH Desktop / Webの空の会話画面に、フォルダを選んで整理する入口を追加します。 既存のフォルダ選択・GUI認証を使います。AI接続やAPIキーは不要で、分類は端末内で実行します。 空の会話のプリセット選択位置をこの入口に切り替えます。プリセットは設定画面から選択できます。 プラグインを無効にすると標準の入口に戻ります。 1. フォルダを選ぶ（WebではDSHが動いている端末の場所を入力できます）。 2. ファイル名、分類、件数、必要な容量を確認する。 3. 「確認した内容でコピーする」を押す。 4. 保存先を確認する。必要なら「整理を取り消す（コピーを保管）」を押す。 元ファイルは移動・削除しません。写真・資料・表・動画・音声・その他へ拡張子で分類して、 新しい `rdsh-organized-` フォルダへコピーします。 取り消しはコピー先全体を隠し保管フォルダ `.rdsh-organize-undone-` へ移します。 コピーを編集していても、その内容を残します。取り消しで使用容量は減りません。 現在、コピーと取り消しは **Linuxの `/proc/self/fd` が利用できる環境**に対応しています。 Windows・macOSではプレビューのみ利用できます。未対応環境でパスによる実行へ切り替えません。 対象はフォルダ直下の通常ファイル200件・合計256 MiBまで。走査は1000項目までです。 子フォルダ、隠しファイル、シンボリックリンク、ハードリンクは対象外です。 保存先は非公開のディレクトリ（0700）、コピーは非公開ファイル（0600）で作ります。 写真の撮影日・内容の理解、PDF要約、Excel加工、GUI自動操作は今後の機能です。 実行はサーバー内に保存した確認内容と人の確認ボタンに基づきます。 確認は10分間有効、最大4件。ファイルが変わった場合は確認をやり直します。 コピーの途中経過を保存先の `.rdsh-organize.json` へ記録します。 アプリを再起動した場合は、元のフォルダを再選択すると、前回のコピーを保管して取り消せます。 不完全なコピーは自動再開せず、元ファイルと途中のコピーを保持します。 このプラグインはPC全体のサンドボックスではありません。 Linuxでは開いたディレクトリのハンドルとリンクをたどらない読み込み、排他的な新規作成を使います。 同じOSユーザーの別プロセスがフォルダを移動・差し替える状況を、完全に隔離するものではありません。 作業中は選択フォルダと整理先を別のアプリから変更しないでください。 実データを外部送信するAPI・モデル向けの実行ツールは公開していません。 ```sh PROFILE=desktop EASY_WORK=1 ./plugins/install.sh PROFILE=web EASY_WORK=1 ./plugins/install.sh node --test plugins/rdsh-easy-work/test/*.test.mjs ``` Desktopではアプリのプラグイン画面から、このディレクトリを追加できます。 最初の導線を検証する段階の任意プラグインです。通常のDSH会話・設定画面は引き続き利用できます。 # rdsh — a fast, safe Rust launcher for `dsh` [![ci](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![dashboard](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml) [![docs](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.85%2B-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [Japanese version](README.ja.md) An independent community project; not an official DeepSeek or DeepSeek Harness project. `rdsh` is a fast, safe launcher for [DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It ports frequently used CLI operations (token calculation, code search, session management) to native Rust, while delegating conversation workflows and model execution transparently to upstream `dsh`. All existing arguments and options continue to work as-is. ## Why rdsh? - ⚡ **Sub-millisecond startup & low memory**: `--version` launches in ~0.90 ms with ~2.9 MB peak memory, compared to ~88 ms and ~66 MB for Node.js-based `dsh`. - 🔄 **100% Drop-in Compatible**: Subcommands that are not rdsh-native are passed straight to upstream `dsh`. Existing scripts and workflows keep running unchanged. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and run health diagnostics (`rdsh doctor`) instantly without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and `rdsh_inspect` can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and inspect local prerequisites (`rdsh doctor --json`) without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and agent tools can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. ## Table of Contents - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Usage](#usage) - [Running with `dsh` Compatibility](#running-with-dsh-compatibility) - [Fast Native Commands](#fast-native-commands) - [Credential sharing with rdsh auth](#credential-sharing-with-rdsh-auth) - [Agent Tool Isolation](#agent-tool-isolation) - [Hook Guard](#hook-guard-rdsh-guard) - [Context Injection](#context-injection-rdsh-context) - [Dependency Graph and Change Impact](#dependency-graph-and-change-impact-rdsh-deps) - [Web UI & Dashboard](#web-ui--dashboard) - [Using with Smart-DSH](#using-with-smart-dsh) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Safety Design](#safety-design) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Community](#community) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Quick Start Already using **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, OpenCode or Gemini CLI**? [Connect the project dashboard through MCP](docs/MCP-CLIENTS.md) to share tasks, questions and structured UI while keeping your current coding agent. This entry point requires Node.js 22+; DSH and Rust are optional. ### 1. Install (Prebuilt Binary) **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --from-release ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell $f = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'rdsh-install.ps1' Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile $f -UseBasicParsing & $f -FromRelease ``` ### 2. Verify & Setup ```sh rdsh --version && rdsh doctor # verify install and original dsh rdsh setup # interactive setup (or rdsh setup --web for browser UI) ``` *Note: If you have an existing login from Codex CLI (ChatGPT OAuth) or opencode, import it with `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex`.* ### 3. Start a Conversation ```sh rdsh tui # start with TUI profile # or rdsh --profile web # start with Web profile ``` ## Requirements | Item | Detail | | --- | --- | | OS | Linux, macOS, WSL, Windows (native) | | DSH runtime | Required for conversations and agent runs (native tools and diagnostics run standalone) | | Rust | 1.85+ (only needed when building from source; prebuilt binaries require no Rust) | | Optional | Node.js 22+ for the [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md); SearXNG for `search-web` | ## Installation ### Building from Source & Advanced Options **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh ./install.sh # build + install to ~/.local/bin/rdsh ./install.sh --as-dsh # also replace `dsh` command (original backed up as dsh-orig) ./install.sh --restore # undo the replacement ./install.sh --prefix=DIR # custom install directory (default: ~/.local/bin) ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh .\install.ps1 # build + install to %LOCALAPPDATA%\rdsh\bin .\install.ps1 -AsDsh # also replace `dsh` command .\install.ps1 -Restore # undo the replacement .\install.ps1 -Wsl # also install inside WSL via install.sh ``` | OS | Script | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./install.sh` | Needs `cargo` or `curl` (guided via rustup if missing). | | WSL | `./install.sh` inside distro | Auto-detects WSL. `install.ps1 -Wsl` installs in both environments. | | Windows (native) | `.\install.ps1` | Needs Rust and MSVC build tools (`winget install Rustlang.Rustup`). | ## Usage ### Running with `dsh` Compatibility Run any standard `dsh` command unchanged: ```sh rdsh tui # equivalent to: dsh --profile tui rdsh --profile web --patch x.yml # launch with configuration overlay rdsh --dry-run tui -- --resume id # print what would be executed ``` When installed with `./install.sh --as-dsh`, typing `dsh` automatically uses the fast `rdsh` launcher. ### Fast Native Commands Native tools execute in Rust without starting Node.js: ```sh rdsh tokens ./README.md # estimate token count (~4 chars = 1 tok, CJK = 1 tok each) echo "..." | rdsh prune --max-tokens 4000 # prune context within a token budget rdsh search TODO --dir . --max 100 # fast parallel text search rdsh sessions --limit 20 --tokens # list sessions and unpacked token estimates rdsh compact ./s.jsonl # compact session JSONL (source remains untouched) rdsh doctor # check health of dsh, environment, and paths rdsh doctor --json # read-only metadata for scripts; no DSH/Node launch rdsh profiles / rdsh skills # list available profiles and skills rdsh desktop status # detect the DeepSeek Harness Desktop app and profile rdsh bench --n 5 # benchmark startup speed between rdsh and dsh ``` On Windows, compressed session histories are not opened until rdsh can reject parent junctions safely; `sessions --tokens` may omit those histories and its totals are inexact. ### Credential sharing with rdsh auth External credentials are inventoried without showing their values. Nothing is copied until you select a source and credential. OAuth copies use DSH's existing version-1 store at $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; API keys use its named refs. The selection policy contains only identifiers at $DSH_HOME/rdsh-auth-sharing.json. ```sh rdsh auth # sources, destinations, selection and undo steps rdsh auth --json # secret-free machine-readable inventory rdsh --dry-run auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # preview; writes no files rdsh auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # share only Codex OAuth rdsh auth --select opencode:openai-codex --import # OpenCode openai maps to openai-codex rdsh auth --select codex:OPENAI_API_KEY --import # separate opt-in for Codex's API key rdsh auth --select env:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY --import # explicitly persist this environment key rdsh auth --unselect codex:openai-codex # stop future copies; retain the existing copy rdsh setup # sync selected credentials, then guide setup rdsh setup --web # inventory, selection commands and explicit key save ``` For a one-time import, use `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex --source codex` or `rdsh auth --import --ref OPENAI_API_KEY --source codex`. These filters do not save or extend future-copy consent; `--select`/`--unselect` are separate persistent policy changes. Repeat --select/--unselect for individual credentials. Selecting enables future imports from that CLI/provider, including boot, dump-config, plugin, raw dsh delegation and setup. --import immediately applies the selection. Even a newer grant in another, unselected CLI cannot be chosen. Newer DSH grants and existing API-key refs/records remain in place. Other entries, comments and line endings are preserved. Unix credential and policy files use mode 0600. The inventory checks Codex's ~/.codex/auth.json and OpenCode's $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json (or its platform default data directory), plus the legacy ~/.config/opencode/auth.json fallback. Selectors for OpenCode use DSH provider IDs; opencode:openai-codex is the selector for its openai login. Environment-key persistence supports DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. These are format/presence checks, not live authentication tests. An environment variable already supplied to rdsh is inherited by DSH and its child processes without rdsh writing a file. The JSON inventory marks this route persistent=false, lists its destination and explains how to stop/revoke it. Using the reference does not opt in to storing it. setup --yes no longer saves every environment key; choose each one with auth --select env:NAME --import. Interactive setup and the web form still allow an explicit, individual key save. **Scope and undo:** saved entries are available to every DSH profile using the same DSH_HOME. Unselect stops future rdsh imports; it does not delete a saved copy or invalidate a running process. Stop DSH and remove the named record/ref from the credential store to stop using a saved copy. To invalidate the credential itself, revoke the OAuth grant or rotate the API key at its provider. That may also disconnect the source CLI. This controls rdsh copying, not DSH's own refreshes, inherited environment access or an OS sandbox. **Migration:** existing DSH credentials are retained. A missing policy selects nothing, including for legacy auth --import. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=1 does not restore the old import-all behavior. Inventory and preview first, then choose the sources you need. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=0 disables automatic imports while keeping the selection; an explicit auth --import still works. Invalid/unreadable policies fail closed instead of falling back to legacy sync. Consent changes and rdsh credential writes share a lock, so a completed unselect cannot be bypassed by a queued rdsh import using an earlier policy. After a crashed writer, check that no rdsh auth/setup writer is active before removing $DSH_HOME/.rdsh-auth-sharing.lock; the launcher skips copying while it is locked. setup --web issues a new local access key at startup in its #key=... URL. The tab retains that key; status reads, key saves and closing require it. Keep the startup URL private. The page shows copy destinations and separate unselect, saved-copy removal and provider revocation steps before a key save. ### Optional extras (off by default) Server-type features stay off until enabled, so a plain install remains a fast dsh: ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve,search-web rdsh settings get extras.enable ``` | Extra | Command | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `serve` | `rdsh serve` (default :38080) | Local status page, localhost only, per-launch key. | | `search-web` | `rdsh search-web "query" --limit 5` | Needs SearXNG. | To connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that dsh does not ship (HAI, Sarashina, a home llama.cpp / vLLM / LM Studio / Ollama server), add it as a profile route: ```sh rdsh provider add hai --model deepseek-v4-flash # key from HAI_API_KEY or --key-stdin rdsh provider add sarashina # key from SARASHINA_API_KEY; mini and nano built in rdsh provider add local-openai --base-url http://host:8080/v1 --discover --no-key rdsh provider list # presets, per-profile route and key status ``` Details: [docs/PROVIDERS.md](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Model Catalog (`rdsh models`) DeepSeek Harness answers "which models can this provider serve?" from the catalog bundled in its `@earendil-works/pi-ai` dependency, which is generated when that package is published. Anything a provider changes afterwards is absent from the picker until that dependency is upgraded — and a profile that lists `models:` explicitly replaces the bundled catalog for the route anyway. `rdsh models` reads the provider's own catalog (the local Codex CLI, or Kimi Code's `/v1/models` endpoint with the profile's API key) and folds it into the profile: ```sh rdsh models # read-only: missing ids and stale names rdsh models --provider kimi-coding # one provider only rdsh models sync # add missing entries, refresh stale names rdsh models sync --profile web --dry-run # preview one profile ``` Nothing is deleted, an existing entry keeps every other byte (a name the provider's current one already contains is left as written), and a profile the command does not recognize is refused instead of rewritten. The harness picks the changes up on the next config reload or restart. ### Agent Tool Isolation Delegated agent tools keep normal file access by default: the model reads and writes the project like any other tool. `--share-file` isolates **`rdsh_inspect` only**. On Linux (with bubblewrap and prlimit) that tool sees just the files you explicitly share: ```sh rdsh --share-file README.md --share-file src/main.rs --profile tui ``` From `rdsh_inspect`, only the shared files are mounted read-only, host files stay out of reach and the sandbox has no network. Turn the same boundary on for every run with `rdsh features on agent_tool_sandbox` (off again with `rdsh features off agent_tool_sandbox`, or force it with `RDSH_SECURITY=1`). Other DSH tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `run_code`, ...) are **not** isolated and follow upstream DSH permissions and approvals. Startup prints `[rdsh security] rdsh_inspect is isolated; other DSH tools use upstream permissions`. ### Hook Guard (`rdsh guard`) Integrates with DSH `hooks.json` to inspect and block dangerous commands before execution: ```sh echo "$input" | rdsh guard --deny "rm -rf /*" --deny "*token*" ``` For an opt-in structured check of supported file tools, pass a policy file. This example permits `Read` only under one existing project directory: ```json { "schema": 1, "rules": [ { "id": "project-read", "tool": "Read", "access": "read", "roots": ["/absolute/project/path"] } ] } ``` ```sh echo "$hook_json" | rdsh guard --policy-file ./hook-policy.json --json ``` The structured classifier supports the `Read`, `Write`, and `Edit` file-path schemas. It canonicalizes the working directory and target, checks the selected tool and read/write scope against existing policy roots, and reports `allow`, `deny`, or `unknown` with a non-sensitive reason. In JSON mode an `allow` is classification only and omits `decision`; the host still owns permission and approval. Unknown tools, shell commands, malformed input, and unsupported tool arguments fail closed. Shell parsing and network destinations are not implemented. Path checks are advisory and can race with later filesystem changes; this hook is not an OS sandbox. Use the actual execution sandbox for enforcement. ```json { "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "rdsh guard --deny \"rm -rf /*\"" }] } ] } } ``` ### Context Injection (`rdsh context`) `rdsh context inject` assembles this turn's context — goal, constraints, decisions, working set, git state, retrieved code, and curated memory — and emits it in the DSH `UserPromptSubmit` hook contract, so the model sees it without any copy-paste: ```sh rdsh features on context_engine # the engine is opt-in rdsh context hook install # merges $DSH_HOME/hooks.json (idempotent) rdsh context hook status --json ``` The hook is fail-open: it never blocks a prompt and always exits 0. Only an unreadable settings document or an unparseable payload inject nothing at all; a corrupt index or a missed deadline drops just what depends on them — the graph or the code search — and still injects goal, constraints, and memory. Injection has its own budget (`context.inject_budget`, default 1200 tokens) and deadline (`context.inject_deadline_ms`, default 1200 ms); once the deadline passes the code search is skipped and only memory, goal, and constraints go out. Memory holds curated items, not a transcript dump: ```sh rdsh context remember "Keep the API compatible" --kind constraint rdsh context distill --session ~/.dsh/sessions///session.v4.jsonl.zstd --apply rdsh context memory --json # active and superseded entries rdsh context forget mem_ab12cd34ef56 ``` `distill` reads user turns only (zstd session logs included) and extracts decisions, constraints, and retractions with deterministic markers, superseding an older overlapping entry instead of guessing. `rdsh context build --require-stable` exits 3 unless the snapshot is provably stable: a file or git state that changed during assembly counts, and so does a git state it cannot read, so a stale or unknown snapshot is never reported as fresh. ### Dependency Graph and Change Impact (`rdsh deps`) ```sh rdsh deps build # incremental index under $DSH_HOME/rdsh-index rdsh deps query engine_score # where a symbol is defined and referenced rdsh deps impact src/context.rs # direct/transitive dependents + affected tests ``` The extractor covers Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, and Go and records imports, definitions, and static call sites per file. Unchanged files (same size and mtime) are reused, so repeated runs stay fast. It is a static approximation: dynamic dispatch, indirect calls, macros, and generated code remain explicitly `unknown` and are reported as unresolved counts rather than guessed, and a missing index means "no information", never "no dependencies". When the index exists, `rdsh context build` and `rdsh context inject` also pull in the graph neighbours of the files their search matched, so a retrieved excerpt arrives with the files it actually depends on. Native execution overhead is ~1 ms per invocation. ## Low-end hosts Default profile: `RDSH_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, then `general.default_profile` in rdsh settings, then local `tui`, else a guided error. Set the saved default with `rdsh settings set general.default_profile web`; an explicit `--profile ` keeps its precedence. rdsh aims to remain useful on modest machines: older x86-64 CPUs, older Linux distributions, and hosts without Node.js installed. - **Faster Node startup.** When rdsh launches dsh, it sets `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` to `~/.cache/rdsh-node-compile-cache`, letting Node reuse compiled code across launches (Node 22.1 or newer; older versions ignore it). An existing `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` value is preserved. Set `RDSH_NODE_COMPILE_CACHE=0`, or use `--passthrough` / `RDSH_PASSTHROUGH=1`, to opt out. - **Broad CPU support.** Prebuilt x86-64 binaries do not require AVX or BMI; the static musl build also runs on systems with older glibc. - **Session token estimates.** `sessions --tokens` reads a decompressed size from the zstd frame header when available. Most streaming frames need the `zstd -dc` fallback. Results are cached under `~/.cache/rdsh/sessions-tokens.json` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME` takes precedence); set `RDSH_TOKENS_CACHE=0` to disable the cache. A `?` marks an estimate that could not be read, for example when the zstd CLI is unavailable. - **Bounded parallel work.** Search and session scans use at most eight worker threads. The zstd CLI fallback uses 8 to 32 parallel processes. - **Native commands without Node.** Commands such as `tokens`, `search`, and `sessions` keep working without Node. To delegate conversations, install `@deepseek-ai/dsh` or set `DSH_ORIG_BIN` (or `RDSH_ORIG_BIN`). - **Low-priority updates.** `sync-dsh.sh` updates dsh and rdsh, verifies archive bytes against that registry, and rolls back a failed update candidate. By default it uses the stable release selected by the reviewed repository digest registry; set `RDSH_SYNC_FROM_SOURCE=1` to build from `main` under `nice -n 19` and `ionice -c3` when available. The systemd unit runs at low priority; adjust its `ExecStart` to your checkout. ## Web UI & Dashboard ### Lightweight Local Web UI (`rdsh serve`) A lightweight status and token estimation page running on localhost (default `:38080`, does not conflict with DSH `:3080`): ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve # enable the server feature rdsh serve # launch (bound to localhost, protected with a one-time token) ``` ### Extended Dashboard (`rdsh-dashboard`) Optional Node.js dashboard for project metrics, human-in-the-loop Q&A, and mobile access (requires Node.js 22+): ```sh rdsh-dashboard project --project ``` *On native Windows, the dashboard runs in the system tray and can be opened or stopped from the taskbar (`--no-tray` keeps it in the terminal). See [dashboard/README.md](dashboard/README.md). External agent CLIs (cursor-agent, devin) can be run as supervised jobs: see [docs/AGENT-RUNNERS.md](docs/AGENT-RUNNERS.md).* ## Desktop App (Electron) DeepSeek Harness Desktop is an Electron shell around the complete Web application. It shares `$DSH_HOME` with the CLI but owns a **reserved profile** (`$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop`) and its own bundled command runtime, so the npm `dsh` CLI cannot manage its plugins. `rdsh desktop` detects all of that and forwards plugin attachment to the app's own command — rdsh never boots or rewrites the profile: ```sh rdsh desktop status # app, command runtime, profile, plugin state (read-only) rdsh desktop install --plugins-dir . # rdsh-settings + default third-party (sound, gitview) rdsh desktop install --plugins-dir . --compute # + the resident compute bridge rdsh desktop install --plugins-dir . --no-sound --no-gitview # skip third-party rdsh desktop verify # exit nonzero when the profile has no rdsh plugin ``` The same is available through the profile installer and the installers: ```sh PROFILE=desktop ./plugins/install.sh # every recommended package, forwarded correctly ./install.sh --desktop # attach the rdsh plugins during installation ``` *Quit the app before attaching plugins, reopen it afterwards. The app's own Plugins page installs the same packages without any command. The Electron runtime itself is never replaced: in-app delegation stays limited to the opt-in, fail-open compute bridge. See [DESKTOP-INTEGRATION.md](docs/DESKTOP-INTEGRATION.md).* Two optional plugins extend the existing Desktop/Web runtime: - [File organization](plugins/rdsh-easy-work/README.md): select a folder, preview extension-based categories, copy after confirmation, and archive the copies to undo. Originals stay in place. Execution currently requires Linux; Windows and macOS support preview only. No AI connection is needed. - [Bounded exploration subagents](plugins/rdsh-subagent-optimizer/README.md): fresh context, bounded concurrency and output, and active duplicate suppression through the native DSH `spawn` provider (0.2.0-rc.2). Use the app's Plugins page to add the corresponding directory, or enable `EASY_WORK=1` / `SUBAGENTS=1` in `plugins/install.sh`. These are opt-in features being prepared for 0.4.0. See the [acceptance evidence](docs/reviews/2026-10-14-easy-work.md). [Desktop SDK and upstream preparation](desktop/README.md) provide a pinned official SDK, an isolated fork home, bundled Rust launcher, and a dedicated rustdsh update channel. Source preparation and SDK transport are tested; signed Desktop installers and update acceptance still require platform builds. ## Using with Smart-DSH [Smart-DSH](https://github.com/hikarioyama/Smart-DSH) (a web-profile plugin bundle) works smoothly alongside rdsh: ```sh rdsh doctor # check dsh version and Smart-DSH bundles rdsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/bundle # add plugins rdsh --profile web # boot web with plugins enabled ``` Ports never collide (DSH Web: `3080`, rdsh serve: `38080`). Ports never collide (dsh web GUI :3080, `rdsh serve` :38080). With `install.sh --as-dsh`, point Smart-DSH helper scripts at `dsh-orig` or export `DSH_PACKAGE_DIR`. ## Web dashboard For the read-only workflow member board in DSH's conversation GUI, use the [verified source-patch preparation tool](plugins/workflow-board/README.md) with an isolated compatible source checkout. It includes the 18-file board/UI projection patch, compatibility diagnostics and fixture tests; building and adopting the patched DSH are separate steps. For bounded MCP resource artifacts and explicit resource-link reads, use the [verified source-patch preparation tool](plugins/mcp-resource-artifacts/README.md) with an isolated checkout at its pinned DSH revision. Resource links are never fetched automatically, binary payloads stay out of model text, and building or adopting the patched DSH are separate steps. ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve # replaces the enabled-extra list rdsh serve # open the URL containing #key=... printed by rdsh (localhost only) ``` | API | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `GET /api/version` | version (requires key) | | `GET /api/doctor` | health check | | `POST /api/tokens` | token estimate for `{"text"}` | | `POST /api/prune` | prune `{"text","max_tokens"}` to budget | | `GET /api/bench?n=3` | startup measurement | | `GET /api/sessions?limit=20` | recent sessions | | `GET /api/skills`, `/api/profiles` | name lists | All APIs require the per-launch key in the `X-RDSH-Token` header (the browser UI reads it from its URL). No CDN is used; the page works offline. `rdsh serve` is the quick local status page. For project metrics, human Q&A, and phone access, use the optional [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md) (needs Node.js 22+): `rdsh-dashboard project --project ` or `rdsh-dashboard harness` for the original Harness Web UI. On native Windows the launcher can live in the tray (right-click Open / Exit, double-click opens; `--no-tray` stays in the terminal). Add `--include-project ` to a project launch to show read-only active, waiting, and needs-attention counts for only the projects explicitly listed at startup. Details stay in each project's dashboard; unreadable projects show their last successful observation time and an unknown state. The original Harness update banner appears right after an update is recorded, every two hours from its update time, and on every full page reload. Dismiss / X or a successful updater check closes the current occurrence; the two-hour schedule continues. Unchanged release checks do not record a new update. Switching projects keeps it closed until the next slot, and close events reach other GUI ports of the same OS user. Activating new code needs one normal GUI restart/reload; see [browser verification](docs/evidence/update-notice-repeat/README.md). rdsh bundles o

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # Scoped PTC tool catalog This optional Cordis bundle adds tool discovery to an existing, authorized DSH PTC composition. It supports `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools@0.2.0-rc.2` and uses the public registry, original SDK renderers and `system-prompt/assemble` waterfall. The original `run_code`, runtime provider, scheduler, guards, approval policies and canonical output validation retain execution ownership. The guarded rdsh launcher forces Native tools. This bundle refuses activation there with `RDSH_CATALOG_GUARDED_NATIVE`; it does not enable PTC in that launcher. Nothing installs the bundle or changes an existing user profile automatically. MCP connection, OAuth and deferred server loading remain owned by their existing services; this catalog enumerates only registered tools. ## Configuration For an original DSH composition that already supplies `tools`, `systemPrompt` and `ptcRuntime`, add this local package through the existing DSH bundle/profile mechanism. Its [bundle patch](cordis.patch.yml) supplies these defaults: ```yaml config: inlineTokenBudget: 16384 inlineTools: [] maxSearchResults: 20 ``` `inlineTools` is an explicit ordered list of exact names whose declarations may be included after the two discovery helpers. A name outside the calling scope is never displayed. A declaration that does not fit stays discoverable. If even the mandatory discovery declarations cannot fit, prompt assembly fails with `RDSH_CATALOG_BUDGET` and an actionable size, rather than omitting the discovery API. A scope that restricts or shadows those helpers fails with `RDSH_CATALOG_SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE`. The budget counts UTF-8 bytes as a conservative token upper bound for byte-based tokenizers. It is deliberately conservative, **not measured DeepSeek token usage**. It covers the complete replacement `tools:sdk` section, including existing execution instructions and discovery guidance. Other system-prompt sections, native wire schemas in `both` mode, returned describe results, and upstream assembly allocations are outside that budget. Only the two helpers and explicit `inlineTools` influence this SDK text. Adding an unrelated tool/schema does not rewrite it. The public waterfall still runs after upstream assembles the full SDK, so this reduces model input cost without claiming to reduce upstream assembly CPU or memory. ## Discovery from the original PTC program ```ts const found = await tools.rdsh_catalog_search({ query: "failed deployment build logs", namespace: "mcp/github", limit: 3, }); if (found.status !== "ok" || found.tools.length === 0) return found; return await tools.rdsh_catalog_describe({ name: found.tools[0].name, revision: found.revision, }); ``` After reading the complete returned schema/declaration, invoke the exact name inside the original PTC program, for example `await tools[exactName](args)` in TypeScript. Python uses its original SDK and `getattr(tools, exact_name)(args)`. The returned declaration is reference text, not executable code to evaluate. - `rdsh_catalog_search` ranks names and descriptions, supports exact namespace prefix boundaries (`.`, `/`, `:`, `__`), and pages an empty query as a thin catalog. `offset`, `limit`, and `nextOffset` describe tool pagination; namespace summaries and description previews report truncation explicitly. - `identifier` filters one normalization collision group. Normalization is diagnostic only. Calls always use exact original names; no alias is created. - `rdsh_catalog_describe` returns complete input/output JSON Schemas, a schema digest and the declaration from the **original** TypeScript/Python renderer. Missing and restricted names return the same `not_found` result, without acknowledging a namespace, collision group, schema or existence. - `revision` identifies the current visible names/descriptions and detects changed search pages. A describe result's separate `schemaDigest` identifies its input/output schemas. Results are recomputed for each calling scope; there is no cross-scope cache or durable tool-state storage. Scope membership is discovery eligibility. Argument-dependent guards, approval and current execution policy can still refuse a discovered call. Search does not simulate a tool body or an approval. Restriction/permission changes after discovery remain authoritative at original nested dispatch. ## Verification and comparison From the repository checkout: ```sh npm ci --prefix plugins/rdsh-ptc-catalog --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund npm test --prefix plugins/rdsh-ptc-catalog node plugins/rdsh-ptc-catalog/benchmark.mjs --output /new/path/benchmark.json ``` The benchmark writes a new file exclusively. It compares 1,000 visible tools and 80 fixed query/execution fixtures against the original full inline SDK. It records encoded input payload size (`js-tiktoken` / `cl100k_base`), fixture lookup success, incorrect body calls, outer PTC submissions, nested dispatches, assembly time and prompt stability. The baseline knows the expected exact name. Search and describe share one discovery submission; the invocation uses a second submission. These are fixture/protocol measurements, not model quality, DeepSeek tokenizer measurements, real provider usage or billed cost. Tests also execute a fixed program through DSH's original Node provider in a fresh home/workspace without inherited provider credentials. They verify complete types, hidden-tool refusal, actual nested events and guard refusal. That execution fixture uses a full-access policy and makes no confinement claim. The separate mandatory [guarded-runtime probe](../../tests/guarded-runtime-probe.mjs) verifies that this bundle cannot lift rdsh's Native/kernel boundary. GitHub CI runs the catalog tests and benchmark on Linux, macOS and Windows, and retains the benchmark report as an artifact. Source-specific results and new/old output are in [PTC catalog evidence](../../docs/evidence/ptc-catalog/README.md). Upstream contracts: [tools API](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/f97c0438fb1608bbc4c08c88a27344249795ea22/docs/tool-catalog.md), [system-prompt waterfall](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/f97c0438fb1608bbc4c08c88a27344249795ea22/docs/subsystems/system-prompt.md), [PTC provider](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/f97c0438fb1608bbc4c08c88a27344249795ea22/docs/subsystems/ptc-runtime.md). # rdsh — a fast, safe Rust launcher for `dsh` [![ci](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![dashboard](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/dashboard.yml) [![docs](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/actions/workflows/docs.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.svg)](https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.85%2B-orange.svg)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [Japanese version](README.ja.md) An independent community project; not an official DeepSeek or DeepSeek Harness project. `rdsh` is a fast, safe launcher for [DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It ports frequently used CLI operations (token calculation, code search, session management) to native Rust, while delegating conversation workflows and model execution transparently to upstream `dsh`. All existing arguments and options continue to work as-is. ## Why rdsh? - ⚡ **Sub-millisecond startup & low memory**: `--version` launches in ~0.90 ms with ~2.9 MB peak memory, compared to ~88 ms and ~66 MB for Node.js-based `dsh`. - 🔄 **100% Drop-in Compatible**: Subcommands that are not rdsh-native are passed straight to upstream `dsh`. Existing scripts and workflows keep running unchanged. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and run health diagnostics (`rdsh doctor`) instantly without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and `rdsh_inspect` can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. - 🛠 **Fast Native Utilities**: Estimate tokens, search code, list sessions, and inspect local prerequisites (`rdsh doctor --json`) without starting Node.js. - 🛡 **Safe by Default**: Read-only commands never modify source files, credentials are never automatically synced or exported, and agent tools can be confined to explicitly shared files on Linux. ## Table of Contents - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Requirements](#requirements) - [Installation](#installation) - [Usage](#usage) - [Running with `dsh` Compatibility](#running-with-dsh-compatibility) - [Fast Native Commands](#fast-native-commands) - [Credential sharing with rdsh auth](#credential-sharing-with-rdsh-auth) - [Agent Tool Isolation](#agent-tool-isolation) - [Hook Guard](#hook-guard-rdsh-guard) - [Context Injection](#context-injection-rdsh-context) - [Dependency Graph and Change Impact](#dependency-graph-and-change-impact-rdsh-deps) - [Web UI & Dashboard](#web-ui--dashboard) - [Using with Smart-DSH](#using-with-smart-dsh) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Safety Design](#safety-design) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Community](#community) - [Credits](#credits) - [License](#license) ## Quick Start Already using **Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, OpenCode or Gemini CLI**? [Connect the project dashboard through MCP](docs/MCP-CLIENTS.md) to share tasks, questions and structured UI while keeping your current coding agent. This entry point requires Node.js 22+; DSH and Rust are optional. ### 1. Install (Prebuilt Binary) **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash -s -- --from-release ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell $f = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'rdsh-install.ps1' Invoke-WebRequest -Uri https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile $f -UseBasicParsing & $f -FromRelease ``` ### 2. Verify & Setup ```sh rdsh --version && rdsh doctor # verify install and original dsh rdsh setup # interactive setup (or rdsh setup --web for browser UI) ``` *Note: If you have an existing login from Codex CLI (ChatGPT OAuth) or opencode, import it with `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex`.* ### 3. Start a Conversation ```sh rdsh tui # start with TUI profile # or rdsh --profile web # start with Web profile ``` ## Requirements | Item | Detail | | --- | --- | | OS | Linux, macOS, WSL, Windows (native) | | DSH runtime | Required for conversations and agent runs (native tools and diagnostics run standalone) | | Rust | 1.85+ (only needed when building from source; prebuilt binaries require no Rust) | | Optional | Node.js 22+ for the [Node.js dashboard](dashboard/README.md); SearXNG for `search-web` | ## Installation ### Building from Source & Advanced Options **Linux / macOS / WSL**: ```sh git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh ./install.sh # build + install to ~/.local/bin/rdsh ./install.sh --as-dsh # also replace `dsh` command (original backed up as dsh-orig) ./install.sh --restore # undo the replacement ./install.sh --prefix=DIR # custom install directory (default: ~/.local/bin) ``` **Windows (PowerShell)**: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/jimoto-no-llm/rustdsh.git cd rustdsh .\install.ps1 # build + install to %LOCALAPPDATA%\rdsh\bin .\install.ps1 -AsDsh # also replace `dsh` command .\install.ps1 -Restore # undo the replacement .\install.ps1 -Wsl # also install inside WSL via install.sh ``` | OS | Script | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./install.sh` | Needs `cargo` or `curl` (guided via rustup if missing). | | WSL | `./install.sh` inside distro | Auto-detects WSL. `install.ps1 -Wsl` installs in both environments. | | Windows (native) | `.\install.ps1` | Needs Rust and MSVC build tools (`winget install Rustlang.Rustup`). | ## Usage ### Running with `dsh` Compatibility Run any standard `dsh` command unchanged: ```sh rdsh tui # equivalent to: dsh --profile tui rdsh --profile web --patch x.yml # launch with configuration overlay rdsh --dry-run tui -- --resume id # print what would be executed ``` When installed with `./install.sh --as-dsh`, typing `dsh` automatically uses the fast `rdsh` launcher. ### Fast Native Commands Native tools execute in Rust without starting Node.js: ```sh rdsh tokens ./README.md # estimate token count (~4 chars = 1 tok, CJK = 1 tok each) echo "..." | rdsh prune --max-tokens 4000 # prune context within a token budget rdsh search TODO --dir . --max 100 # fast parallel text search rdsh sessions --limit 20 --tokens # list sessions and unpacked token estimates rdsh compact ./s.jsonl # compact session JSONL (source remains untouched) rdsh doctor # check health of dsh, environment, and paths rdsh doctor --json # read-only metadata for scripts; no DSH/Node launch rdsh profiles / rdsh skills # list available profiles and skills rdsh desktop status # detect the DeepSeek Harness Desktop app and profile rdsh bench --n 5 # benchmark startup speed between rdsh and dsh ``` On Windows, compressed session histories are not opened until rdsh can reject parent junctions safely; `sessions --tokens` may omit those histories and its totals are inexact. ### Credential sharing with rdsh auth External credentials are inventoried without showing their values. Nothing is copied until you select a source and credential. OAuth copies use DSH's existing version-1 store at $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml; API keys use its named refs. The selection policy contains only identifiers at $DSH_HOME/rdsh-auth-sharing.json. ```sh rdsh auth # sources, destinations, selection and undo steps rdsh auth --json # secret-free machine-readable inventory rdsh --dry-run auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # preview; writes no files rdsh auth --select codex:openai-codex --import # share only Codex OAuth rdsh auth --select opencode:openai-codex --import # OpenCode openai maps to openai-codex rdsh auth --select codex:OPENAI_API_KEY --import # separate opt-in for Codex's API key rdsh auth --select env:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY --import # explicitly persist this environment key rdsh auth --unselect codex:openai-codex # stop future copies; retain the existing copy rdsh setup # sync selected credentials, then guide setup rdsh setup --web # inventory, selection commands and explicit key save ``` For a one-time import, use `rdsh auth --import --provider openai-codex --source codex` or `rdsh auth --import --ref OPENAI_API_KEY --source codex`. These filters do not save or extend future-copy consent; `--select`/`--unselect` are separate persistent policy changes. Repeat --select/--unselect for individual credentials. Selecting enables future imports from that CLI/provider, including boot, dump-config, plugin, raw dsh delegation and setup. --import immediately applies the selection. Even a newer grant in another, unselected CLI cannot be chosen. Newer DSH grants and existing API-key refs/records remain in place. Other entries, comments and line endings are preserved. Unix credential and policy files use mode 0600. The inventory checks Codex's ~/.codex/auth.json and OpenCode's $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json (or its platform default data directory), plus the legacy ~/.config/opencode/auth.json fallback. Selectors for OpenCode use DSH provider IDs; opencode:openai-codex is the selector for its openai login. Environment-key persistence supports DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. These are format/presence checks, not live authentication tests. An environment variable already supplied to rdsh is inherited by DSH and its child processes without rdsh writing a file. The JSON inventory marks this route persistent=false, lists its destination and explains how to stop/revoke it. Using the reference does not opt in to storing it. setup --yes no longer saves every environment key; choose each one with auth --select env:NAME --import. Interactive setup and the web form still allow an explicit, individual key save. **Scope and undo:** saved entries are available to every DSH profile using the same DSH_HOME. Unselect stops future rdsh imports; it does not delete a saved copy or invalidate a running process. Stop DSH and remove the named record/ref from the credential store to stop using a saved copy. A missing policy selects nothing, including for legacy auth --import. RDSH_AUTH_AUTOSYNC=1 does not restore the old import-all behavior. Inventory and preview first, then choose the sources you need. URL. The tab retains that key; status reads, key saves and closing require it. Keep the startup URL private. The page shows copy destinations and separate unselect, saved-copy removal and provider revocation steps before a key save. ### Optional extras (off by default) Server-type features stay off until enabled, so a plain install remains a fast dsh: ```sh rdsh settings set extras.enable serve,search-web rdsh settings get extras.enable ``` | Extra | Command | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `serve` | `rdsh serve` (default :38080) | Local status page, localhost only, per-launch key. | | `search-web` | `rdsh search-web "query" --limit 5` | Needs SearXNG. | To connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that dsh does not ship (HAI, Sarashina, a home llama.cpp / vLLM / LM Studio / Ollama server), add it as a profile route: ```sh rdsh provider add hai --model deepseek-v4-flash # key from HAI_API_KEY or --key-stdin rdsh provider add sarashina # key from SARASHINA_API_KEY; mini and nano built in rdsh provider add local-openai --base-url http://host:8080/v1 --discover --no-key rdsh provider list # presets, per-profile route and key status ``` Details: [docs/PROVIDERS.md](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Model Catalog (`rdsh models`) DeepSeek Harness answers "which models can this provider serve?" from the catalog bundled in its `@earendil-works/pi-ai` dependency, which is generated when that package is published. Other DSH tools (`bash`, `read`, `write`, `run_code`, ...) are **not** isolated and follow upstream DSH permissions and approvals.
