# dsh-git-panel

[English](README.en.md) | 简体中文

![dsh-git-panel](docs/assets/banner-zh.png)

`dsh-git-panel` 是一个 DSH Web GUI 插件，在对话工作区里提供 IDE 风格的 Git 面板。它把分支列表、提交历史图、未提交变更的提交与 amend、语法高亮的差异对照集中到一个常驻标签页，并在输入框左侧放一个 zsh 风格的分支标记，让你在对话过程中随手查看仓库状态、提交改动，不必切到终端或另开 IDE。

面板只读取当前会话工作目录所在的 Git 仓库，所有 git 命令都以 argv 数组经宿主的 subprocess 服务执行，不拼接 shell 字符串，工作目录锁定在仓库根，并带超时与输出上限。插件不改动 git 配置，写操作（提交、amend、暂存、丢弃）都有明确入口。

## 安装

```bash
# npm（默认）
dsh plugin --profile web add @xbzbing/dsh-git-panel@latest

# 或从 GitHub 仓库安装（仓库已提交构建产物，无需本地构建）
dsh plugin --profile web add github:xbzbing/dsh-git-panel
```

安装或更新后，重启 `dsh web` 服务再刷新页面，工作区标签栏（「对话」「轨迹」之后）就会出现 **Git** 面板。插件分 host 与 client 两半，宿主挂载和 client bundle 清单都在服务启动时定型，因此代码更新（安装、`add` 覆盖 `lib`）通常需要重启服务，仅刷新页面可能看不到变化。面板内的配置项（详情页的输入框标记开关、差异默认视图）走配置热写，改动即时生效、无需重启。

> **兼容性**：已在 `dsh@0.2.1-alpha.4` 上实测，安装、Git 面板、输入框标记与 host RPC 均可正常使用。

## 功能

- **Git 总览**：三栏布局。左栏是分支 / 标签列表，点击某个引用即按它过滤历史；中栏是提交历史图，支持按提交信息、commit 哈希、作者、日期搜索，悬停某条提交弹出卡片显示完整提交信息（comment）；右栏是选中提交的变更文件树与提交信息，点击文件在弹出的 modal 里查看该文件在此提交中的差异。
- **变更记录**：面向本地工作区。左栏是统计条（文件数 / 增删行数 / 最近变更时间）、带复选框的未提交变更列表、以及含 **Amend** 复选框的提交框，支持逐文件暂存 / 取消暂存 / 丢弃与手动提交；右栏是选中文件的差异对照。
- **AI 生成提交信息**：提交框旁的「AI 生成」按钮根据当前未提交变更（勾选了文件则只看这些文件）与最近一次提交的风格，调用你在 DSH 中配置的模型生成提交信息，填入提交框后可编辑再提交；没有可生成的变更、模型服务不可用或生成失败都会给出明确提示。**隐私提示：生成请求会把 diff 内容发送给你在 DSH 中所配置模型的供应商。** 可在插件详情页关闭该按钮，并调整输入预算（发送给模型的 diff 上限，默认 128 KiB）、输出上限（默认 4096 tokens，思考模型的推理计入该预算）与生成超时（默认 15 秒）。
- **标签管理**：在「Git 总览」右栏的提交详情顶部可为选中的提交创建标签（轻量标签，或带说明的附注标签）；该提交上已有的标签以可删除的标签片呈现，删除走二次确认。创建与删除标签都只作用于本地仓库，不会推送到远程，如需同步需自行 `git push <remote> <tagname>`（或 `--tags`）。
- **切换分支**：鼠标移到 Git 总览左栏的本地分支或远程引用行上，行尾出现「切换」按钮（窄面板在「筛选分支」底部弹层的行上，触屏设备按钮常显）；当前分支没有该按钮，单击行本身仍是筛选提交历史。点击「切换」后弹出确认框。远程引用不会直接检出（那会游离 HEAD）：已有同名本地分支就切换它，否则确认后执行 `git checkout -b <名> --track <origin/名>` 创建本地分支并设置跟踪。确认框显示「当前 → 目标」；有未提交变更时列出数量并提供两种选择——直接切换（与目标分支冲突时由 Git 拒绝、工作区不变），或先贮藏（含未跟踪文件）再切换，之后到「变更记录 → 贮藏」手动恢复（不会自动恢复，恢复冲突需手动解决）。切换成功后提交历史、分支列表、变更列表与文件浏览的目录缓存一并刷新。
- **提交回撤**：同一处提交操作区可「还原此提交」（revert，追加一个反向提交、不动工作区）或「重置到此」（reset，软 / 混合 / 硬三挡）。硬重置会列出将被永久丢弃的未提交改动并要求额外勾选确认，始终不作为默认方式；检测到未提交改动时提示这些改动可能是 dsh AI 正在进行的工作。还原与重置都只改写本地仓库，不会推送到远程，远端分支需你自行推送同步。
- **贮藏（stash）**：「变更记录」页可将当前未提交更改贮藏起来（可填说明），下方的贮藏列表支持应用 / 弹出 / 丢弃；弹出或应用遇到冲突时保留贮藏条目并提示，不会半途丢失。丢弃走二次确认。
- **共享工作区护栏**：标签 / 贮藏 / 还原 / 重置等写操作与 dsh 的 AI 共用同一仓库，弹窗底部统一提示「可直接让 AI 执行 Git 操作」；撞上 `.git/index.lock`（另一进程正在操作）会自动重试一次并给出「Git 正忙」提示而非原始报错。
- **文件浏览**：直接打开工作区「Git」标签时，非 Git 目录默认进入文件浏览；Git 仓库中无未提交变更则进入「Git 总览」，有未提交变更则进入「变更记录」。非 Git 目录也能浏览，以当前工作目录为根。左栏目录树按需加载（点开才读取下一层，不显示 `.git`），按文件类型显示 dsh 官方图标，被 `.gitignore` 忽略的条目半透明呈现，宽度可拖动；右栏可预览代码、文本和图片，顶部可复制文件相对路径，过大文件或其他二进制文件显示提示。Markdown 默认显示源码，可点击「渲染」切换到 dsh 自带的 Markdown 视图；HTML 默认显示源码，可点击「渲染」在隔离沙箱（`allow-scripts`、无同源权限）中预览页面，不会自动执行。大文件的源码视图按行虚拟化（只渲染视口内的行），超大文件关闭语法高亮、超长行截断，保证流畅。
- **图片缩放**：文件浏览与差异对照的图片共用同一缩放组件——Mac 触控板双指捏合（Chromium/Firefox/Safari 15+ 以 Ctrl+滚轮事件送达、旧 Safari 走 gesture 事件）与 <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+滚轮都以光标为锚点缩放（10%–800%），放大后可用双指滚动、滚轮、滚动条或**鼠标左键拖拽**平移（抓手光标；拖拽不会被当成双击，另拖原生滚动条不受影响），浮动工具栏提供 − / 百分比 / + / 适应窗口 / 全屏（全屏入口只在工具栏，图片单击不触发，否则每次双击都会被第一次单击打断），双击在适应窗口与 100% 间切换，灯箱内可继续缩放拖拽，<kbd>Esc</kbd>、点关闭钮或点灯箱空白区域退出。
- **代码内查找**：文件浏览的源码视图与差异对照都支持 <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>⌘</kbd>+<kbd>F</kbd> 就地查找——高亮全部命中并保留语法着色，显示「当前 / 总数」，<kbd>Enter</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> 或 `‹` `›` 在命中间跳转，可切换区分大小写（默认不敏感），<kbd>Esc</kbd> 关闭。命中统计覆盖整份内容，视口外的命中同样计入并可跳转。
- **语法高亮差异**：总览弹窗、变更记录和文件浏览共用 dsh 官方语法高亮，按文件扩展名选择语言，语法资源按需加载；差异视图的改动词级强调保留原有交互。
- **对照模式**：差异支持「统一 / 对照 / 变更前 / 变更后」四种视图切换。统一视图为单栏行内对比（改动行前后紧邻，省横向空间），对照视图为左右并排；两种视图都带块间隐藏上下文的按需展开与改动行的词级高亮。默认视图可在插件详情页选择（统一 / 并排），也可在每个差异视图工具栏临时切换。
- **移动端 / 窄面板自适应**：面板宽度收窄到 620px 及以下（手机竖屏，或右侧栏挤压面板）时自动切换为单栏「钻取」布局——三栏折叠为一栏，列表与详情 / 差异 / 预览之间点击进入、带「返回」按钮退出；Git 总览的分支筛选改为从底部升起的面板（bottom sheet），提交行改为两行式更易点按，顶栏控件换行到第二行而非隐藏，差异对比在窄屏隐藏「对照」（并排）模式。面板变宽后自动恢复三栏布局，桌面体验不变。触控设备（如平板）上逐文件操作按钮常驻显示、点按区域放大。
- **显示输入框标记开关**：插件详情页可切换输入框标记；关闭后输入框不再显示分支标记，改为在「Git」标签旁显示状态圆点（绿=已同步、橙色=有变更），两者互斥，保存后立即生效。同一处配置区还可设置差异对比的默认视图（统一 / 并排）、提交历史图的线条样式（平行线 VSCode 风格 / 紧凑 git log 风格，默认平行线）。「AI 生成提交信息」为独立配置卡片：开关按钮之外，可调整输入预算 / 输出上限 / 生成超时三项（范围 16–512 KiB / 256–16384 tokens / 5–120 秒，超出范围的值会被夹到边界）。
- **输入框 Git 标记**：一个 zsh 主题风格的 `<仓库名> (<分支>)` 标记，仓库名青色，`(分支)` 在已同步时为绿色、有未提交变更时为橙色；悬停显示完整仓库路径，点击跳转面板（有未提交变更进入变更记录，否则进入 Git 总览）；非 Git 目录不显示输入框标记，可通过工作区的「Git」标签进入文件浏览。
- UI 跟随 DSH 系统语言设置，支持简体中文和英文。

## 界面

| Git 总览 | 文件差异 modal |
| :---: | :---: |
| ![Git 总览：分支、提交历史图、提交详情与 hover 卡片](docs/assets/screenshots/1-git-panel-overview.png) | ![文件差异 modal：语法高亮的统一 / 并排对照、块间按需展开与词级高亮](docs/assets/screenshots/2-overview-tab.png) |
| 变更记录 | 文件浏览 |
| ![变更记录：统计条、未提交变更列表、提交框与差异对照](docs/assets/screenshots/3-changes.png) | ![文件浏览：懒加载目录树、官方类型图标、忽略项半透明与文件预览](docs/assets/screenshots/4-files.png) |

## 架构

插件分 host / client 两半，通过 typert Remote 网关通信。

- **Host**（`lib/host/`）：`gitPanel` 命名空间上的 Cordis + typert `GitPanelService`，暴露 `snapshot` / `run` / `query` / `suggest` / `version` 五个端点，仅做端点委托与生命周期接线；git 命令经宿主 `subprocess` 服务执行（argv 数组、无 shell、cwd 锁仓库根、超时 + 输出上限）；`suggest` 端点经宿主 `llm` 服务用你已配置的模型一次性生成提交信息。
- **Client**（`lib/client.js`）：一个 React 包，注册 `conversation.view` 面板和 `conversation.input.left` 标记。每会话一个快照控制器（轮询 + turn 完成后刷新 + 连接重置重拉），标记、变更记录页和统计条共用同一份快照，避免重复 git 命令。

## 开发

```bash
node build.mjs      # tsc（host d.ts）+ esbuild（host 逐模块 js + client bundle + testkit）
npm run typecheck   # 类型检查
npm run test:unit   # 纯算法与 host 端点单测（node --test）
npm run test:e2e    # 隔离的 file:// 无头浏览器 e2e（不碰任何运行中的实例）
npm test            # 单测 + e2e
```

host 产物按 `src/host/` 逐模块输出（一个源文件一个 js，堆栈直接落在出问题的模块），且不做压缩：typert 网关靠方法参数名做参数校验，压缩会改名并破坏 wire 契约。client 改动没有热重载，需重新构建并刷新页面。`lib/` 作为构建产物随 git 提交入库，改动 `src/` 后必须重新构建并提交，否则从 GitHub 安装会加载到过期入口；测试期生成的 `lib/testkit.mjs` 不入库。本地联调：把插件加入 dsh web profile 的 `dsh.profile.bundles`，用 `file:` 依赖指向本目录，构建后即生效。

## 项目结构

```text
src/
  host/
    types.ts        wire 数据模型的唯一权威源（client 直接复用）
    index.ts        GitPanelService：端点委托与生命周期接线
    git.ts          subprocess → 带超时的 GitRunner
    core.ts         workspace 解析 + snapshotForSession
    actions.ts      GitAction → git 命令序列（commit / amend / stage 等）
    queries.ts      history / diff / file-lines / image-diff / dir-list / file-content / show / branches / tags / worktree-stats
    suggest.ts      AI 生成提交信息（diff 收集 + ctx.llm 一次性调用）
    parser.ts       git 输出解析为结构化数据
    version.ts      本包版本 + GitHub release 更新检查
  client/
    rpc.ts          gitPanel 端点的 client 面
    controller.ts   每会话快照控制器
    Panel.tsx       主面板壳：子 tab 路由 + 版本条
    OverviewTab.tsx Git 总览三栏 + hover 卡片
    ChangesTab.tsx  变更记录页
    FilesTab.tsx    文件浏览（懒加载目录树 + 文件预览）
    DiffView.tsx    差异视图（统一 / 并排 / 变更前 / 变更后）
    GitPill.tsx     输入框标记
    code-spans.ts   将语法高亮 token 按词级改动区间切分
    git-graph.ts    提交图车道布局
    file-tree.ts    路径折树
    diff.ts         unified diff → 并排行 + 统一行 + 统计
```

## 许可证

本项目采用 [MIT License](LICENSE)。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-aux-degrade **Compaction summaries and session titles stop burning their output budget on reasoning.** > ⚠️ **DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates. [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-1.5-8a2be2.svg)](#compatibility) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-desktop%20%7C%20web-lightgrey.svg)](#compatibility) **English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)
--- ## What this is Besides the main conversation, a DSH session has a pile of **auxiliary LLM calls** running behind the scenes: generating compaction summaries, starting session titles, enhancing prompts. They share the same model as the main conversation, yet often **specify no reasoning effort** — so they inherit the high level you set and burn the entire output budget on reasoning. The result is that a compaction summary is cut off halfway by `max_tokens`, and that truncation is **silent**: nothing reports an error, the next turn simply starts with a piece of context missing. A session title that tops out halfway and turns into half a word is the same disease. `dsh-aux-degrade` hooks into the `llm/stream` waterfall and scales the auxiliary call down before it is sent. --- ## The four things it does All four happen inside the same `llm/stream` hook. **Note: only #1 is controlled by the `enabled` switch**; #2–#4 execute under any configuration — this is deliberate, because they fix problems like "an upstream plugin omitted required information", not optional optimizations. ### 1. Lower the reasoning effort to `off` If any one of the following conditions holds, this call's `reasoningEffort` is overridden to `off`: | Criterion | Description | |---|---| | **By purpose** | `purpose` falls in the `purposes` list (by default covering `compaction`, `session-title`, `title`) | | **By originating plugin** | the initiator is in the `auxPlugins` list (by default recognizing `dsh-prompt-enhance`) | | **By shape** | `purpose` is not declared and `tools` is not an array — a call of this shape is auxiliary | **And** the caller itself has not explicitly specified `reasoningEffort`. If it set a level itself, this plugin lets it through and does not override someone else's explicit intent. To use a different level instead of `off`: `config.effort = 'low'` and the like. ### 2. Raise `maxTokens` to no less than 1024 Some callers set `maxTokens` extremely small (worst case 1) together with a high reasoning level, which amounts to "truncated before the body even starts". This plugin gives it a floor: **no less than 1024**. It can be overridden with an environment variable: ```bash DSH_AUX_MAXTOKENS_FLOOR=2048 # use a different floor DSH_AUX_MAXTOKENS_FLOOR=0 # turn this item off ``` ### 3. Append two faithful-preservation requirements to the compaction instruction The biggest risk of a compaction summary is not "short", it is "lossy". Under pressure a summary generator prioritizes narrative and drops hard facts: paths, commands, error codes, constraints. Whenever this call has `purpose === 'compaction'`, the plugin appends two sections to the end of the compaction instruction: ```markdown ## Standing facts & constraints (MUST keep verbatim) ## Commands & outcomes (MUST keep verbatim) ``` **Idempotent**: if the instruction already contains these two sections, they are not appended again. ### 4. Clear `tools` on compaction calls A compaction summary does not need to call any tool. Keeping the tool definitions both consumes prompt space and gives the model the opportunity to "just call a tool while it is at it" — which turns what should be a plain-text summary generation into multiple round trips. For calls with `purpose === 'compaction'`, `tools` is cleared. It can be turned off with `config.noTools = false`. ### Logging Whenever any of #2–#4 acts, one line is printed: ``` [aux-degrade/context] maxTokens下界=1024 压缩去tools=true 补两节=true ``` --- ## 9. The official-patch notice: one dialog, naming the patch and how to apply it The one official patch this plugin **requires** (`pi-ai-max-tokens-floor`, editing `dist/api/simple-options.js` inside `@earendil-works/pi-ai`) is announced by **this plugin itself**, in one dialog. Why it is required: upstream pi-ai clamps `max_tokens` to 1, so auxiliary calls (compaction summaries, session titles) can come back with one or two characters — and whatever the summary never covered really does disappear from the context. This plugin can turn the high thinking level off and raise the floor from the plugin layer, but **it cannot change that clamp** (the third-party dist exposes a read-only ESM namespace). - **How to apply it (any one of three)**: **A** press "Copy the prompt" and hand it to **your own agent**; **B** `node apply.mjs --check`, then `node apply.mjs --apply --only pi-ai-max-tokens-floor`; **C** apply by hand with `git apply -p1`; - **The patch library**: ; - **Detection**: a **content hash** (`pristine` / `patched`) plus the `*.orig` backup; when it cannot decide it says **"cannot tell"** and never guesses "applied"; - **Once applied, it stops appearing**; "Do not remind me again" is permanent and recorded **per patch id**, so a patch added later is still announced. The dialog also lists **the other official patches** (owned by no plugin), so nothing goes unseen. ## Configuration The configuration file is the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: aux-degrade config: enabled: true purposes: [] models: [] effort: off ``` | Key | Type | Code default | Effect | |---|---|---|---| | `enabled` | boolean | **`false`** | Controls only #1 (lowering reasoning effort). It takes effect only when set to `true` — what this repository's `cordis.patch.yml` sets is `true` | | `purposes` | string[] | `[]` → `['compaction', 'session-title', 'title']` | Identify auxiliary calls by purpose | | `auxPlugins` | string[] | `[]` → `['dsh-prompt-enhance']` | Identify auxiliary calls by originating plugin. Passing `['__none__']` disables this criterion entirely | | `models` | string[] | `[]` (unrestricted) | Apply only to the specified models | | `effort` | string | `'off'` | The level to lower to | | `noTools` | boolean | `true` | Whether compaction calls have `tools` cleared (#4) | > ⚠️ **`enabled: false` does not mean "zero side effects".** The old documentation said so, and it is wrong. `enabled` only stops #1 (lowering reasoning effort); #2–#4 (raising the `maxTokens` floor, appending the two faithful-preservation requirements, clearing `tools` for compaction) run **before** any `enabled` check in the code, and execute as soon as the `purpose` conditions are met. To stop #2, use `DSH_AUX_MAXTOKENS_FLOOR=0`; for #4 use `config.noTools = false`; #3 (appending the two sections) has no separate switch. ### Why is `dsh-prompt-enhance` recognized by default? Because when it initiates a call it **does not pass `purpose`** — the "by purpose" criterion above is completely ineffective for it. Without this `auxPlugins` criterion, its calls would inherit the high reasoning level all the way through, the output budget would be eaten by inference, and the symptom would be a flood of 502s and half responses. This criterion exists for its sake. --- ## 📚 Tutorials | Document | What it covers | |---|---| | [Install & official patches (English)](tutorial-install-and-official-patches.md) | How to install all four plugins (two verified routes) and what to do about the official patches — including prompts that let **your own agent** apply them the patches themselves ship as a library: | | [安装与官方补丁（中文）](tutorial-install-and-official-patches.zh-CN.md) | the same, in Chinese 补丁本体已开源成补丁库： | --- ## 🔗 The rest of the family Each plugin installs on its own; together they save the most. The other three: - [`dsh-context-reclaim`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-context-reclaim) — Context reclamation: bounded tool results, a folded tool surface and a stable prefix - [`dsh-capability-composer`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-capability-composer) — Capability composer: switchable tool/skill/MCP sets instead of one bloated surface - [`dsh-composer-launcher`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-composer-launcher) — Launcher: one panel for compositions, plugins and MCP, plus the extension walkthrough > All of them are **DSH 1.5 only**; newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates. Plugins that need official patches announce them in the UI once you install them — nothing goes unseen. ## Installation ### From GitHub (recommended; measured on a fresh `DSH_HOME`) ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add github:xiamubumu/dsh-aux-degrade ``` One command. DSH registers it into the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` by itself. ### From a local tarball (air-gapped machines) Download `dsh-aux-degrade-1.1.0.tgz` from [Releases](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-aux-degrade/releases), then: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-aux-degrade-1.1.0.tgz ``` ### From the DSH plugin marketplace / npm (not yet possible) The marketplace submission (an `awesome-dsh-plugin` PR) has not been filed and nothing is published on npm yet ⇒ **neither route works today**. Once it is listed/published, installing from the marketplace, or `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-aux-degrade`, becomes valid. > ⚠️ **Known issue: do not feed the release asset's tarball URL to `dsh plugin add`.** > `dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/.../releases/download/v1.1.0/....tgz` fails on the pnpm DSH bundles (10.34.5) with > `ERR_PNPM_MISSING_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` ([pnpm#14351](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14351), fixed upstream only in pnpm ≥ 12.5.1). > Installing a second plugin that way **always** fails — use the two routes above instead. After installing you **need to restart DSH** — host-side plugins are only loaded when DSH starts. This plugin has **no runtime dependencies at all**; `peerDependencies` only declares the official `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`. --- ## Compatibility ### Coexistence: does it fight other plugins? (measured 2026-10-15) **Server-side seams — no conflict.** Of the 44 plugins installed on the test machine, **21** also hook at least one of `llm/stream`, `tools/pre-execute`, `tools/post-execute`, `system-prompt/assemble`, `session/event` — and **20 of them are cooperative** (every handler calls `next()` to pass through). This plugin runs alongside all of them, including `dsh-vision-router`, which hooks four of the same seams. The reason: DSH event seams are a **middleware waterfall**. As long as every party calls `next()` and only makes incremental edits, they **compose** instead of pre-empting each other. **Client slots**: this plugin occupies **none** — it is a server-side plugin with no front end. > Only **`chain`** slots render just the first entry; `list` slots stack, and `keyed` slots give each key its own cell. **This plugin occupies no `chain` slot.** **The three cases that do collide (honestly stated)** 1. The other plugin **rebuilds** the same seam wholesale (rewrites the whole system prompt / tool result) instead of editing incrementally; 2. The other plugin takes the **same `chain`** slot; 3. Both need a patch to the **same official file** — this one is reported as an explicit `conflict` by the patch library `apply.mjs --check`, never as a silent failure. **Measured coexistence**: `dsh-context-reclaim` + `billion-context@0.1.175` share one profile with no conflict — the former rides the **Cordis event bus**, the latter rides an **agent bootstrap layer** (bootstrap-hook / native loader, shipping bundled payloads for six different agents). They share no seam. | | | |---|---| | **DSH kernel** | **1.5 series** (`0.1.5-rc.2` ≤ version < `0.2.0`) — this is exactly the range written in `package.json`'s `engines.dsh`. Later DSH versions will be followed up | | **Form factor** | **Desktop ✅ · Web ✅** — more precisely, **anything running DSH is supported**; this plugin only hooks Cordis's `llm/stream` seam and does not depend on any desktop-only capability | | **Operating system** | Windows · macOS · Linux | | **Node syntax** | 20 and above (**you do not need to install Node yourself**, DSH ships its own runtime) | --- ## 🔗 Interaction with other plugins ### 🔗 With `dsh-context-reclaim` (the context governance pair) — install both together `dsh-aux-degrade` and [`dsh-context-reclaim`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-context-reclaim) are the two halves of the same "context governance" scheme. **Installing both together is strongly recommended; this is the most important interaction this plugin has.** **① They share the same routing criterion.** Both plugins use the same test to tell a "main-conversation call" from an "auxiliary call": ``` tools.length > 0 ? 'main' : 'aux' ``` reclaim uses it to tag every request with `route=`, and aux-degrade uses it to decide whether this call counts as an auxiliary call. Only when the criterion is identical will the two plugins avoid one saving while the other leaks. > One detail worth knowing: the criteria on the two sides are **not literally identical**. reclaim looks at whether the `tools` array has any content; on the "by shape" criterion aux-degrade additionally requires `purpose === undefined`, so as not to hit main-conversation calls that explicitly declare a purpose. So "calls that get degraded" is a subset of "aux-routed calls" — **degrading is more conservative than routing**, and that is deliberate. **② How they divide the work.** aux-degrade handles **calls** (how much reasoning budget this call spends, what the output floor is, whether the compaction instruction needs the faithful-preservation requirements); reclaim handles **content** (purification and bounding of tool results before they enter history, tool definition surface folding, prefix stabilization). **③ What happens without the other.** | Installed alone | Result | |---|---| | Only aux-degrade | Everything works as usual. Auxiliary calls are saved and compaction summaries are not truncated. But tool results are not purified or bounded, and long results enter history unchanged | | Only reclaim | Everything works as usual. But auxiliary calls still burn the full reasoning budget and compaction summaries can still be silently truncated — reclaim will only print `[reclaim/summary-audit] ⚠️ 摘要缺 N/8 段` in the log to remind you, **it will not modify the summary itself** | **④ They do not depend on each other.** aux-degrade only imports the official `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, does not import reclaim, and does not probe whether it is installed. **Either one can be installed alone and work normally** — which is also why they are two repositories rather than one. **⑤ In one sentence.** reclaim keeps "the context from getting fat", aux-degrade makes "the places that should be short actually short". Install both, and context governance is complete. ### 🔗 With `dsh-composer-launcher` No direct coupling. ### 🔗 With `dsh-capability-composer` No direct coupling. --- ## FAQ
Will it lower the reasoning effort of the main conversation too? No. All the criteria point at "auxiliary calls": either the purpose is in the list, or the originating plugin is in the list, or the call declares no `purpose` at all and has no tools. A main-conversation call touches none of the three. And **if the caller explicitly set `reasoningEffort` itself, this plugin always lets it through** — it does not override anyone's explicit intent.
Does `enabled: false` turn it off completely? No. `enabled` controls only #1 (lowering reasoning effort). #2–#4 execute under any configuration. This is not a bug — those three fix problems like "an upstream plugin omitted required information", and switching them off would let the upstream keep failing. If you really want to turn items off one by one: `DSH_AUX_MAXTOKENS_FLOOR=0` turns off #2, `noTools: false` turns off #4, and #3 has no separate switch.
Why does it recognize `dsh-prompt-enhance` by default? Because it does not pass `purpose` when it initiates a call, so the purpose criterion alone cannot identify it. And it happens to be the plugin hit hardest by this problem — if it is not recognized, it inherits the high reasoning level, the output budget is eaten by inference, and the symptom is a flood of 502s and half responses.
Do I need to restart after installing? Yes. Host-side plugins are loaded when DSH starts.
Does it support web DSH? Yes. This plugin only hooks Cordis's `llm/stream` waterfall seam and does not depend on Electron or any desktop-only capability. **As long as it is DSH, both desktop and web work.**
--- ## Repository layout ``` dsh-aux-degrade/ ├── index.js # the entire implementation (single file, no external dependencies) ├── cordis.patch.yml # DSH plugin manifest patch ├── package.json ├── verify.mjs # offline self-check: node verify.mjs ├── README.md # English └── README.zh-CN.md # Simplified Chinese ``` ## Self-check ```bash node verify.mjs ``` Runs offline and writes nothing to disk. It checks the manifest fields, the syntax, whether any private key or backup file slipped in, and whether any hard-coded machine path exists in the runtime code. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © 2026 夏目 ([xiamubumu](https://github.com/xiamubumu))

# dsh-capability-composer

**The resident tool surface collapses into a few switchable sets, shrinking the system prompt on demand.**

> ⚠️ **DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates.

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-1.5-4c6ef5.svg)](#compatibility)
[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)](#compatibility)

**Shrink what the model sees, not what is running.**

---

## Table of contents

- [What this is](#what-this-is)
- [What it does (four mechanisms)](#what-it-does-four-mechanisms)
- [How a composition is resolved (three levels)](#how-a-composition-is-resolved-three-levels)
- [UI](#ui)
- [Screenshots](#screenshots)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [HTTP API](#http-api)
- [🔗 Integration](#-integration)
- [Known limitations (stated plainly)](#known-limitations-stated-plainly)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Compatibility](#compatibility)
- [FAQ](#faq)
- [Repository layout](#repository-layout)
- [Self-check](#self-check)
- [License](#license)

---

## What this is

By default DSH stuffs all of the following **into every single request**:

| What gets stuffed in | Measured size |
|---|---|
| **Tool schema** registered by every installed plugin | 414 tool definitions / ~65.6K tokens |
| The **catalog of all skills** | ~76K tokens as a baseline |
| The **system-prompt section** registered by each plugin | `agent-teams:usage` ≈1296 tok + `plugin:dsh-docker` ≈579 tok + `plugin:api-client` ≈254 tok |

Every request pays for "the things you might use", while only a few of them are actually useful in this turn.

`dsh-capability-composer` groups these into **compositions**, and **only lets the current composition into the context**.

### What it does / what it does not do

Let's make the boundary clear first, because this is where misunderstandings happen most easily:

| ✅ It does | ❌ It does not |
|---|---|
| Narrow **the plugin catalog the model sees** | Never turns off any plugin — plugin processes keep running, the UI keeps showing them |
| Shadow **skill catalog entries** that are not on the list | Never removes skills — `/skill-name` can still be invoked manually |
| Make tools **non-resident by default** (keeping only the core + meta tools) | Does not restrict execution — `invoke_tool` can call anything by default |
| Prune the **system-prompt sections** registered by plugins, according to the composition | Does not touch committed history |
| Resolve compositions at the session / workspace / global levels | Does not modify any third-party plugin file on disk |

In one sentence: **it shrinks "the catalog the model can see", not "the things that are running".** Plugins keep running, skills stay available, tools stay callable — all that changes is how much gets stuffed into each request.

---

## What it does (four mechanisms)

### ① Tools are non-resident by default

**Only 31 are resident**: the 28 official core tools, plus 3 meta tools — `search_plugins` / `load_plugin` / `invoke_tool`.

All other tools **never enter the tools list**. The model sees them in the catalog section of the system prompt (section heading `# 可用插件与 MCP 工具`), and calls them directly when needed:

```js
invoke_tool({ tool: "mcp__vnpy__run_backtest", args: { ... } })
```

Use `load_plugin` when a whole group needs to be loaded:

```js
load_plugin({ ids: ["mcp:vnpy"] })
```

**The granularity is "plugin", not "tool name".** This is deliberate: finer granularity was tried — after 417 / 211 tool names were compressed away, the model had no idea what to search for, which made things harder to use instead. The granularity now is the plugin.

Mounting it prints one log line saying so:

```
工具按需加载已挂载：常驻白名单 28 个 + 元工具 3 个（其余全部按需；组合只决定可见范围）
```

### ② Skill shadowing (not disabling)

A skill that is not in the current skill composition gets a **shadow entry with the same name** registered:

- `invocation.modelInvocable: false` — does not enter the skill catalog the model can see and auto-invoke
- `rank: 0` — the lowest rank wins, shadowing the original skill

**`/skill-name` can still be invoked manually.**

One shadow entry is mounted at the global level, and every agent gets one more at the **"nearest level"**, so that session-level compositions also take effect at the agent dimension.

### ③ Plugin compositions narrow "the model's plugin catalog"

Narrowing happens **when the catalog section is generated**, not by unloading plugins.

There are **two lines that are never narrowed**:

- **MCP server lines** — one line per MCP server; the tools inside a server are not governed by compositions
- **The "unassigned tools" fallback line** — tools that cannot be attributed to any plugin are always kept

### ④ System-prompt sections registered by plugins are pruned by composition too

Plugin compositions **cannot control** "the system-prompt sections a plugin registers for itself" — those are inserted by the plugin itself in `system-prompt/assemble`, and are a different thing from the catalog section.

This plugin's `prunePluginSections()` is the only place that can prune them according to the current plugin composition.

Measured saving: **≈2129 tokens / request**:

| Section | Size |
|---|---|
| `agent-teams:usage` | ≈1296 tok |
| `plugin:dsh-docker` | ≈579 tok |
| `plugin:api-client` | ≈254 tok |

**Fail-open design** — better to prune too little than to prune by mistake:

- A section whose owner cannot be identified is always kept
- A section without a namespace is always kept
- When the visible plugin list is empty, **nothing is pruned**, and the log records 「没有『不在组合里』的依据，宁可留着」
- When the plugin list cannot be obtained, nothing is pruned either

Every drop prints one line of evidence to the log.

It can be turned off with `DSH_COMPOSER_PRUNE_PLUGIN_SECTIONS=0`.

---

## How a composition is resolved (three levels)

**The rule is "the nearest level that specifies something wins" — not a strict override.**

| Level | Description |
|---|---|
| 1. **Session** | specified for the current session alone |
| 2. **Workspace** | specified for the current working directory (`cwd`) |
| 3. **Global** | `pinned[axis]['*']` |

A few easy-to-get-wrong points:

- **An empty string / an empty array / `null` all count as "not specified"** and keep inheriting from the level above — they do not mean "specified as empty"
- **A single level can select several entries**; the union is taken
- **An empty list = no filtering** (not "select none"). To select none, use `__none__`

The UI shows which level the current one comes from: 『当前会话』 / 『当前工作区』 / 『全局』 (Session / Workspace / Global).

---

## UI

It installs into DSH's **Settings → Plugins**, adding two tabs:

### Plugin compositions

Decides which plugins appear in **the model's plugin catalog**.

### Skill compositions

Decides which skills appear in **the model's skill catalog**. You can create a composition, rename it, delete it (with a second confirmation), rename a series, delete a series, select all / select none, and search skills.

### Changes take effect immediately, no restart needed

- UI changes are **debounced by 400 ms**, then `POST /dsh-capability-composer/state`
- After the host writes to disk, the state is refreshed immediately

### Saving merges item by item per composition name, not a whole-state overwrite

The server state is the base; only composition names that **actually exist** in the local draft are overwritten. So a composition created elsewhere will not be accidentally deleted by this UI.

The trade-off: a composition deleted here will be "resurrected" if it still exists on the server. **This is a deliberately conservative direction** — losing a composition costs far more than keeping one extra composition.

---

## Screenshots

### Skill compositions page

Manage which skills each composition contains under Settings → Plugins → Skill compositions, and which level 「这里用」 ("Use here") applies to.

![Skill compositions](screenshots/01-skill-compositions.png)

### Skill scope

Organize skill compositions by series, and use the dropdown to pick which set the current session / current workspace / global each use.

![Skill scope](screenshots/02-skill-scope.png)

---

## 9. Official patches: this plugin needs none

This plugin only occupies `system-prompt/assemble` and the skills service, so it **needs no official DSH patches** and shows no patch dialog — that notice belongs to the two plugins that do need patches (`dsh-context-reclaim`, `dsh-aux-degrade`).

To see what the ten official patches do and whether you want them:

- the tutorial "Install & official patches" → `tutorial-install-and-official-patches.md` (shipped inside this plugin);
- the patch library → <https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-patch-library> (ten self-contained patches, an adaptive applier, five ways to apply them, ready-made prompts).

## Configuration

### State file

**There is exactly one**:

```
<DSH_HOME>/capability-composer/compositions.json
```

The resolution order for `<DSH_HOME>`:

| Platform | Path |
|---|---|
| All | `DSH_HOME` environment variable (takes priority) |
| Windows | `%APPDATA%\dsh-desktop\harness` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/dsh-desktop/harness` |
| Linux | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dsh-desktop/harness` or `~/.config/dsh-desktop/harness` |

**If none of them exists, it errors out and exits — it never guesses a hard-coded path and silently writes into it.**

A `compositions.json.bak` backup is made automatically before every write.

Two other runtime files (both are caches; delete them and they are rebuilt automatically):

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `capability-composer/entry-id-map.json` | cache from package name → entry id |
| `.composer-resident-tools` | the auto section of the resident tool list |

### First install starts empty

A fresh machine gets `defaultState()` — four empty slots, no compositions, no pins. **No seed and no
"starter pack" is shipped**: every composition in such a file would be somebody else's, and a new
user opening the composer must not find arrangements they never created.

**Your existing `compositions.json` is never overwritten and never cleared** — an empty state is
written only when the file is absent or unreadable.

### Environment variables

**This plugin has no cordis config; everything is tuned through environment variables.**

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_COMPOSER_MIDDLEWARE_FULL` | **on** | full pass-through on the execution side (`invoke_tool` can reach MCP tools and tools of dependency agents) |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_TOOL_SEARCH` | **on** | register the `search_plugins` searcher |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_PRUNE_PLUGIN_SECTIONS` | **on** | prune the system-prompt sections registered by plugins, according to the composition |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_CATALOG_FALLBACK` | **on** | fallback source for catalog data |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_CACHE_SAFE` | **on** | cache-safe mode |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_GUARD` | **on** | guard check |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_DIAG` | **on** | diagnostics log |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_AUTOLOAD_MAX` | `0` | auto-load limit |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_SHRINK_ENTRIES` | off | catalog entry shrinking |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_HISTORY_REWRITE` | off | history rewrite |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_RESIDENT_BUDGET` | — | resident budget |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_RESIDENT_FILE` | — | resident tool list file |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_EXTRA_TOOLS` | — | extra tools to keep resident |
| `DSH_COMPOSER_RESIDENT_EXCLUDE` | — | resident exclusion list |
| `DSH_SEMGREP_SHORT_PATH` | `C:\dshse` | semgrep short-path junction (see below) |

**About `DSH_SEMGREP_SHORT_PATH`**: this is **the only** absolute path with a default value in this plugin's runtime code. It has to match the junction path hard-coded by the semgrep plugin patch in the marketplace, otherwise that patch cannot self-heal. It can be overridden with an environment variable; when semgrep is not installed, the relevant function simply returns `not-installed` — it is code that never executes.

---

## HTTP API

Prefix `/dsh-capability-composer`.

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/state` | read the snapshot |
| `GET` | `/skills` | list skills |
| `GET` | `/effective?sessionId=&cwd=` | the effective list after three-level resolution |
| `GET` | `/catalog` | plugin catalog (for the composition picker) |
| `POST` | `/state` | write state |

### Security

- **Anything non-loopback is 403** (`loopback only`)
- **A failed Origin check is always 403** (`origin not allowed`) — local tools that send no Origin are let through

### `POST /state` has a hard gate

The body must carry either `compositions` or `pinned`, otherwise it is rejected with 400:

> 拒绝写入：body 必须是状态对象（或 `{state: ...}`），且至少带 compositions / pinned —— 免得一个空 body 把组合清空 [refusing the write: the body must be a state object (or `{state: ...}`) and must carry at least compositions / pinned — so that an empty body cannot wipe the compositions]

**This gate was added after a real incident**: a `{state: {…}}` wrapper was once POSTed by mistake, wiping **9 plugin compositions + 21 skill compositions**.

---

## 🔗 Integration

### With dsh-composer-launcher

**Without this plugin, the launcher does not break.**

The launcher has an integration table that probes `GET /dsh-capability-composer/state`:

| Case | Launcher behavior |
|---|---|
| Probe succeeds | shows 「按组合收窄 N / 共 M 已装插件」 ("shrunk by composition N / M plugins installed"); the picker can read the composition contents |
| Probe fails | **silently skipped** — the integration list just shows `HTTP xxx`, and plugin names fall back to rendering the package name |

The source comment, verbatim: 「有就连，没有就静默跳过（不存在是正常状态）」.

**Conversely, without the launcher this plugin works as usual** — this plugin never probes the other side; the other side probes it.

### With dsh-mcp-manager-ui

**This plugin does not manage MCP, and does not read the MCP panel's data.**

Only two things relate to MCP:

1. **Excluding the MCP panel from its own plugin catalog** — `dsh-mcp-panel` / `dsh-mcp-connector` / `dsh-mcp-manager-ui` / `dshmarket` / `dsh-client-ui-settings-plugins` and this plugin itself never enter the "plugins managed by compositions" list
2. **Generating one line per MCP server in the catalog section** (id looks like `mcp:<server>`), so the model can load the whole group with `load_plugin({ ids: ["mcp:<server>"] })` when needed

**This line is never narrowed by compositions.**

The exact wording of that hint in the UI:

> MCP 工具完全不受这里影响，归 MCP 面板自己管。

**Without the MCP panel nothing happens** — it is not in the dependencies.

### With dsh-context-reclaim

**The two plugins do not depend on each other, but their responsibilities complement each other.**

The `prunePluginSections()` capability lives in this plugin because **compositions cannot control the system-prompt sections a plugin registers for itself** — that has to be done in a place that can see both "the current composition" and "the fully assembled prompt", and this plugin happens to be that place.

**Installing this plugin alone, without reclaim: everything works normally**, except that tool results are not sanitized / bounded.

---

## Known limitations (stated plainly)

1. **Tool attribution is guessed by scanning source string literals; it is not an authoritative mapping.** That is why `/state` carries three honest annotation fields: `exact` (exactly determined), `uiOnly` (only used in the UI), `scanCertain` (scan confidence).
2. **The first scan of the plugin catalog takes about 5 seconds**; after that it goes through the `entry-id-map.json` cache.
3. **Auxiliary calls that do not pass `purpose`** are classified as the main route and are not affected by degradation.
4. **`GET` on `/state` has a side effect**: with `?_probeKeys=` it writes the reported real keys into the auto section of `.composer-resident-tools` (it only writes the file; a restart applies it).

---

## 📚 Tutorials

| Document | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [Install & official patches (English)](tutorial-install-and-official-patches.md) | How to install all four plugins (two verified routes) and what to do about the official patches — including prompts that let **your own agent** apply them the patches themselves ship as a library: <https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-patch-library>  |
| [安装与官方补丁（中文）](tutorial-install-and-official-patches.zh-CN.md) | the same, in Chinese 补丁本体已开源成补丁库：<https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-patch-library>  |

---

## 🔗 The rest of the family

Each plugin installs on its own; together they save the most. The other three:

- [`dsh-context-reclaim`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-context-reclaim) — Context reclamation: bounded tool results, a folded tool surface and a stable prefix
- [`dsh-aux-degrade`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-aux-degrade) — Auxiliary-call degradation: summaries and titles stop burning their budget on reasoning
- [`dsh-composer-launcher`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-composer-launcher) — Launcher: one panel for compositions, plugins and MCP, plus the extension walkthrough

> All of them are **DSH 1.5 only**; newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates. Plugins that need official patches announce them in the UI once you install them — nothing goes unseen.

## Installation

### From GitHub (recommended; measured on a fresh `DSH_HOME`)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:xiamubumu/dsh-capability-composer
```

### From a local tarball (air-gapped machines)

Download `dsh-capability-composer-1.0.0.tgz` from [Releases](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-capability-composer/releases), then:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-capability-composer-1.0.0.tgz
```

### From the DSH plugin marketplace / npm (not yet possible)

The marketplace submission (an `awesome-dsh-plugin` PR) has not been filed and nothing is published on npm yet ⇒ **neither route works today**.

> ⚠️ **Known issue: do not feed the release asset's tarball URL to `dsh plugin add`.**
> `dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/.../releases/download/v1.0.0/....tgz` fails on the pnpm DSH bundles (10.34.5) with
> `ERR_PNPM_MISSING_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` ([pnpm#14351](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14351), fixed upstream only in pnpm ≥ 12.5.1).
> Installing a second plugin that way **always** fails — use the `github:` shorthand or a local tarball path instead.

### From a local directory

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-capability-composer
```

### ⚠️ Do not use `npm install` / junction / link

This plugin ships `install.mjs` and `install.ps1`; the comment inside states the reason:

> 不走 Junction —— Junction 会被 DSH 的 `projectGenerations()` 静默丢掉字段，重启后 link 与依赖项一起消失，插件整个不可见，日志里一行都没有。 [do not go through a Junction — DSH's projectGenerations() silently drops fields, so after a restart the link and its dependencies disappear together, the plugin becomes entirely invisible, and not a single line shows up in the log.]

The correct approach is to copy it into a generation entity + write `generation.json` / `desired.json` + call the official `projectGenerations()`.

### Restart DSH after installing

Host plugins and patches are loaded **only at startup**.

### After installing, changes in the workspace do not take effect automatically

`install.mjs` states it clearly: 「从此**工作区里的改动不会自动生效**，改完要重跑一次本脚本」.

---

## Compatibility

### Coexistence: does it fight other plugins? (measured 2026-10-15)

**Server-side seams — no conflict.**

Of the 44 plugins installed on the test machine, **21** also hook at least one of `llm/stream`, `tools/pre-execute`, `tools/post-execute`, `system-prompt/assemble`, `session/event` — and **20 of them are cooperative** (every handler calls `next()` to pass through). This plugin runs alongside all of them, including `dsh-vision-router`, which hooks four of the same seams.

The reason: DSH event seams are a **middleware waterfall**. As long as every party calls `next()` and only makes incremental edits, they **compose** instead of pre-empting each other.

**Client slots**:

| Slot | Kind | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `settings.plugins.tab` | `list` | its own tab |
| `tool.call.toolview` | `keyed` | one cell per key |


> Only **`chain`** slots render just the first entry; `list` slots stack, and `keyed` slots give each key its own cell. **This plugin occupies no `chain` slot.**

**The three cases that do collide (honestly stated)**

1. The other plugin **rebuilds** the same seam wholesale (rewrites the whole system prompt / tool result) instead of editing incrementally;
2. The other plugin takes the **same `chain`** slot;
3. Both need a patch to the **same official file** — this one is reported as an explicit `conflict` by the patch library `apply.mjs --check`, never as a silent failure.

**Measured coexistence**: `dsh-context-reclaim` + `billion-context@0.1.175` share one profile with no conflict — the former rides the **Cordis event bus**, the latter rides an **agent bootstrap layer** (bootstrap-hook / native loader, shipping bundled payloads for six different agents). They share no seam.


| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| **DSH** | **the 1.5 series** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Later DSH versions will be followed up |
| DSH Desktop | ✅ |
| DSH Web | ✅ |
| **As long as it is DSH** | ✅ everything works |
| Windows / macOS / Linux | ✅ |
| Node | 20+ at the syntax level; **but you do not need to install it yourself** — DSH Desktop bundles the runtime, and the plugin is loaded into that runtime |
| Runtime dependencies | **zero** |

---

## FAQ

<details>
<summary>Can a composition "turn off" a plugin to save memory or CPU?</summary>

No. **There is no action that turns a plugin off.**

Plugins load as usual, run as usual, and appear in the UI as usual. The only thing saved is **context** — the catalog section and the system-prompt sections get shorter, and each request pays fewer of those tokens.

</details>

<details>
<summary>If a plugin is not selected in a composition, can its tools still be called?</summary>

Yes. **What a composition narrows is "the catalog the model can see", not execution permission.**

By default `DSH_COMPOSER_MIDDLEWARE_FULL` is on, so the execution side is unrestricted — `invoke_tool` can reach MCP tools and tools of dependency agents.

</details>

<details>
<summary>If a skill is not in the composition, is it disabled?</summary>

No. The skill is still registered; it just **does not enter the skill catalog the model can auto-discover** (`modelInvocable: false`).

**The slash command `/skill-name` can still be invoked manually.**

</details>

<details>
<summary>I changed a composition in the UI — do I need to restart DSH?</summary>

No. It is saved automatically after a 400 ms debounce and takes effect immediately.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Is there a config file for tuning parameters?</summary>

**No.** This plugin reads no cordis config at all (`cordis.patch.yml` contains only a 5-line `insert`).

Everything tunable is an **environment variable**; see the table above.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Does this plugin support MCP management? Does it ship an MCP panel?</summary>

**Neither. The MCP panel is not its.**

The panel you see under "Capabilities → MCP" is **another plugin's** UI. This plugin does only the two MCP-related things: excluding the MCP panel from its own plugin catalog, and generating one line per MCP server in the catalog section.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Can the UI follow the DSH language setting?</summary>

**Yes.** The copy lives in two tables (140 keys each) and the plugin reads the host's `locale` service, so switching the DSH language switches the UI live. Adding a third language is a `registerLanguage(id, table)` call — the registry is not hard-coded to these two.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Is the tool-to-plugin mapping accurate?</summary>

**It is guessed by scanning; it is not an authoritative mapping.** That is why the API carries three honest annotation fields: `exact` / `uiOnly` / `scanCertain`.

It is accurate in the vast majority of cases, but do not use it as authoritative data.

</details>

---

## Repository layout

```
dsh-capability-composer/
├── cordis.patch.yml        插件挂载入口（5 行）
├── package.json
├── lib/
│   ├── index.js            宿主半边：状态、HTTP 接口、目录生成、段裁剪
│   └── client.js           客户端半边：设置里那两个页签
├── install.mjs             安装脚本（不走 Junction）
├── install.ps1             Windows 用
├── screenshots/
├── verify.mjs              自检
├── README.md               English (this file)
└── README.zh-CN.md         Simplified Chinese
```

---

## Self-check

```bash
node verify.mjs
```

Zero dependencies, offline, writes nothing to disk. It checks manifest fields, entry syntax, leftover secrets, and hard-coded absolute paths.

---

# dsh-composer-launcher

**One "+" panel for compositions, plugins and MCP.**

> ⚠️ **DSH 1.5 only** (`>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0`). Newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates.

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-1.5-4c6ef5.svg)](#compatibility)
[![Host](https://img.shields.io/badge/host-desktop%20%7C%20web-2f9e44.svg)](#compatibility)
[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)](#compatibility)

**The composer's `+` button, turned into a real menu.**

---

## Table of contents

- [What this is](#what-this-is)
- [What it does](#what-it-does)
- [Screenshots](#screenshots)
- [The browser extension](#the-browser-extension)
- [Settings](#settings)
- [HTTP routes](#http-routes)
- [Interface language](#interface-language)
- [🔗 Integration](#-integration)
- [Known limitations (stated plainly)](#known-limitations-stated-plainly)
- [Installation](#installation)
- [Compatibility](#compatibility)
- [FAQ](#faq)
- [Repository layout](#repository-layout)
- [Self-check](#self-check)
- [License](#license)

---

## What this is

By default the `+` button left of the composer opens a file picker. Everything else you may want to point the model at — a browser tab you are looking at, an earlier conversation, a skill, an MCP server, one of the plugins installed on this machine — has to be typed by hand, or referenced with `@`.

`dsh-composer-launcher` replaces that button with a **three-group menu**:

| Group | What is in it |
|---|---|
| **Add** | files and folders, earlier chats, plan mode, goal mode |
| **Capabilities** | slash commands, skills, MCP servers |
| **Common plugins** | one row per installed plugin, plus an "all plugins" row |

What you pick does not get pasted in as text. It becomes a **reference chip** on a rail above the input box — the same native chip kind the host already renders for `@` references — and only turns into message text when you actually send.

There is also an **optional browser extension** (`DSH Tab Bridge`) which pushes your real browser's tabs to the plugin over a loopback HTTP bridge, so the Tabs row lists the pages you genuinely have open rather than a throwaway debug instance.

---

## What it does

### 1. The `+` menu (three groups)

A 360px panel, opened from the button at the `conversation.input.left` slot.

- **Add** — *Files and folders* (the host's own picker, multi-select, drag-and-drop; falls back to `@` references when the host exposes no folder picker), *Chats* (via `remote.sessionReferenceResolver`; chats only, no files), *Plan*, *Goal*.
- **Capabilities** — *Commands* (whatever the host's slash-command service offers), *Skills* (read live with `ctx.remote.skills.list({ sessionId })`), *MCP* (needs the host's `remote.mcpManager`).
- **Common plugins** — one row per plugin returned by `ctx.remote.pluginInventory.list()`. That list is read from the host on every load, so installing, removing or disabling a plugin is reflected immediately and there is no cache to keep in sync. Three modes decide which rows appear: `pinned`, `frequent`, `mixed` (see [Settings](#settings)).

Every row can be switched off individually from the settings card.

### 2. Reference chips

Picked items land on a rail **above** the input box (`conversation.input.dock`). A chip is `{ label, kind, icon }` plus an optional `url`, where `kind` is one of `web`, `plugin`, `skill`, `mcp`. Clicking the `×` removes it.

Two properties are worth naming, because both were bugs before they were features:

- **A web chip keeps its address.** A page title with no URL is useless to whoever reads the message — the chip carries the URL and the payload includes it.
- **A session reference stays a chip.** Writing a reference back through the plain-text draft API silently downgrades it to body text; the plugin renders it as a chip instead and never round-trips it through the text editor.

Chips are **per session**, so two chat tabs never share a rail.

On send, each chip is serialised into the message with a short marker, so the model can tell a referenced page from an attached file:

| Chip kind | Marker |
|---|---|
| web page | `【参考网页】<title> — <url>` |
| plugin | `【使用插件】<name>` |
| skill | `【技能】<name>` |
| MCP server | `【MCP】<name>` |

> These markers are literal and stay in Chinese in both interface languages. They are part of the text the **model** reads, not interface copy — translating them would change what the model sees.

### 3. Settings card

Registered on the `settings.plugin.item` slot as a card titled **Launcher** — 「启动器」 in the Chinese interface. It is collapsed the first time you open it and remembers that choice. All twelve fields are listed under [Settings](#settings).

### 4. Debug browser (fallback)

The Tabs row can also read tabs over a remote-debugging port from a Chromium process it starts itself. That is what **Launch debug browser** does — and when the extension is staged, the same call attaches it with `--load-extension` and then verifies through the debugging port that it really mounted, so this route needs no manual step at all (see [The browser extension](#the-browser-extension)). It stays a fallback rather than the primary path because it only ever sees that one throwaway-profile instance, never the browser you already have open.

### 5. Loopback bridge

The host half owns a small HTTP bridge on `127.0.0.1:43130` (override: `DSH_LAUNCHER_BRIDGE_PORT`) so the extension can push tabs into it. It binds loopback only, yields politely if an older instance already holds the port, and is used for nothing else.

---

## Screenshots

**The `+` menu — Add / Capabilities / Common plugins — with the Tabs row fed by the extension**

![The composer + menu with the Tabs group and the connected extension](screenshots/01-composer-menu-tab-bridge.png)

**The Tabs row reading a real Microsoft Edge window over the bridge**

![Tab list pushed from Microsoft Edge](screenshots/02-tab-list-edge.png)

**The MCP servers the Capabilities group can reference — the row is built from the host's `remote.mcpManager`**

![MCP servers listed by the host](screenshots/03-mcp-servers.png)

**The plugin inventory the Common plugins group is built from, including its "N / M" narrowing counter**

![Plugin inventory with composition filtering](screenshots/04-plugin-inventory.png)

---

## The browser extension

The plugin works without it — the Tabs row simply says the extension is not installed and points at the button. With it, the row lists the tabs of your **everyday browser**.

### Three ways to get it loaded

Chromium will not let anything silently sideload an extension into the browser you use every day. That is a browser security rule with no plugin-side workaround, so the goal is a different one: make every *remaining* step either automatic or one click.

| Route | What happens | Manual steps |
|---|---|---|
| **A — a browser this plugin starts** | The plugin spawns a separate Chromium process with `--load-extension` pointing at the staged copy, then **verifies through the debugging port that the extension really mounted** | none |
| **B — your everyday browser** | The Tabs row offers *Open the extensions page* and *Copy the extension path*, so loading it once is a paste and a "Load unpacked" | one time, ~20 seconds |
| **C — managed machines** | Chromium enterprise policy (`ExtensionSettings` / `ExtensionInstallForcelist`) pointing at a self-hosted, signed CRX plus an HTTPS update manifest | admin rights; **not shipped here** |

**Route A is verified, not assumed.** After launching, the plugin asks the debugging port for its raw target list and looks for *this* extension's own worker (`chrome-extension://<id>/background.js`) rather than "some extension" — every Chromium ships several of its own. Chromium reports no error when `--load-extension` is ignored, so a launch on its own proves nothing.

If our worker is missing, the plugin retries once on a clean profile `~/.dsh-edge-agent-ext` and says so in the `healed` and `note` fields of its answer. That is not defensive padding: a profile that was ever opened *without* the command-line switches can stop honouring them, and the plugin's default profile `~/.dsh-edge-agent` does exactly that on some machines. If both attempts fail, `extensionLoaded` comes back `false` and the Tabs row falls back to reading tabs over the debugging port — the plugin never claims a step it did not actually complete.

Firefox cannot be started this way: the launcher passes Chromium-only switches, which is why it is the one browser the plugin's table marks as manual-only.

Route B is what those two buttons and `install-extension.ps1` are for (see *Which browsers* below) — nothing in either contains a drive letter or a user name.

Route C is a real answer for fleets, and out of scope here: it needs administrator rights, a CRX you signed yourself, and an HTTPS endpoint serving the update manifest. This repository ships none of that, and no README should pretend otherwise.

### How it works

It does not poll. The extension **pushes**:

| Trigger | Action |
|---|---|
| `tabs.onCreated` / `onUpdated` / `onRemoved` / `onActivated` / `onMoved` / `onAttached` / `onDetached` | push immediately |
| a 1-minute `alarms` heartbeat | push |
| browser startup, install, update | push |

Each push is a `POST` to `http://127.0.0.1:43130/composer-launcher/tabs` with `{ tabs: [...] }`. A failed push is swallowed, never thrown — the bridge is allowed to be down, and the extension must not spam console errors while it is.

The host keeps the last push for **65 seconds** (`PUSH_TTL_MS`), deliberately longer than the 1-minute heartbeat, so one slow tick cannot make the row flicker to empty. An **empty** push is ignored rather than obeyed (`ignored: 'empty-push-kept-previous'`), because a browser that momentarily reports nothing must not wipe the list.

Pushed fields are `{ id, title, url, host, favIconUrl, browser }`. Internal pages are filtered before sending: `chrome:`, `edge:`, `brave:`, `opera:`, `vivaldi:`, `about:`, `devtools:`, `chrome-extension:`, `extension:`, `moz-extension:`.

The popup shows the connection state, lets you edit the port, and has a **Save and push now** button for when you do not want to wait for the next heartbeat.

### Which browsers

The extension is Manifest V3 and talks to `globalThis.browser ?? globalThis.chrome`, so it loads in every Chromium browser as well as Firefox.

| Browser | Extensions page | Loading |
|---|---|---|
| Microsoft Edge | `edge://extensions` | Load unpacked |
| Google Chrome | `chrome://extensions` | Load unpacked |
| Brave | `brave://extensions` | Load unpacked |
| Vivaldi | `vivaldi://extensions` | Load unpacked |
| Opera | `opera://extensions` | Load unpacked |
| Arc | `arc://extensions` | Load unpacked |
| 360 极速浏览器 | `chrome://extensions` | Load unpacked |
| QQ 浏览器 | `chrome://extensions` | Load unpacked |
| Firefox | `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox` | Load Temporary Add-on |

Chromium browsers do not allow silent sideloading — that is a browser security rule, not something a plugin can work around (routes A and C above are the two exceptions, and C needs an administrator). So for your everyday browser the plugin's job is to **point precisely**: the Tabs row has an *Open the extensions page* button (route `POST /composer-launcher/open-extensions-page`, which picks the first Chromium installed here) and a *Copy the extension path* button, and `install-extension.ps1` does the same from a terminal — it enumerates the browsers actually installed on this machine (on Windows from the `StartMenuInternet` registry keys, on macOS and Linux from the platforms' own locations), prints them, and opens the right extensions page for the one you choose. `-Browser <id>` picks one non-interactively. Nothing in that script contains a drive letter or a user name.

Firefox is offered but flagged differently in the plugin's own browser table: it is not offered to the debug-browser launcher, because that launcher passes Chromium-only flags.

### Port

Default `43130`, or whatever `DSH_LAUNCHER_BRIDGE_PORT` holds when it parses as an integer between 1024 and 65535. That override exists so two DSH instances on one machine can each keep their own bridge instead of one stealing the port from the other (this repository's own end-to-end tests use it for exactly that reason). The extension's port is editable in its popup: if you change one, change the other — a mismatch only means the Tabs row reports the extension as offline and falls back to the debug port.

`43129` is recognised as the legacy port and migrated automatically on first read.

---

## Settings

Namespace `composer-launcher`. Every field is a boolean or a number except the last, and all of them are optional.

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `showWeb` | `true` | Show the Tabs row |
| `webCount` | `3` | How many tabs to show before the "N more tabs" row |
| `port` | `9222` | Local **CDP** port (the debug-browser path, not the bridge) |
| `showFiles` | `true` | Show the files-and-folders row |
| `showPlan` | `true` | Show the plan row |
| `showGoal` | `true` | Show the goal row |
| `showCmd` | `true` | Show the slash-command row |
| `showSkill` | `true` | Show the skills row |
| `showMcp` | `true` | Show the MCP row |
| `pluginMode` | `"mixed"` | `pinned` \| `frequent` \| `mixed` |
| `pluginCount` | `5` | How many plugin rows to show before the "all plugins" row |
| `pinned` | `[]` | Plugins that always appear, regardless of mode |

> `pinned` is empty on purpose, and the client half keeps the same empty default. It used to list two plugin names in the host schema only, which made the two halves disagree — a user who never opened the settings would see two pinned rows they had never chosen.

---

## HTTP routes

Everything is served under `/composer-launcher` on the host's existing web server. The plugin does not open a second web port (the bridge on 43130 is a separate, tiny loopback socket for the extension).

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/tabs` | The extension pushes its tab list. Returns `{ ok, accepted }` — or `{ accepted: 0, ignored: 'empty-push-kept-previous', kept: N }` when an empty push was refused |
| `GET` | `/tabs?port=` | Merged tab list (extension first, CDP second). Returns `{ source, stale, port, sources: { extension, cdp, mixed }, extensionHint, tabs, error }` |
| `GET` | `/stage-extension` | Copy the bundled extension to a stable path and return `{ extensionDir, dir, browsers, note }` — `browsers` is the list of browsers actually installed here |
| `GET` | `/linked-plugins` | Probe partner plugins. Returns `{ linked: [{ id, label, ok, detail }] }` |
| `POST` | `/open-debug-browser` | Start a Chromium instance with a debugging port **and the staged extension attached**; the answer carries `extensionLoaded` (verified over the debugging port, not assumed), plus `healed`/`note` when a clean profile was needed |
| `POST` | `/open-extensions-page` | Open the extensions page of the first Chromium installed on this machine, for the one-time manual load. Returns `{ ok, browser, url }` |
| `GET` | `/bundles` | The profile's mounted-plugin manifest |
| `GET`\|`HEAD` | `/favicon?u=<encoded>` | Same-origin favicon proxy: it sniffs the bytes, caches for 6 hours, and serves with `default-src 'none'; sandbox` |
| `GET`\|`HEAD` | `/bridge` | Bridge identity: `{ bridge: true, pid, port, holding, startedAt }` |
| `POST` | `/bridge-yield` | Ask an older instance to release the bridge port |
| `GET` | `/health` | `{ plugin, extensionTabs, extensionAt }` |

Anything else under the prefix returns 404 `{ ok: false, error: 'not found' }`.

Writes are guarded: a non-`GET`/`HEAD` request is rejected with 403 `cross-site request rejected` unless it comes from no origin at all, from a `chrome-extension://` or `moz-extension://` origin, or from the same host. The favicon proxy is the one route that accepts an arbitrary URL, which is exactly why it is sandboxed and byte-sniffed rather than trusted.

---

## Interface language

Plugin-owned interface text follows the **host's language**, not a setting of its own.

- The client half injects the `locale` service, reads the active locale, and retranslates when it changes — live, without a reload.
- Two tables ship today: **zh** and **en**, 194 keys each, flat and dot-namespaced (`'button.title'`, `'settings.title'`, `'jump.composer.missing'`).
- Lookup order is **active language → en → the key itself**. `t()` can never return `undefined` and can never throw — a missing translation degrades to English, and a missing key degrades to a visible key name rather than a blank row.
- If the locale service is unreachable, the language falls back to `document.documentElement.lang`, then `navigator.language`, then `en`.
- The registry is extensible: `registerLanguage(id, table)` adds a table, and the plugin announces the languages it has to the host's locale service so they can appear in its language picker.
- The **extension** cannot use the host's locale service (it is a separate browser process), so it uses the browser's own `_locales` mechanism with `en` and `zh_CN`, and reads `api.i18n.getUILanguage()`.

---

## 🔗 Integration

### With `dsh-capability-composer` — a real, two-way link

This is the one integration that changes what you see, so it is worth being precise about it.

**What the launcher does.** It declares one linked plugin:

```
{ id: 'capability-composer', label: '能力组合器', path: '/dsh-capability-composer/state' }
```

At startup it probes that path and logs `connected` or `absent` per plugin. In the client half it then uses the composer's own endpoints:

| Uses | Endpoint | If the composer is missing |
|---|---|---|
| The plugin rows' narrowing scope | `/dsh-capability-composer/effective?sessionId=…` | Falls back to listing **all** plugins and shows why |
| The settings-jump buttons | `/dsh-capability-composer/state` | Buttons do not jump; a dismissible banner names the missing plugin |

**What happens when the composer is absent.** Nothing breaks. The Common plugins group lists every installed plugin instead of the narrowed set, and the two **Set composition**（「设置组合」）buttons refuse to jump — clicking one shows, for 15 seconds:

> dsh-capability-composer is not installed — install and enable it, then come back and hit Set composition.

**The probe is deliberately optimistic.** A rejected or non-2xx response means "not installed", but a network-level failure (the sandbox transport throwing) is treated as **reachable**. A false "not installed" would be worse than a false "installed": the first hides a working button, the second only means the jump lands on a settings page that is missing its tab.

**What the launcher does not do.** It does not compute the narrowing numbers. The "N / M plugins installed" counter is rendered here, but its two numbers come from the composer (`N`) and from this plugin's own plugin inventory (`M`). And the launcher never writes composer state.

### With the MCP panel — an entry point, not a dependency

The **MCP** row in the Capabilities group is fed by the host's `remote.mcpManager` service (in practice, provided by an MCP manager plugin). This plugin's host half contains **no MCP code at all**; it does not read, configure or restart MCP servers.

If that service is absent, the MCP row is simply unavailable, and clicking it returns a plain reason rather than failing silently. Which servers exist, whether they are enabled, and what tools they expose is entirely the MCP panel's business.

### With the rest of this family

`dsh-composer-launcher` has no code-level relationship with `dsh-context-reclaim` or `dsh-aux-degrade`. They solve different problems — those two work on what enters the context and what the auxiliary model calls spend; this one works on how you point the composer at things. Installing any of them alone is fine; the plugin inventory row for a missing sibling simply shows as not installed.

---

## Known limitations (stated plainly)

- **The enable/disable switch is not wired.** Plugin rows show state and link to settings; they do not toggle a plugin on or off.
- **Real tabs need the extension** (or the debug browser). There is no third path — a plugin cannot reach into a browser it is not running inside.
- **The bridge port is `43130` unless `DSH_LAUNCHER_BRIDGE_PORT` overrides it.** The extension's side is editable in its popup.
- **Chromium will not let this plugin install the extension into the browser you already use.** It can start its own browser with the extension attached, and it can point precisely at the manual steps; installing silently into an existing browser requires an enterprise policy and administrator rights, which this repository does not ship.
- **Firefox's MV3 support means a temporary load** in most builds; that is a browser constraint, not a plugin one.
- **The favicon proxy accepts arbitrary URLs.** It is sandboxed, byte-sniffed and size-limited, but it is still the one route worth understanding before you expose a machine.

---

## 9. The browser-extension notice: one dialog, naming the steps

The browser extension belongs to this plugin (the "+" launcher), so this dialog is this plugin's own. It appears once, the first time the interface opens after installation, and spells out:

- **Why it cannot install itself**: Chromium has a hard rule — nothing may silently sideload an extension into the browser you use every day. The plugin has already staged the files, but the one "Load unpacked" click has to be yours.
- **Three routes**: **A, zero clicks** — press "Open with the extension loaded" and the plugin starts a separate browser instance with the extension attached; **B, into your everyday browser** (one time only) — press "Open the extensions page" → Developer mode → Load unpacked → pick the folder the dialog prints; **C** follow `tutorial-browser-extension.md`.
- **Detection**: the extension pushes its tab list to the plugin; **a received push means "installed"** and the dialog stops appearing immediately. No push means "not installed". Nothing is guessed.
- **Always available**: the browser group has a "How to install" button that brings this same guide up on demand, even after the extension is installed.

**This plugin needs no DSH patches at all** — patches are announced by the plugins that need them, the extension by this one, and neither speaks for the other.

## 📚 Tutorials

| Document | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [Browser extension tutorial (English)](tutorial-browser-extension.md) | How to get the extension loaded: the zero-manual route A, the everyday-browser route B, the enterprise route C; how to verify it, what to do when it fails, and a prompt for your own agent |
| [浏览器扩展教程（中文）](tutorial-browser-extension.zh-CN.md) | the same, in Chinese |
| [Install & official patches (English)](tutorial-install-and-official-patches.md) | How to install all four plugins and what to do about the official patches the patches themselves ship as a library: <https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-patch-library>  |
| [安装与官方补丁（中文）](tutorial-install-and-official-patches.zh-CN.md) | the same, in Chinese 补丁本体已开源成补丁库：<https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-patch-library>  |

---

## 🔗 The rest of the family

Each plugin installs on its own; together they save the most. The other three:

- [`dsh-context-reclaim`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-context-reclaim) — Context reclamation: bounded tool results, a folded tool surface and a stable prefix
- [`dsh-aux-degrade`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-aux-degrade) — Auxiliary-call degradation: summaries and titles stop burning their budget on reasoning
- [`dsh-capability-composer`](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-capability-composer) — Capability composer: switchable tool/skill/MCP sets instead of one bloated surface

> All of them are **DSH 1.5 only**; newer DSH releases will be supported in follow-up updates. Plugins that need official patches announce them in the UI once you install them — nothing goes unseen.

## Installation

### From GitHub (recommended; measured on a fresh `DSH_HOME`)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:xiamubumu/dsh-composer-launcher
```

One command. That is the whole procedure — no script, no path to edit.

### From a local tarball (air-gapped machines)

Download `dsh-composer-launcher-1.1.0.tgz` from [Releases](https://github.com/xiamubumu/dsh-composer-launcher/releases), then:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-composer-launcher-1.1.0.tgz
```

### From the plugin marketplace / npm (not yet possible)

The marketplace submission (an `awesome-dsh-plugin` PR) has not been filed and nothing is published on npm yet ⇒ **neither route works today**.
Once listed/published, searching for **dsh-composer-launcher** in the marketplace and installing is all there is to it.

> ⚠️ **Known issue: do not feed the release asset's tarball URL to `dsh plugin add`.**
> `dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/.../releases/download/v1.1.0/....tgz` fails on the pnpm DSH bundles (10.34.5) with
> `ERR_PNPM_MISSING_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` ([pnpm#14351](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/14351), fixed upstream only in pnpm ≥ 12.5.1).
> Installing a second plugin that way **always** fails — use the `github:` shorthand or a local tarball path instead.

### From a local checkout

```bash
node install.mjs
```

or, on Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
```

`install.ps1` runs three steps and stops at the first failure:

1. **Backtick gate** (`strip-backticks.mjs`) — the client bundle must contain zero backticks before it is deployed. It runs first because it can rewrite the file: a bundle checked before a rewrite is not the bundle that ships.
2. **Deploy** (`install.mjs`) — copies the shipped files into a new generation, writes the generation's `generation.json` and `desired.json`, then calls the host's own `projectGenerations()` to make it live. It finishes by **importing the host half for real** and checking the profile manifest, so a bundle that cannot load is caught here rather than at your next boot.
3. **Verification** — the profile's `dependencies`, `dsh.profile.bundles` and the generation projection are read back and asserted.

The script finds Node itself: `PATH` first, then the runtime DSH Desktop ships. **You do not have to install Node.**

### Then restart DSH

The plugin's host half and its patch file are read at boot only. Restart DSH once after installing; the client half is then loaded with the app.

### The extension (optional)

Nothing to do for the zero-touch route: open the composer and press **Launch debug browser** (or *Open a browser with the extension loaded*) in the Tabs row. That starts a Chromium with the staged extension attached and verified — no manual load, no everyday browser involved.

For the browser you actually use, load it once:

```powershell
pwsh -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install-extension.ps1
```

It stages the extension to a stable path, lists the browsers it found on this machine, and opens the right extensions page. Add `-Browser edge` (or `chrome`, `brave`, `vivaldi`, `opera`, `arc`, `360`, `qq`, `firefox`) to skip the question. The Tabs row's *Open the extensions page* and *Copy the extension path* buttons do the first half of that without a terminal; the full walkthrough, including what Chromium does and does not allow, is in [The browser extension](#the-browser-extension).

---

## Compatibility

### Coexistence: does it fight other plugins? (measured 2026-10-15)

**Server-side seams — no conflict.**

Of the 44 plugins installed on the test machine, **21** also hook at least one of `llm/stream`, `tools/pre-execute`, `tools/post-execute`, `system-prompt/assemble`, `session/event` — and **20 of them are cooperative** (every handler calls `next()` to pass through). This plugin runs alongside all of them, including `dsh-vision-router`, which hooks four of the same seams.

The reason: DSH event seams are a **middleware waterfall**. As long as every party calls `next()` and only makes incremental edits, they **compose** instead of pre-empting each other.

**Client slots**:

| Slot | Kind | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `conversation.input.left` | `list` | its own seat |
| `conversation.input.dock` | `list` | stackable |
| `conversation.input.overlay` | `list` | stackable |
| `settings.plugin.item` | `keyed` | one cell per key |


> Only **`chain`** slots render just the first entry; `list` slots stack, and `keyed` slots give each key its own cell. **This plugin occupies no `chain` slot.**

**The three cases that do collide (honestly stated)**

1. The other plugin **rebuilds** the same seam wholesale (rewrites the whole system prompt / tool result) instead of editing incrementally;
2. The other plugin takes the **same `chain`** slot;
3. Both need a patch to the **same official file** — this one is reported as an explicit `conflict` by the patch library `apply.mjs --check`, never as a silent failure.

**Measured coexistence**: `dsh-context-reclaim` + `billion-context@0.1.175` share one profile with no conflict — the former rides the **Cordis event bus**, the latter rides an **agent bootstrap layer** (bootstrap-hook / native loader, shipping bundled payloads for six different agents). They share no seam.


| | |
|---|---|
| **DSH** | **1.5 series only** — `engines.dsh: ">=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0"` |
| **Desktop app** | ✅ supported |
| **Web UI** | ✅ supported |
| **Other DSH hosts** | ✅ if it is DSH, it is supported — nothing here is desktop-specific |
| **Operating system** | Windows, macOS, Linux |
| **Node** | ships with DSH; the syntax used here targets Node 20+ but you never install it yourself |
| **Third-party dependencies** | none — peer dependencies are DeepS
